attorneys.name: Jason F. Abraham
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Jason F. Abraham began his career with Hupy and Abraham as a personal injury lawyer in Milwaukee in 1993. He was promoted to shareholder in 1999. He received his Juris Doctor from Marquette University Law School in 1992. He is licensed to practice in Wisconsin, Iowa, and Missouri. Attorney Abraham is also actively involved in the legal community. He serves on the board of the Wisconsin Association for Justice and is a lifetime member of ABATE of Wisconsin and ABATE of Iowa.

Beyond his professional memberships, Attorney Abraham is well known for his community work and support for Milwaukee and the surrounding area. He serves on the steering committee for the Black-N-Blue Ball. He is a board member of Ridin’ to a Cure Foundation and serves on the board of Feeding America.

He has received widespread recognition for his results and client service. He holds an AV Preeminent rating from Martindale-Hubbell and a 10.0 superb rating from AVVO. He has been named to the Wisconsin Super Lawyers list since 2014. Since 2009, he has been recognized as one of the Top 100 Trial Lawyers: Civil Plaintiff by the National Trial Lawyers. He was named a Leader in the Law by the Wisconsin Law Journal and Lawyer of the Year by the NAACP Milwaukee.

Overall, Attorney Abraham has settled and fought for his clients, resulting in a combined value of approximately $400 million. This includes numerous recoveries exceeding $1 million. His expertise in personal injury matters has given him the opportunity to lecture in numerous states across the nation.

attorneys.name: Tara Adolph
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Green Bay, WI
attorneys.bio:
Born and raised in southwest Minnesota, attorney Tara Adolph received a Bachelor of Science in Justice Administration with a minor in Professional Communications from Southwest Minnesota State University in 2009. She was one of the youngest students accepted to Marquette University Law School at the age of 19. Attorney Adolph received her Juris Doctor degree upon graduation from Marquette in 2011. While attending Marquette, she completed more than 120 hours of pro bono service. Her judicial internship included working with Judge David Borowski of the Milwaukee County Circuit Court Felony Division and with the National Guard Staff Judge Advocate in Madison, Wisconsin. Attorney Tara Adolph also worked as a law clerk for two Milwaukee law firms and focused on both civil and criminal law. Adding to her law experience and knowledge, she is a certified Guardian ad Litem and an advocate for children in family and juvenile matters.

This Green Bay, Wisconsin attorney is a general law practitioner and practices in a broad range of legal areas, including family law, Guardian ad Litem work, CHIPS cases, traffic citations, litigation and criminal law. She's knowledgeable and passionate about protecting her client's rights and compassionate.

Family law includes a wide array of legal issues, such as prenups, divorce, child custody, visitation and support. Attorney Tara Adolph encourages her clients to participate in non-adversarial options for family issues, including mediation. As an alternative to a court hearing, these processes are quicker, less expensive and tend to help all parties keep good relationships. Neutral third parties are assigned to help couples address issues and come to an agreed resolution. During these processes, attorney Tara Adolph can act as your legal advisor and review agreements before you sign. At the same time, she's a strong litigator should an agreement not be reached, and a court trial is the only solution.

Being charged with a crime is a serious matter. While misdemeanors are minor offenses, felonies are taken seriously by the court and may result in high fines, long prison sentence and the loss of employment. Tara Adolph does a thorough investigation to ensure probable cause existed, takes depositions from witnesses, uses experts for your defense and develops a strong defense strategy.

If a plea is offered from the prosecution, attorney Tara Adolph will advise you whether it's in your best interest to accept it. She'll be totally honest with you about the evidence and help you make the best decision.

From family law to criminal law and municipal law to traffic law, turn to attorney Tara Adolph for legal advice with a personal touch. Your future is just as important to her as it is to you.

attorneys.name: Steven R. Alpert (1948
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury -- Plaintiff Lawyers in Manitowoc, WI
attorneys.bio:
Steven R. Alpert was the founding partner of the firm, starting his practice in 1976 after receiving his undergraduate degree from the University of Wisconsin, graduating cum laude, and obtaining his law degree from Marquette University Law School. He served as the first municipal judge in Manitowoc and was a past president of the Manitowoc County Bar Association. Attorney Alpert was the incorporator of the first Indochinese MAA in Wisconsin (1978), and had the first successful prosecution of an Open Meeting Law Complaint in Wisconsin. He also settled one of the first reported TMJ cases in Wisconsin.

In addition to his distinguished career as an attorney, Steve devoted his adult life to serving the Manitowoc community. He was a supervisor on the Manitowoc County Board and a member of the Manitowoc Planning Commission. He was also a past president of the Rotary Club and served on the Board of Directors for numerous community organizations, including the Manitowoc County Ice Center, Aquatic Center, Public Library and the Haven Homeless Shelter. Steve will always be remembered for his kindness, wry sense of humor and unwavering support for his family.

attorneys.name: David K. Anderson
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney David K. Anderson is the managing partner at Chirafisi Anderson, S.C., where he focuses exclusively on criminal defense and OWI representation. Since beginning his legal career in 2015, he has represented individuals facing misdemeanor and felony charges in courts throughout southern and central Wisconsin.

Attorney Anderson approaches criminal defense with an emphasis on preparation, analysis, and accountability. He understands that criminal charges often arise from complex circumstances, and he works to ensure that each case is evaluated on its specific facts rather than assumptions or routine charging practices. His work includes close review of the evidence, identification of legal and constitutional issues, and early assessment of how a case is likely to proceed in the specific court involved.

As managing partner, Attorney Anderson remains directly involved in client representation. He prioritizes clear communication and informed decision-making, advising clients candidly about the law, the process, and their available options while remaining prepared to litigate when doing so is in the client’s best interest.

Attorney David K. Anderson focuses his practice exclusively on criminal defense and OWI matters. He represents individuals charged with misdemeanors and felonies, as well as clients facing Operating While Intoxicated (OWI) and related impaired driving offenses in Wisconsin state and federal courts.

A significant portion of Attorney Anderson’s work involves OWI defense, including cases that require careful evaluation of traffic stops, field sobriety testing, chemical testing procedures, and the scientific and evidentiary issues that commonly arise in impaired driving prosecutions. His approach reflects an understanding that OWI cases often turn on technical details and procedural compliance, in addition to the underlying facts.

In addition to OWI matters, Attorney Anderson handles a broad range of criminal cases from investigation and charging through motion practice, hearings, and trial. His practice emphasizes individualized strategy based on the evidence, the applicable law, and the practices of the specific court involved.

Attorney David K. Anderson began his legal career in 2015 after earning his Juris Doctor, with a certificate in litigation, from Marquette University Law School. During law school, he served in the trial division of the Milwaukee County Public Defender’s Office, where he gained early courtroom experience working on criminal cases and representing clients facing serious charges.

That experience provided a foundation in trial preparation, evidentiary analysis, and courtroom advocacy. Since entering private practice, Attorney Anderson has built his background handling criminal cases at all stages of the process, including motion practice, evidentiary hearings, and trial-level litigation in courts throughout southern and central Wisconsin. His experience reflects familiarity with the procedural differences and local practices that can significantly affect how cases are resolved.

In addition to his work in Wisconsin circuit courts, Attorney Anderson is admitted to practice before the United States District Court for the Western District of Wisconsin. His background includes experience navigating both state and federal court systems and the distinct procedural requirements of each.

Attorney David K. Anderson has been recognized by peers for his work in criminal defense and OWI matters.

He has been selected as a Super Lawyers – Rising Stars honoree for eight consecutive years (2018–2025). This distinction is awarded to a limited number of attorneys based on peer evaluation and professional achievement.

Attorney Anderson is an active member of professional organizations focused on criminal defense and impaired driving litigation, including the National College for DUI Defense, the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, and the Wisconsin Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers.

Timothy B. Anderson ("Tim"), a long-time Shareholder with Remley Law, S.C., emphasizes a business-related legal practice, involving business transactions, litigation, collection, employment, real estate, and estate planning matters for individuals, start-ups, nonprofits and long-established businesses. Early on in his career, Tim was selected as one of the Fox Valley's top "Thirty under Thirty" in the September 10, 2001 edition of the Post Crescent, saluting up-and-coming business leaders. Tim has also been rated as a Premium Pick in a survey of lawyers conducted by Fox Cities Magazine. To this day, Tim continues to have a strong presence and reputation in the Fox Valley legal community and surrounding counties. As for his education, Tim earned his J.D. degree from Marquette Law School and earned his B.A. degree in Political Science and English from Marquette, where he studied under former Wisconsin Congressman Scott L. Klug and former U.S. Secretary of Defense Les Aspin. As for his interests outside the law, Tim is passionate about his time afield, hunting and fishing with friends and family whenever he can. He and his wife Emily live in Neenah and assist numerous charitable organizations, with an emphasis on animal rescue/welfare, in the Fox Valley area.

attorneys.name: Dino Antonopoulos
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Law Lawyers in Elm Grove, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Dino Antonopoulos is the founder of Antonopoulos Legal Group (“ALG”). From the beginning of his legal career, Dino formed meaningful relationships and friendships with clients. It’s those relationships and the bond he has with his clients that motivated Dino to start ALG. Dino wanted to create a firm culture focused on these types of relationships between attorneys and clients. Honesty, hard work, loyalty, and a commitment to fight for clients are the main principles Dino built the firm on. His mom taught him the value of these principles as a kid working in their family restaurant business. To appreciate how a business operates and how important every individual is to the success of a business, Dino worked in all facets of the restaurant operations including cleaning tables, washing dishes, scrubbing floors, and serving customers. Dino eventually managed multiple restaurants as a high schooler and into college.

Almost 20 years into his legal profession, Dino has developed a reputation for excellent communication, client advocacy, and favorable results. Dino is fortunate that he had the opportunity to gain invaluable courtroom experience early in his legal career representing closely held businesses and financial institutions in complex commercial litigation, including litigating seven figure jury trials. The courtroom experience along with the types of clients Dino represents naturally gravitated Dino into the transactional world.

Dino took the experience of identifying as well as attacking issues in complex commercial litigation and applying those lessons to business, real estate, and financing transactions such as the preparation of governing documents for companies and asset purchase agreements relating to acquiring companies. Dino represents financial institutions and various closely held companies including manufacturers, distributors, retailers, developers, builders, contractors, real estate brokerage firms, and service providers. The key to the selection of clients is identifying clients who share the same principles and values of ALG.

As outside general counsel to closely held companies, Dino takes on an in-depth advisory and consulting role focusing on complex issues and developing strategic as well as practical solutions.Dino and his wife, Stephanie, live in Brookfield, Wisconsin with their four children – Ellie, Mikey, and twins Emma and Andrew. Dino and Stephanie run in circles most days with their kids’ schedules. Dino coaches his kids in various team sports. Dino applies the same principles in his professional life to the coaching world.

Dino received his Bachelor’s Degree from the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee in 2002 and his Juris Doctorate from Marquette University in 2005.

Dino took the experience of identifying as well as attacking issues in complex commercial litigation and applying those lessons to business, real estate, and financing transactions such as the preparation of governing documents for companies and asset purchase agreements relating to acquiring companies. Dino represents financial institutions and various closely held companies including manufacturers, distributors, retailers, developers, builders, contractors, real estate brokerage firms, and service providers. The key to the selection of clients is identifying clients who share the same principles and values of ALG.

As outside general counsel to closely held companies, Dino takes on an in-depth advisory and consulting role focusing on complex issues and developing strategic as well as practical solutions.Dino and his wife, Stephanie, live in Brookfield, Wisconsin with their four children – Ellie, Mikey, and twins Emma and Andrew. Dino and Stephanie run in circles most days with their kids’ schedules. Dino coaches his kids in various team sports. Dino applies the same principles in his professional life to the coaching world.

Dino received his Bachelor’s Degree from the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee in 2002 and his Juris Doctorate from Marquette University in 2005.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Litigation Lawyers in Oshkosh, WI
attorneys.bio:
“Jenna you never back down, and always have to have the last word – you should be an attorney.”

Sixteen years ago, when Jenna’s mother uttered those few words, she had no idea that it would end up being the pivotal moment in her strong-willed daughter’s life. In the 8th grade, Jenna fell in love with the concept of helping people using her tenacity and confidence in the legal world. Prior to Law school, Jenna had the unique opportunity to work as a receptionist for Attorney Greg Wright. She found herself surrounded by incredible work ethic, a team atmosphere, and genuine concern for client care. It was then that her plan to pursue a legal career with a focus on Personal Injury Litigation was solidified.

After completing law school, Jenna again joined the Greg Wright Law team as a licensed attorney. Her passion has only intensified, as she works tirelessly to negotiate consistently brilliant results for her clients. Jenna is currently mainly working in Personal Injury Litigation. Her sincere dedication to every client is evident in the detail-oriented, individualized service she provides. It is Jenna’s unusual ability to communicate and bridge the gap between what has been done, and what others say can’t be accomplished that makes her stand out above the rest when it comes to her leadership and abilities. Jenna has proven instrumental in this company’s success with her commitment to taking on challenging cases and being a true advocate for each client she serves.

Jenna graduated from Northern Illinois University College of Law, Magna Cum Laude in May 2013. Jenna is licensed in two states: Illinois and Wisconsin. She passed her Illinois Bar Exam in fall 2013 and has been submitted to practice law in Illinois by the State Bar of Illinois. In spring 2014, Jenna was submitted to the State Bar of Wisconsin to practice law in this state after passing the Wisconsin Bar Exam.

attorneys.bio:
Attorney Valerie J. Asimacopoulos is an associate attorney with a passion for family law. Attorney Asimacopoulos is committed to helping her clients navigate and understand each step of the court process. She understands that the court process can be intimidating, which is why she ensures open and honest communication with her clients.

Attorney Asimacopoulos attended Marquette University where she graduated magna cum laude with an Honors Bachelor of Arts degree in Economics and Political Science. She also attended Villanova University Charles Widger School of Law where she received her Juris Doctorate degree. While in law school, Attorney Asimacopoulos competed on Villanova Law's National Trial Team and was a quarterfinalist in Villanova's 60th Annual Reimel Moot Court Competition.

Attorney Asimacopoulos tirelessly advocates for her clients while keeping their expectations realistic. She is empathetic, analytical, and thorough. While Attorney Asimacopoulos strives to find an advantageous middle-ground between all parties, when all else fails, her strong litigation skills assist her clients in receiving a favorable resolution to their issues.

She represents clients in family law related matters including divorce, post-judgment disputes, maintenance modifications and enforcement, spousal support, paternity actions, child custody and placement actions, placement enforcement, child support, child support modifications and enforcement, child removal, child abuse, contempt orders, harassment, domestic violence, and restraining orders.

Attorney Asimacopoulos is licensed to practice law in the State of Wisconsin.

attorneys.name: Elisabeth S. Bach
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Elisabeth S. Bach-Van Horn is a Partner with the firm's Family Law Practice Group. She joined the firm in 2011.

Prior to joining the firm, for three years Liz was a staff attorney with Legal Aid of Western Missouri, representing victims and survivors of domestic abuse in divorce, paternity, and child custody matters.

In addition to representing clients in a variety of family law matters, Liz has particular training and experience in representing children’s best interests as a Guardian ad Litem, and in representing clients in collaborative divorce, a process that is designed to address all of the traditional family law issues in a manner which is conducive to positive results for the whole family. Liz is serving as the 2021 Chair of the Collaborative Family Law Council of Wisconsin, Inc. (CFLCW), whose Mission Statement is “an association of professionals working together to teach, learn, practice, and promote family centered processes, using interdisciplinary teams, to respectfully resolve family law concerns including separation and divorce.”

attorneys.name: Kristi R. Baker
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Long before law school, Kristi advocated for children and families both in the court system and in the community. She advocated for abused and neglected children as a volunteer and as a foster parent. Her work as a volunteer coordinator for homeless families with children gave her insight into the challenges faced by families in Dane County in finding basic resources and gave her a profound respect for parents working to meet their children’s needs in the midst of chaos. She seeks to be a fair, compassionate, and zealous voice for her clients.

PRACTICE AREAS

School Law (including IEPs and expulsion)

Divorce and Dissolution

Child Custody, Placement, and Support

Paternity

Guardian ad litem Appointments

CHIPS

Guardianship

Foster Parent Rights

Grandparent Rights

Adoption

Appeals

LGBTQ Family Law

Transgender Law

EDUCATION

Kristi earned her law degree cum laude in 2014 from Hamline University School of Law in St. Paul, Minnesota. During law school, Kristi was the Student Director of the Hamline Child Advocacy Clinic, serving as a student attorney in St. Paul and Minneapolis on a variety of child-related cases. Kristi graduated from the University of Wisconsin-Madison with a B.A. in English in 1992.

COMMUNITY AND PROFESSIONAL ACTIVITIES

Kristi serves on the Board of the Children and the Law Section of the State Bar, an elected position. She also served on the Board of the Wisconsin CASA (Court Appointed Special Advocates) from 2014 to 2018. Prior to and during law school, Kristi volunteered with CASA of Rock County, advocating for eight children over five years and now appreciates working with the Wisconsin CASA in supporting programs throughout the state. She is a member of the Dane County Bar Association and a former member of the DCBA Law for the Public Committee.

In 2016, Kristi was accepted into Wisconsin Pro Bono Honor Society. In order to be accepted into the Honor Society, she had to provide at least 50 hours of qualifying pro bono (free) legal services to benefit people of limited means.

PERSONAL

Kristi and her husband are proud of their two adult sons and their former foster son who remains part of their lives. She enjoys hiking and exploring state and national parks and has especially loved traveling out west to Colorado, Wyoming, and South Dakota. On the weekends and evenings, she loves curling up with a good book and her two dogs, Bernie and Gracie.

attorneys.name: Melissa Louise Barrette
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Sheboygan, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Melissa Barrette has a reputation for aggressively representing her client and not hesitating to take cases to trial. Her record includes both pre-trial dismissals and winning acquittals by jury in both felony and misdemeanor cases involving charges of drunk driving, child abuse and sexual assault. She understands that her role includes being both a compassionate advisor to her clients and a legal champion in court.

In 2019, she partnered with long-time colleague Attorney Brett Kaehne to continue a life dedicated to defending those accused of crimes. Prior to forming Kaehne and Barrette S.C., Attorney Barrette practiced criminal defense in Sheboygan for six years. Attorney Barrette is a member of the Sheboygan County bar association, the Wisconsin Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers (WACDL), the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers (NACDL), and the National College of DUI Defense (NCDD). She is also a member of the NORML legal committee.

Attorney Barrette attended the University of Wisconsin. As an undergraduate, she triple-majored in Legal Studies, Political Science and Sociology and served as the President of the University’s Legal Studies Association. After graduation, she immediately enrolled in the University of Wisconsin Law School. While there, she gained acceptance into the prestigious Wisconsin Innocence Project, reviewing claims of actual innocence and evaluating where other attorney’s failed their clients. Attorney Barrette also worked at the Madison Department of Civil Rights, where she fought to preserve social justice.

attorneys.bio:
Alex Becker's practice focuses on collections, commercial litigation, and municipal law.

Alex assists businesses with collections of delinquent accounts from other businesses and consumers, taking effort to help avoid lawsuits and litigation whenever possible. Alex works with the firm's creditors’ rights team to draft documents including Promissory Notes, Settlement Agreements, Forbearance Agreements, litigation-related pleadings, and more. Based in Murphy Desmond's Madison office, Alex can assist clients throughout Wisconsin.

attorneys.name: Emily Bell
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Emily Bell is an associate attorney at Nicholson Goetz & Otis, S.C. While she handles all types of criminal charges, she specializes in defending individuals charged with Operating While Intoxicated (OWI) and related offenses.

Attorney Bell has substantial experience with Wisconsin drunk driving defense and engages in complex OWI litigation, including challenging the validity of traffic stops, searches, and warrants, challenging prior convictions, handling allegations that her clients refused to submit to chemical testing, and litigating administrative matters of driver’s license suspension and revocation. She also has significant knowledge of Wisconsin’s blood and breath testing practices and has advanced training in the administration of roadside sobriety tests.

She dedicates a substantial portion of her practice to mounting a successful defense of individuals accused of serious crimes across the state of Wisconsin, including homicide, weapons charges, domestic violence, disorderly conduct, reckless endangerment of safety, and fraud.

Attorney Bell is a fierce advocate for her clients and is prepared to fight for them in every possible scenario. She has tried dozens of case in front of Wisconsin juries in addition to resolving countless cases via bench trials and pretrial litigation.

As a passionate advocate for criminal justice, she frequently presents at Wisconsin seminars and trainings, including the Wisconsin Public Defender Annual Conference, the Wisconsin State Bar’s Build Your Practice series, the Wisconsin Association for Justice’s summer and winter seminars, and trainings sponsored by The Legal Aid Society of Milwaukee. Based on her expertise, she was asked to be on the faculty of a multi-day workshop where she trained public defenders on how to handle a drunk driving defense cases from start to finish.

Attorney Bell is a Midwesterner through and through. She grew up in Michigan and graduated from Grand Valley State University in 2005 with degrees in philosophy and liberal studies. She moved on to Wisconsin to earn her juris doctorate from Marquette University Law School in 2009. In addition to her legal practice, she is a member of the Wisconsin Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers and the State Bar of Wisconsin’s Civil Rights & Liberties section. When she is not fighting for the rights of others, she enjoys long distance running and attempting to recreate desserts she sees on baking shows.

Awards and Honors

Honors

WACDL Martin Hanson Memorial Prize Award Winner, 2024

attorneys.name: Robert E. Bellin Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury - Plaintiff Lawyers in Neenah, WI
attorneys.bio:
My law practice concentrates on personal injury, and mainly car, truck and motorcycle crashes. I will help victims navigate the pitfalls of dealing with their own insurance, another driver's insurance, payment of medical bills, lost wages, and property damage. Injuries can become a life changing event, and we handle the legal and insurance issues so the victim can concentrate on healing and getting back to normal life. And, I DO NOT represent insurance companies.

I handle cases all over Wisconsin, but concentrate in the Fox Valley. I regularly represent clients from Appleton, Neenah, Menasha, Oshkosh, Green Bay, Waupaca, Shawano, DePere, Wrightstown, Greenleaf, Hortonville, Greenville, Kaukauna, Chilton, Freedom, Kimberly, Manitowoc, Oconto and more. I also have 25 years of experience in courts all over the state, including Outagamie County, Winnebago County, Brown County, Waupaca County, Shawano County, Calumet County, Door County, Marinette County, Waushara County, Portage County, Marathon County, Kewaunee County, Dane County, Dodge County, Milwaukee County, Waukesha County, Oconto County and many more.

Call or email me for answers to your questions about personal injury, car accident, truck accident, motorcycle accident, wrongful death, slip, trip and fall, dog bite, civil litigation and business litigation. Here is another link to an article where I represented the victims of fraud in Outagamie and Waupaca County https://madison.com/news/local/olympian-s-parents-victims-of-extortion/article_3afd7686-38f1-5ec0-8bc9-730efdfce6d2.html. I have handled numerous high profile cases, and recovered compensation for clients in both state and federal courts, but all cases are important to those involved, and I will talk to you even if you do not end up needing an attorney. I have handled cases ranging from whiplash to multi-million dollar wrongful death, and many large settlements which remain confidential. You can see my reviews on our homepage and more here:

I have also published helpful videos: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UClSOJuNlphBNVr_QDHkpXWg

attorneys.name: Stephanie Benske
attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices of Benske, Gatzke, McFadden and Rose
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in New Berlin, WI
attorneys.bio:
Stephanie Benske is an attorney at the firm Benske, Gatzke, McFadden and Rose, LLC., located in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. She focuses her practice on family law matters.

Ms. Benske attended Omaha Marian High School, a private institution in her hometown of Omaha, Nebraska. She was accepted to and enrolled at Creighton University, also located in Omaha, after she graduated from Omaha Marian. During her time in Nebraska, she acquired significant professional experience through her involvement in the State Legislature and active participation in political campaigns. She actively participated in the sorority Chi Omega, fostering enduring interpersonal relationships and assuming the role of secretary for a duration of two years.

In 1998, Ms. Benske successfully completed her Juris Doctor degree at Creighton Law School. She was granted the opportunity to serve as a visiting scholar at Marquette Law School during her third year of legal education. In addition, she acquired significant professional experience through her internship under the guidance of the Honorable Daniel Noonan at the Children's Court Center located in Milwaukee County, Wisconsin.

Ms. Benske has curated educational resources and delivered instructional sessions on adoption and family law matters to legal professionals, facilitated by the National Business Institute. She has made an appearance on the television program Dateline alongside her colleague Paulette Brazil to discuss a case pertaining to familial matters. She has held memberships in several esteemed organizations, including the Inns of Court, Society of Family Law, Justinian Society, and the Wisconsin Club. Furthermore, she has leveraged her expertise in political campaigning to provide support for judicial campaigns. She has volunteered her time at the Volunteer Self Help Legal Clinic, a program provided at the Milwaukee County Courthouse.

Ms. Benske successfully completed the Mediation program at the University of Wisconsin – Milwaukee. She offers professional mediation services aimed at resolving familial matters. She possesses considerable expertise in the field of adoption law. She possesses extensive experience in managing a considerable number of adoption cases. Additionally, she brings a distinctive perspective to her practice, as she has personally undergone the process of adopting children, both internationally and domestically.

Ms. Benske is employed at the Children's Court Center, where she is involved in the management of Child in Need of Protection or Services (CHIPS) cases. Her responsibilities encompass both private cases and serving as an intake attorney at the Center. Additionally, she has immense experience with guardianships.

attorneys.practice_type: Business Law and Litigation Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
For over 25 years, Amy has provided practical legal advice clients can use to make sound business decisions, helping business owners avoid costly legal issues so they can devote their time and resources to developing their business. When problems arise, she represents businesses in court and arbitration, applying years of litigation experience to helping achieve results.

Typical clients are mid-sized businesses and financial institutions. Clients include finance companies, online merchants and service providers, automobile dealers, manufacturers, technology companies, and businesses involved in various commercial activities.

Business owners appreciate Amy’s approach: “I felt comfortable and more at ease that Amy handled everything. I could sleep at night because it was in her hands. I set standards very high and Amy met them; it was a wonderful experience.” (Carla S., business owner; business transactions client.) “She changed my whole opinion of working with a lawyer; she’s very comfortable. If anyone is looking for a lawyer to work with, it is a no-brainer for me to recommend Amy.” (Matt K., business owner; business transactions client.) Clients in litigation, compliance, and contract law have also referred to Amy as “thorough in her analysis,” “ready to lend a hand at the drop of a hat,” described her “response rate as incredible,” and stated “Amy cuts to the chase and asks the right questions; she makes the right recommendations.”

Philosophy behind our business law advice

You know best how to run your business. Our role is to help protect it from legal liability. With an appropriate business structure, sound contracts, and solid compliance advice, Bentley Tuffnell Law’s clients can sleep at night knowing we are watching for legal issues while they run their businesses.

attorneys.name: Chuck Berendes
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Lawyers in La Crosse, WI
attorneys.bio:
Chuck is a La Crosse native and an Aquinas graduate. Chuck did his undergraduate studies at St. John's University in Collegeville, MN where he served two years on the Student Senate, spent a semester in China and delivered the commencement address at the graduation ceremony. Upon graduation Chuck moved to San Diego for an adventure. While in California Chuck worked as a foreman on the construction of a large apartment building and led five men who had been released from San Quentin prison just days before starting work on the construction site. It was this experience that motivated Chuck to attend law school. He moved back to the Midwest and attended the University of St. Thomas School of Law. While at St. Thomas Chuck was involved in a number of volunteer opportunities including founding an after school study program at a local elementary school and recruiting other law students to serve as tutors. Chuck also served as the Student Body President in his third year of law school. During law school Chuck married his wife Polly, also a La Crosse native and their first child was born at the beginning of his last semester at St. Thomas. After law school Chuck and his family returned to La Crosse and Chuck took a position as an immigration attorney at Catholic Charities. Chuck worked at Catholic Charities for 9 years and built an immigration practice that served immigrants from all over the western side of Wisconsin. For half of his time at Catholic Charities Chuck also served as the Assistant Executive Director of the agency overseeing the creation of the Warming Center in La Crosse and another in Wausau and a full time homeless shelter in Eau Claire and varied programs from adoption, to services for children on the autism spectrum. During his time at Catholic Charities Chuck and Polly had two more children and Chuck earned a Masters in Business Administration from Viterbo University. Before joining Pittman & Pittman Chuck served as the General Manager of a local real estate company and learned much about the real estate industry.

As an experienced immigration attorney at Pittman & Pittman, Chuck has helped numerous individuals and families navigate the complex immigration system. He specializes in fiancé visas, marriage-based Green Cards, Naturalization and cases involving parole in place. Chuck understands the importance of keeping families together and has successfully represented many US citizen wives whose undocumented husbands were at risk of deportation. With compassion and expertise, he guides his clients through the legal process, ensuring that US citizen spouses and their loved ones have the best possible chance at obtaining legal status and building a life in America.

Chuck and Polly live in La Crosse with their three children. Chuck is active in numerous community organizations including his parish, and serves on the board of the MidWest Music Fest, Beer By Bike Brigade, La Crosse SOUP, and was the board president Shelter Development and spent years in leadership with the Cub Scouts when his sons were young. Chuck enjoys spending time with his family on road trips or watching sporting events around the Midwest.

attorneys.name: Marcus J. Berghahn
attorneys.practice_type: White Collar Criminal Defense Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Marcus Berghahn defends individuals and businesses accused of criminal misconduct. His practice encompasses all types of criminal cases at all stages of criminal proceedings-investigation, pre-charging negotiation, practice before a Grand Jury or a John Doe magistrate, motion hearings, jury trial, sentencing-on through to appeal. Because of the depth of his experience, Marcus also counsels witnesses and victims when they are involved in criminal proceedings. Marcus takes pride in helping clients through a very difficult time in their lives and delivers on what he believes are three core client needs: "Helping clients understand exactly what will happen at each stage of their case and what that means for them; having compassion for the stress and anxiety attendant to criminal cases; and listening to a client's concerns and priorities in order to deliver the best advice possible, leading to the best result possible."

Marcus lectures regularly on topics of criminal law at continuing legal education seminars. He is an adjunct professor at the University of Wisconsin Law School where he teaches a seminar on constitutional and criminal law. Marcus is a double Badger, completing both undergraduate and law school at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

attorneys.name: Janel Bergsbaken
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Elkhorn, WI
attorneys.bio:
With over a decade of time dedicated to her legal practice, Janel has established herself as a skilled advocate in Wisconsin’s civil litigation field. As an associate at Godfrey, Leibsle, Blackborn & Howarth, S.C. since 2015 and a partner since 2021, she has built a comprehensive trial practice, concentrating in complex business disputes, construction law, land use matters, and personal injury cases.

Throughout her career, Janel has earned recognition from clients and colleagues alike for her exceptional legal writing—characterized as concise, polished, and strategically aggressive. Her ability to deconstruct complex legal issues into compelling arguments has proven instrumental in achieving favorable outcomes for her clients. This reputation was cultivated during her law school tenure, where she served as Editor-in-Chief of the Wisconsin Law Review, developing the research, writing, and citation expertise that continues to set her work apart. Her meticulous attention to detail and talent for crafting persuasive arguments have become hallmarks of her practice, whether she is drafting motions for summary judgment in complex commercial disputes or preparing briefs to compel discovery of electronic records in personal injury litigation. She is particularly skilled at creating detailed chronological timelines of events that help mediators, arbitrators, judges, and juries understand the facts and sequence of events in complex cases.

Janel’s recent successes demonstrate her ability to secure exceptional results for her clients across diverse litigation matters. In a complex construction dispute, she successfully advocated for a homeowner client, ultimately securing an offer from the contractor to buy back the home—a rare and significant outcome that provided her client with the potential for complete resolution to their construction nightmare. Janel has also received favorable outcomes for individuals who suffered personal injuries due to motor vehicle accidents caused by drivers using electronic devices and homeowners victimized by dishonest contractors who engaged in theft and violated Wisconsin's Home Improvement Practices Act. Additionally, Janel recently achieved a significant victory through a successful Daubert motion, which resulted in an order prohibiting an opposing party’s construction expert from testifying at the time of trial—a strategic win that substantially strengthened her client’s position.

Janel is licensed to practice in Wisconsin and the Eastern District of Wisconsin. She is a Double Badger, having earned both her undergraduate degree and J.D. from the University of Wisconsin. Outside of her legal practice, Janel enjoys attending local farmers markets, touring regional wineries, discovering local coffee shops, and, more recently, following professional golf.

attorneys.bio:
Attorney Patrick M. Bertrandt graduated with honors from the University of Wisconsin Oshkosh (B.S. 1999) (magna cum laude) and was the recipient of the Socratic Award granted by the University of Oshkosh Philosophy Department. Attorney Bertrandt then received his law degree at the University of San Diego School of Law (J.D. 2002). While in California, Attorney Bertrandt worked at the San Diego Superior Court as a mediator resolving disputes between small claims litigants.

In 2002, Attorney Bertrandt took the Wisconsin Bar Examination and was admitted to practice law in this state. He began his practice as a general practitioner representing clients in criminal, family, and real estate matters. In addition, Attorney Bertrandt has also consulted on implementing a successful dispute resolution mechanism for Ford Motors Corporation.

In 2006 he was elected chairperson for the Wisconsin Young Lawyers Division and represents the interests of lawyers and the community both in Wisconsin and throughout the country. He presently focuses his practice on representing the interests of victims injured in accidents.

Attorney Bertrandt is a member of the American Association for Justice, the American Bar Association and Wisconsin Bar Associations. He has also been admitted to practice law in the United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit, United States Eastern and Western District Courts of the State of Wisconsin and all other courts in the State of Wisconsin.

attorneys.name: John A. Birdsall
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Having taken 290-plus cases to trial, Mr. Birdsall has attended to a wide range of violations, from minor traffic offenses to charges that may result in lengthy incarceration and hefty fines, if found guilty. They include murder, assault, homicide, driving under the influence (DUI), traffic offenses, sex crimes, violent crimes, juvenile offenses, fraud, theft and more.

After graduating with his Bachelor of Arts from the University of Wisconsin–Madison, Mr. Birdsall earned a doctorate in law from the University of Wisconsin Law School in 1989. The same year, he was authorized to practice law in Wisconsin and later in New York (2017).

One of Mr. Birdsall’s noteworthy cases includes a first-degree reckless homicide case, where he was able to secure a not-guilty verdict by cross-questioning the state's witnesses and employing a DNA specialist. Additionally, in 2009, the Wisconsin Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers awarded him the Martin Hanson Advocate's Prize, a prestigious honor bestowed upon attorneys who have accomplished the rare and impressive feat of winning a criminal homicide case. He has also had other homicide cases dismissed without trial after lengthy legal battles including a case involving a false confession and a case where he proved through DNA that a different person committed the crime.

Mr. Birdsall comprehends the anguish, fear and pressures his criminally accused clients face, and he utilizes all legal options available to obtain a favorable outcome. He believes that every citizen has the right to a fair and impartial trial, regardless of the accusation they may be facing. For his high ethical standards, professionalism and accomplishments, he is rated AV Preeminent* through Martindale-Hubbell and 10 out of 10 on Avvo.

Involved in his legal community, Mr. Birdsall has held several leadership positions in the Wisconsin Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, the State Bar of Wisconsin and the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers. He is also a part of the Rotary Club of Milwaukee, the Milwaukee Rescue Mission and the YMCA of Metropolitan Milwaukee – to name a few. He also spearheaded efforts over 15 years to raise the rates paid to counsel appointed to represent poor people and is co-counsel for a class action against the Wisconsin State Public Defenders Office for their failure to find attorneys for the poor allowing them to languish for months in jail without an attorney.*AV®, AV Preeminent®, Martindale-Hubbell Distinguished and Martindale-Hubbell Notable are certification marks used under license in accordance with the Martindale-Hubbell certification procedures, standards and policies. Martindale-Hubbell® is the facilitator of a peer-review rating process. Ratings reflect the anonymous opinions of members of the bar and the judiciary. Martindale-Hubbell® Peer Review Rating™ falls into two categories – legal ability and general ethical standards.

attorneys.name: David J. Bischmann
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
For Dave, it is all about helping people. That is the reason he went to law school, and the reason he became interested in personal injury law, where he fights for people who have had their life turned upside down through no fault of their own. For over 25 years, Dave has dedicated his practice to representing people injured by careless drivers, unsafe premises, and people wrongly denied insurance coverage by Fortune 500 companies who all too often favor profits over paying what they owe. Dave is committed to ensuring a fair and effective justice system for anyone who has been injured by the misconduct or negligence of others, which is why he is a proud member of the National Crime Victim Bar Association, American Association for Justice and the Wisconsin Association for Justice.

Throughout his career Dave has been part of a collaborative team of attorneys, representing tens of thousands of injured people throughout Wisconsin and the Midwest, fighting to obtain maximum recovery for their clients, in cases both big and small. For example, he was instrumental in establishing creative theories of liability and insurance coverage to help obtain a $2 million settlement for a woman who was paralyzed when a UTV rolled over in a farm field, over $3.2 million for a man severely burned in an apartment fire caused by an arsonist, and $2.5 million for three siblings whose parents were tragically killed by a drunk driver in Wisconsin. However, rest assured that Dave is just as passionate providing VIP service and results to those who have suffered less serious injuries and damages, helping to ensure that every client recovers what they are entitled to under the law.

attorneys.name: Lisle W. Blackbourn
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury and Land Use litigation Lawyers in Elkhorn, WI
attorneys.bio:
Lisle W. Blackbourn is the President and Managing Partner of Godfrey, Leibsle, Blackbourn & Howarth, S.C., and chairs the firm's litigation division. Lisle earned his law degree from Marquette University Law School in 1982, where he was a member of the Marquette Law Review.

Lisle has received board certification from the National Board of Trial Advocacy (NBTA) as a Civil Trial Specialist. NBTA is accredited by the American Bar Association to provide board certification through a rigorous application process and an exacting set of standards and examinations on a nationwide scale. Board certified trial attorneys engage in litigation of civil controversies before state and federal courts.

To become board certified, Lisle was required to pass the NBTA written examination, which covers trial law, civil procedure, evidence, and ethics. The exam is written and graded by attorneys and law professors. The NBTA also requested submission of confidential performance reviews from judges before whom Blackbourn had appeared, and from attorneys with whom he had worked. NBTA reviewed samples of legal briefs Blackbourn had written for scholarly content. Blackbourn was further required to submit proof of participation in at least 100 jury trials and other contested matters as lead counsel, to demonstrate a concentration of his practice in trial law.

The NBTA board certification process is designed to identify lawyers who possess an enhanced level of skill and expertise in trial advocacy, and who have demonstrated superior professional competence. Nationally, only about 2200 attorneys have received civil trial board certification to date.

Lisle is a Fellow of the Litigation Counsel of America, a national trial lawyer honorary society whose membership is limited to less than one-half of one percent of American lawyers. Fellowship in the LCA is highly selective and by invitation only. Wisconsin's LCA Fellow delegation includes only 58 lawyers and judges. Fellows are selected based upon excellence and accomplishment in trial law, both at the trial and appellate levels, and superior ethical reputation.

Lisle has been named a Wisconsin Super Lawyer by the Wisconsin Super Lawyers magazine since 2010. The Super Lawyers listing is based upon 12 indicators of peer recognition and professional achievement - things like experience, verdicts, clients, honors and awards. The Wisconsin Super Lawyers listing represents the top 5 percent of the lawyers in the state.

Lisle has received an "AV"® rating from the prestigious Martindale-Hubbell Peer Review ratings service. Under this worldwide lawyer rating program, individual attorneys are reviewed in confidence by their peers. Grades are given for professional ability and ethical standards. Lisle has been awarded the AV® rating by his fellow lawyers. This is the highest rating available, reflecting Lisle's "preeminent" legal ability rating and his "very high" ethical standard rating. Lisle has maintained an AV® rating for over 20 years.

Lisle has developed a comprehensive civil trial practice, concentrating in complex business, corporate, and land use litigation, along with extensive experience in plaintiffs' personal injury matters. Lisle has achieved successful results for many clients, large and small, commercial and individual, and has appeared in state and federal courts throughout the United States. Lisle's recent experiences include recovering significant personal injury damage awards for several individuals and families victimized by negligent conduct, representing small businesses with regard to land use, zoning and constitutional law damages claims, representing landowners in the enforcement of easements and restrictive covenants, representing corporations and individuals in professional services malpractice claims and assisting clients with the establishment and defense of riparian property rights.

Lisle is licensed to practice in all courts in Wisconsin, including the Federal District Court, Eastern and Western Districts of Wisconsin. Lisle has also been admitted to practice in the Federal District Court for the Northern District of Illinois and the Federal District Court for the Northern District of Ohio.

Lisle is a member of the Walworth County Bar Association (President 1995-1996), State Bar of Wisconsin, Wisconsin Association for Justice (formerly Wisconsin Academy of Trial Lawyers), and the American Association of Justice (formerly Association of Trial Lawyers of America).

attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of David A. Blumberg
attorneys.practice_type: Interstate Child Custody Jurisdiction Lawyers in Glendale, WI
attorneys.bio:
David A. Blumberg is an attorney in private practice in Milwaukee County, Wisconsin. As a family law practitioner, he limits his practice to interstate child custody jurisdiction and enforcement cases. He is a recognized authority on child custody jurisdiction and on the Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act.

Attorney Blumberg graduated from the University of Southern California Law School in 1970 and practiced in Southern California until 1985. In 1982, he became one of the first lawyers to be certified by the State Bar of California as a Specialist in Family Law. From 1986 to 1999, he practiced family law in New York, where he also edited and published the New York Family Law Update, a weekly newsletter for New York family lawyers and judges.

After moving his practice to Southeast Wisconsin, he narrowed his family law practice to child custody cases. In 2007 he began further limiting his practice to interstate child custody jurisdiction and enforcement cases. That’s all he handles now.

Throughout his career in the law, Attorney Blumberg has tried to improve the lives of children by minimizing conflict between their too-often antagonistic parents.

attorneys.name: Lynn J. Bodi
attorneys.practice_type: Surrogacy and Assisted Reproduction Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Lynn is one of the founders of The Law Center for Children & Families. She is a creative litigator and strategist who devotes her skills to protecting the rights of children. She believes the law should provide solutions, not roadblocks. Her 30 years of experience include many jury and court trials, as well as helping to develop state and national laws and ethical rules for surrogacy and adoption. She acted as expert witness in Mercycare Insurance Company v. Wisconsin Commissioner of Insurance, a Wisconsin Supreme Court case addressing maternity coverage for surrogates.

Her practice focuses on children’s law, both contested and uncontested proceedings, including surrogacy, termination of parental rights, adoption, disruptions, CHIPS, visitation, custody, guardianship, and foster parent, grandparent and family-in-fact issues. She represents clients in court trials, jury trials, and appeals, and is retained frequently by international couples coming to Wisconsin for surrogacy. Lynn is fluent in French and especially loves working with families from France.

Lynn is also one of the founders and is now the sole owner of Adoptions of Wisconsin, Inc., in Madison, Wisconsin. The Law Center serves as the agency’s general counsel and handles all of its terminations of parental rights and adoptions. She also founded and own a surrogacy coordinating program, before selling it in 2017. She strives to ensure the integrity of the family formation process.

PRACTICE AREAS

Surrogacy

Assisted Reproduction

Adoption (Contested and Uncontested)

Appeals

Child Custody, Placement, and Support

CHIPS

Guardianship

Foster Parent Rights

Grandparent Rights

LGBTQ Family Law

EDUCATION

Lynn graduated from the University of Wisconsin-Madison with Honors and was elected to Phi Beta Kappa, majoring in Communication Arts and French. She received her law degree from the University of Wisconsin Law School. She enjoys being able to communicate with her French clients in French and continues to use both her undergraduate degrees, sometimes at the same time.

COMMUNITY AND PROFESSIONAL ACTIVITIES

As a fellow in the Academy of Adoption and Assisted Reproduction Attorneys (“AAAA”), Lynn has been heavily involved in its governance, serving three terms on the Board of Trustees, as past Vice President, and on various committees, including one formed to revise AAAA’s Code of Ethics.

In 2011, Lynn was awarded the U.S. Congressional “Angel in Adoption” award, which recognizes and honors the good work of individuals who have enriched the lives of children through adoption. She was nominated by Congresswoman Tammy Baldwin.

Lynn speaks and writes on legal issues affecting children at the state and national level. She has spoken to judges and court commissioners about surrogacy and adoption, and at American Bar Association Family Law conferences, and she regularly presents at AAAA’s annual and mid-year conferences. At the University of Wisconsin Law School, Lynn has been a guest lecturer on adoption, family law, trial advocacy, and general practice. She has contributed to such publications as Adoptive Families, Adoption Factbook, and Adoption Law: Practice and Procedure in the 21st Century. She also works on state legislation affecting children, including surrogacy legislation and various adoption reform bills.

PERSONAL

Lynn and her husband have two sons and a Labrador Retriever named Dizzy, of whom they are very proud. Lynn enjoys all kinds of fitness activities, including running, weight-lifting, and yoga (especially headstand). She is also a fair violinist, who plays with the Madison Community Orchestra and the choir at her church. For years, Lynn has also worked with Madison Horizons Rotary as a Meals on Wheels driver. Sometimes, she finds time to knit.

Awards and Honors

Attorney Andrew R. Bosshard focuses his practice on business law, acting as general counsel and trusted advisor to privately-held businesses and their owners on issues of start-up, contracts, financing, governance, mergers, acquisitions, real estate, succession and estate planning.

A particular area of emphasis is banking law and creditor rights. Andrew marks the fourth generation Bosshard family member to serve the firm and the La Crosse legal community. Prior to returning home to join Bosshard Parke Ltd., he was associated with the law firm of Cades Schutte LLP a prominent Honolulu law firm.

Attorney Ryan Braithwaite’s legal practice focuses on municipal law, municipal litigation, and general litigation in Wisconsin. Ryan has over 20 years of experience representing municipalities in contract disputes, defense of high-end property tax appeals, eminent domain, handling special assessments, land use, zoning regulations, drafting municipal ordinances and contracts, and open meetings/records.

Ryan’s litigation experience also includes non-municipal general litigation matters such as commercial disputes, contract disputes, product liability, insurance defense, trademark and copyright, federal and appellate litigation, and personal injury cases. Ryan has argued before the Wisconsin Court of Appeals and the 7th Circuit.

Ryan’s background includes presenting on a range of legal topics before the Wisconsin State Bar, CVMIC, and the Civil Trial Counsel of Wisconsin. In addition, he has written articles published in Civil Trial Counsel of Wisconsin and Wisconsin Realtor Magazine. Earlier in his career, Ryan was recognized as a “Rising Star” by Wisconsin Super Lawyers.

Based in the firm’s Madison office, Ryan is also available to assist clients in our Dodgeville and Janesville offices, and throughout Wisconsin.

attorneys.practice_type: Divorce & Family Law Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Julianne Brock focuses her legal practice on family law issues, including divorce, collaborative divorce, paternity, marital agreements (prenuptial and postnuptial agreements), legal separation, post-divorce matters, child support, maintenance/alimony, and grandparents’ rights. In addition, Julianne assists clients with litigation and business legal matters.

Prior to joining Murphy Desmond, Julianne was a legal intern with in-house counsel for a Belgium software company and in-house counsel for a Wisconsin-based life sciences company, where she gained experience in business law and intellectual property.

As a Student Associate with the Frank J. Remington Center’s Family Law Project, Julianne assisted Wisconsin inmates with their family law matters.

During her time at the University of Wisconsin Law School, Julianne was the Senior Managing Article Editor for the Wisconsin Journal of Law, Gender, and Society. She competed on the Moot Court team and led discussion groups for visiting international law students. In addition, Julianne volunteered over 100 hours of her time to various pro bono projects, earning her the “Award of Distinction” from the University of Wisconsin Pro Bono Society. Julianne also received an award for “Family Law” by the American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers-Wisconsin Chapter.

In her spare time, Julianne immerses herself in baking, podcasts, and enjoying all that Madison, Wisconsin, has to offer.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Appleton, WI
attorneys.bio:
While I am relatively new to Wisconsin, I bring years of professional experience to my role as an associate attorney at J. Kippa Law. I have both civil and criminal litigation in my background, but vastly prefer the world of criminal law. My primary experience is as a prosecutor. attorneys.name: Lindsey Burghardt
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Lindsey Burghardt practices exclusively as a Family Law Attorney; however, her previous experience includes: Estate-Planning, Probate and Bankruptcy. Attorney Burghardt’s experience in these areas assists her in giving clients a well-rounded approach to family law, which can often intertwine with other areas of the law. Lindsey frequently serves as Guardian ad Litem in cases involving minor children and works as a Mediator through the Milwaukee County Family Court Commissioner’s Office.

Attorney Burghardt takes an efficient and honest approach to representation of her clients. While acknowledging emotions present in each and every family case, Lindsey is sure to offer her clients realistic solutions that satisfy her clients’ needs and are aimed at reducing conflict. One of Attorney Burghardt’s main goals in representing clients is to give realistic expectations and to keep clients prepared and informed each step of the way.

Attorney Burghardt graduated magna cum laude from Michigan Technological University in 2004, where she received her Bachelor’s Degree majoring in Social Science with a minor in Psychology. She graduated from Marquette Law School in 2007. During law school, and since graduating, Attorney Burghardt’s primary practice area has been family law.

Attorney Burghardt is a member of the Milwaukee Bar Association and the Society of Family Lawyers (“SOFL.”). She is a trained Mediator and regularly Volunteers at the Milwaukee Justice Center, assisting parties with voluntary Parenting Conferences.

attorneys.name: Gretchen Burgess
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning & Probate Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Gretchen Burgess is dedicated to helping individuals and families navigate the complexities of estate planning, including the preparation of revocable and irrevocable trusts, wills, powers of attorney for healthcare and finance, special and supplemental needs trusts, and marital property agreements.

Gretchen also handles the establishment and termination of adult guardianships, as well as the preparation of Wispact trusts. She assists clients in all aspects of the estate administration process, including formal and informal estate administration, special administration, and trust administration.

In addition, Gretchen has significant experience in farm succession planning. In fact, she has presented on farm succession planning to farm families through the University of Wisconsin’s Agricultural Extension program. Her knowledge of the topic is an asset to the firm’s overall abilities to help farmers with business operations, property sales/purchases, divorces, and other legal matters that affect farmers.

Community commitment is important to Gretchen. She is an active member through service on boards of several organizations that affect children, families, and the community overall. She has volunteered her time with Big Brothers Big Sisters, CASA, Crimestoppers, and Rotary Botanical Garden. She is also active in legal organizations and volunteering her time for higher education.

Gretchen is available to meet with clients in the firm’s Madison and Janesville offices, as well as remotely.

attorneys.name: Axel F. Candelaria Rivera
attorneys.practice_type: Administrative and Regulatory Law Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Axel F. Candelaria Rivera’s legal practice combines his background in administrative law and litigation to assist clients on a variety of substantive and procedural legal issues, including professional licensing defense and other administrative law matters.

Axel has litigated before State agencies, circuit courts, and in the Court of Appeals. As an Attorney with the State of Wisconsin Department of Agriculture, Trade and Consumer Protection, Axel drafted and reviewed legislation, provided legal defense to the agency, and pursued prosecutions on behalf of the agency. He also provided legal counsel to board members. Axel represented the State of Wisconsin Department of Revenue for a decade, where he litigated tax cases, assisted with the drafting of administrative rules, analyzed proposed legislation, and presented on tax law changes. He also represented the Wisconsin State Lottery, including in cases involving breach of contract claims.

In addition to Axel’s experience with State agencies, he served as a Senior Tax Manager at Deloitte Tax, LLP, where he appeared before tax tribunals, in and out of Wisconsin, representing companies in tax disputes and litigation. He presented and trained on case law, legislative updates, and audit trends.

Axel served in private practice earlier in his career. He is involved in his community, including serving as a Board Member on the City of Fitchburg’s Zoning Board of Appeals. Axel is fluent in Spanish and English.

Based in the firm’s Madison office, Axel is available to serve clients throughout Wisconsin on professional licensing and administrative law issues.

attorneys.name: Eduardo E. Castro
attorneys.practice_type: Political & Election Law Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
As an Associate in the firm's Litigation Practice Group, Eduardo understands the disruption and uncertainty litigation may bring to a client's life. Clients appreciate Eduardo's careful attention to their needs and goals when legal representation is needed.

A skilled litigator and courtroom advocate, Eduardo maintains a robust and diverse practice. Eduardo assists clients to successful outcomes in numerous areas, including in criminal defense, civil and constitutional rights, political and election law, health law, environmental law, civil litigation, and immigration law. He represents and advises clients at all stages of civil and criminal proceedings in state and federal court, arbitration and mediation, and in front of federal and state administrative bodies.

Eduardo brings a wealth of practical experience to augment his legal advocacy. In 2020, Eduardo worked as the Regional Voter Protection Director for Southeastern Wisconsin on the Biden for President/Democratic Coordinated Campaign. He has served as an Urban Fellow in the Office of the Deputy Mayor for Health and Human Services of the City of New York and as an Americorps® member in a federally qualified health center on the south side of Milwaukee. In law school, Eduardo was a Student Director in the Binger Center for New Americans, representing detained immigrants facing the threat of removal from the United States.

Eduardo is also passionate about promoting diversity and inclusion. He is actively involved in efforts to increase the representation of historically marginalized groups in the legal profession.

attorneys.name: Corey Chirafisi
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Corey C. Chirafisi is a partner at Chirafisi Anderson, S.C., where he focuses his practice exclusively on criminal defense and OWI representation in Wisconsin state and federal courts. With more than two decades of experience, and approximately 120 cases tried to verdict, he has represented individuals facing charges ranging from misdemeanors to serious felony allegations throughout Wisconsin.

As a former prosecutor Chirafisi brings a distinctive perspective to criminal defense. His experience informs his current work, allowing him to evaluate cases with an understanding of prosecutorial decision-making, charging strategies, and trial preparation.

As a partner at Chirafisi Anderson, S.C., Attorney Chirafisi remains directly involved in client representation. He emphasizes careful case evaluation, strategic planning, and clear communication, ensuring that clients understand the process, the evidence, and the legal options available to them at every stage of their case.

Attorney Corey C. Chirafisi represents individuals charged with offenses ranging from misdemeanors to serious felonies, including complex cases that require extensive motion practice and trial preparation.

A substantial portion of Attorney Chirafisi’s work involves OWI and impaired driving defense at all levels. His approach emphasizes careful evaluation of traffic stops, testing procedures, and evidentiary issues, as well as the strategic use of pretrial litigation to challenge the State’s case.

In addition to OWI matters, Attorney Chirafisi handles a broad spectrum of criminal cases in both state and federal court. His practice reflects familiarity with the procedural and strategic considerations that vary by forum, allowing him to tailor defense strategies to the specific facts, evidence, and court involved.

Attorney Corey C. Chirafisi has practiced criminal law for more than two decades. He earned his Juris Doctor from the City University of New York School of Law and was admitted to practice law in Wisconsin in 1998.

Attorney Chirafisi began his legal career as an assistant district attorney in Kenosha County, where he prosecuted a wide range of criminal cases. That experience provided early exposure to charging decisions, case evaluation, and trial preparation from the prosecution’s perspective—insight that continues to inform his defense work.

After transitioning into private practice, Attorney Chirafisi devoted his career exclusively to criminal defense and OWI representation. His background includes extensive experience litigating cases in both Wisconsin circuit courts and federal court, as well as speaking at continuing legal education seminars at the state and national level. His work reflects long-standing familiarity with criminal procedure, evidentiary standards, and courtroom practice across jurisdictions.

Attorney Corey C. Chirafisi has received consistent peer recognition for his work in criminal defense and OWI matters over the course of his career.

He has been selected as a Super Lawyer every year from 2011 through 2025, a distinction awarded to top 5% of defense attorneys based on peer evaluation and professional achievement. Earlier in his career, in 2007 and 2008, he was named a Super Lawyers Rising Star.

Attorney Chirafisi was also been ranked one of the Top 25 Super Lawyers in Madison and recognized as one of the Top 20 attorneys in across all practice areas in 2017–2019 and 2022, reflecting sustained professional respect within the legal community.

Chirafisi received the Martin Hanson award from the Wisconsin Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers for his trial work in State v. Rittenhouse. He also received the SCN award for securing a not guilty verdict in a sex assault case.

attorneys.bio:
Nathan T. Clemens is a dedicated attorney with a diverse legal background and a strong commitment to advocacy and justice. His fluency in Spanish and experience working with a wide range of legal issues allow him to provide comprehensive, client-focused representation.

Nathan graduated Magna Cum Laude from the University of Wisconsin-Green Bay in December 2020, earning a Bachelor’s degree in Spanish and Latin American Culture with a minor in International Business. He then pursued his legal education at Marquette University Law School, where he graduated Cum Laude in May 2024. While at Marquette, he was an active member of the Marquette Immigration Law Association, demonstrating his passion for advocacy.

Nathan’s legal career began in immigration law, where he worked extensively with Spanish-speaking clients at Catholic Charities of the Archdiocese of Milwaukee and Grzeca Law Group. He later expanded his practice to include family law, landlord-tenant law, estate planning, and general civil litigation at Salutz and Salutz Law, LLP.

In November 2024, Nathan joined MGW Law, LLP, where his practice shifted to insurance law, focusing on bad faith litigation and insurance claims disputes. His diverse experience and language skills make him a valuable asset to the firm and a trusted advocate for his clients.

attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Brookfield, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Thomas Corbett is dedicated to his clients, listening closely to their concerns, understanding their goals, and helping them make informed decisions. He understands that family law matters are deeply personal and strives to provide strong legal guidance and steady support throughout.

He pursued his legal education at Marquette University Law School, focusing strongly on family law. Through coursework and clinical experiences, Attorney Corbett gained hands-on experience and knowledge of the legal and practical challenges individuals face during divorce, custody/placement disputes, and other family law matters.

While in law school, he began his career as a law clerk at a Milwaukee-based family law firm and devoted significant time to pro bono service. He volunteered with the Milwaukee Justice Center (MJC) and the Marquette Volunteer Legal Clinics (MVLC), offering support to individuals who could not otherwise afford representation. These experiences inspired his commitment to serving those navigating major life transitions.

While not a native Wisconsinite, Attorney Corbett enjoys living in Wisconsin and is proud to serve individuals and families across the state.

attorneys.name: Michael Covey
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Michael Covey is a criminal defense attorney at Chirafisi Anderson, S.C., where he represents individuals facing serious felony charges in Wisconsin courts. He brings more than two decades of experience in criminal defense, with a practice that has included a wide range of case types and a particular focus on complex, high-exposure litigation.

Attorney Covey’s background includes extensive trial work in cases involving allegations of homicide and sexual assault. His experience in this area reflects a career devoted to courtroom advocacy and the defense of individuals facing the most serious consequences under Wisconsin law. He approaches these matters with careful preparation, close attention to evidentiary issues, and a willingness to litigate cases through trial when appropriate.

In 2023, after nearly two decades in private practice, Attorney Covey joined Chirafisi Law Office, where he worked closely with Attorney Corey Chirafisi litigating complex felony matters. He continues that work as part of Chirafisi Anderson, S.C., bringing the same trial-focused approach and commitment to individualized defense representation to the firm.

Attorney Michael Covey focuses his practice on the defense of serious felony matters in Wisconsin courts. While he has experience across a broad range of criminal cases, his work has concentrated on complex, high-exposure litigation involving allegations of homicide and sexual assault.

His practice in this area emphasizes intensive case investigation, detailed evidentiary review, and trial-level advocacy. Attorney Covey routinely handles cases that require careful analysis of forensic evidence, witness credibility, and constitutional issues, as well as extensive motion practice and pretrial litigation.

In addition to serious felony defense, Attorney Covey has experience representing clients in other criminal matters, including OWI offenses, drug charges, juvenile cases, battery, property crimes, and appellate matters. Across all case types, his practice reflects a trial-focused approach and individualized defense strategy based on the facts and procedural posture of each case.

Attorney Michael Covey has practiced criminal defense law since 2003. He earned his law degree from the University of Wisconsin Law School and has spent his career focused exclusively on criminal defense work in Wisconsin courts.

A significant portion of Attorney Covey’s career has included representing indigent defendants and accepting court-appointed matters, work that has required extensive courtroom experience and familiarity with the full range of criminal procedure. Over time, he developed a practice centered on trial-level litigation and complex felony matters.

After operating the Covey Law Office for approximately 18 years, Attorney Covey closed his solo practice in 2023 and joined Chirafisi Law Office. He now continues his work as part of Chirafisi Anderson, S.C., where he brings a long-standing trial background and experience handling high-stakes criminal cases across Wisconsin.

Attorney Michael Covey has received multiple peer-recognized honors for his work in criminal defense and his service to indigent defendants in Wisconsin courts.

He has been recognized by the Wisconsin Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers with several awards, including the Hanson Memorial Advocate’s Prize (2023) and the Kuchler Nicholson Stilling Award (2023), honoring excellence in criminal defense advocacy. He is also a recipient of the David C. Niblack Award (2019), recognizing outstanding contributions to criminal defense practice.

Attorney Covey’s commitment to public service and pro bono representation has been recognized by the State Bar of Wisconsin, which named him to the Pro Bono Honor Society multiple times between 2014 and 2020. In 2019, he was also the first recipient of the Danny Berkos Award from the Wisconsin State Public Defender, acknowledging exceptional service to indigent clients.

Earlier in his career, Attorney Covey was named Warrior of the Year (2011) by the Dane County Criminal Defense Lawyers Association in recognition of his trial advocacy. He earned that award a second time in 2024.
