attorneys.name: Chase Cripe
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Brookfield, WI
attorneys.bio:
A native Hoosier, Attorney Chase D. Cripe graduated from Indiana University with a degree in political science and minors in business, criminal justice, and Spanish before moving to Wisconsin and attending Marquette Law School. It was there that Chase – by accident – discovered his passion for family law. From then on, he has dedicated himself to the practice and serving clients throughout southern and central Wisconsin.

With a strong foundation in family law and years of experience, Chase has earned a reputation as a relatable and reliable advocate for his clients. Clients commend him for his expertise and unique approach to their cases.

Chase brings a different creative and all-encompassing approach to his practice, along with a comprehensive understanding of family legal principles. One of Chase’s distinguishing strengths is his personalized approach to client communication. Recognizing that legal matters such as these can be emotionally challenging and intimidating, he ensures that his clients feel heard throughout the process and understand what is going on around them. By taking the time to learn their personalities, unique circumstances, concerns, and objectives, Chase tailors his legal strategies to try and achieve the best possible outcomes for his clients in their given situation.

Whether dealing with issues related to child custody/placement, property division, maintenance, or any other aspect of family law, Chase is dedicated to protecting his clients’ rights and interests. His strong advocacy skill and understanding of the broader context help create a strategic vision encompasses not only the legal intricacies, but also the holistic needs and long-term goals of his clients.

Born and raised in Madison, Wisconsin. After college graduation, served two years as U.S. Naval Intelligence Officer (1958 -1960). attorneys.name: Christine Davies D'Angelo
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Waukesha, WI
attorneys.bio:
Christine D' Angelo is a partner at D' Angelo & Grabow, LLP, in Waukesha, Wisconsin. She graduated from the University of Wisconsin Law School, cum laude, in 1999. She concentrates her practice in the area of family law including divorce, child custody, child placement, child support, paternity and post-judgement matters. She is also a certified Family Law Mediator and as a Collaborative Divorce practitioner. She is passionate about trying to help people transition out of a marriage in a way that is both respectful and graceful.

Attorney D'Angelo believes knowledge is power, especially when weighing choices and options in the divorce process. It is her goal to ensure her clients are making the best decisions for themselves and their families by being fully informed and educated about the issues in their case.

Christine grew up in Waukesha, the youngest of three daughters. When she entered the first grade, her mother returned to school to obtain a law degree thus inspiring Christine's career choice. She is a third-generation lawyer and spent the first 14 years of her career in a law practice with her mother.

Attorney D'Angelo is a member of the State Bar of Wisconsin. She currently serves on the Board of Directors and is a Past Chair of the Collaborative Family Law Council of Wisconsin and on the Board of Directors for the Collaborative Foundation of Wisconsin. She has also served in various capacities on the Board of Directors for the Wisconsin Justinian Society of Lawyers and was named Italian of the Year in 2009. Ms. D'Angelo previously served on the Board of Directors for the Waukesha County Bar Association, where she also served a term as President. Outside of the legal system Attorney D'Angelo was a member of the Board of Directors for the Mental Health Association in Waukesha County.

Christine D'Angelo has been selected for inclusion in Wisconsin Super Lawyers for the last 13 years (2011 - 2023) and was named as one of the Top 25 Women Lawyers by Wisconsin Super Lawyers 5 times. She was previously selected as a Wisconsin Super Lawyers-Rising Star in 2006 - 2008 & 2010.

Attorney D'Angelo is AVVO Rated as “Superb” and has been selected as a Leading Lawyer, Divorce & Separation, in 2015 in M Magazine's Leading Lawyers list. AVVO selects roughly the top 2% to 5% of lawyers in each practice area for inclusion on M Magazine's Leading Lawyers list.

When not practicing law, Christine spends her time with her husband, Brad, and their two teenage children. She enjoys reading, watching TV, traveling and college sports especially the Wisconsin Badgers.

attorneys.bio:
Bruce M. Davey is an attorney at the law firm Davey & Goldman Law Firm located in Madison, Wisconsin. Bruce Davey has earned a stellar reputation as an attorney who specializes in labor and employment law. His reputation for effectively handling both civil and criminal trials has helped build his profile. He has made a name for himself as a lightning-fast litigator.

Bruce attended law school at the University of Wisconsin and graduated in 1968; he was subsequently inducted into the Wisconsin chapter of The Order of the Coif. When he was in school, he contributed to the Wisconsin Law Review.

Bruce is included in the Bar Register of Preeminent Lawyers and has an AV Preeminent* peer-review rating from Martindale-Hubbell. From 1987 to the present, he has consistently been included in The Best Lawyers in America. He has been featured numerous times in Madison Magazine, named on its Top Lawyers list. Bruce Davey was recognized by both Law & Politics and Milwaukee Magazine and was included in their Super Lawyers lists from 2005 to 2011.

*AV®, AV Preeminent®, Martindale-Hubbell Distinguished and Martindale-Hubbell Notable are certification marks used under license in accordance with the Martindale-Hubbell certification procedures, standards and policies. Martindale-Hubbell® is the facilitator of a peer-review rating process. Ratings reflect the anonymous opinions of members of the bar and the judiciary. attorneys.name: Dustan Davidson
attorneys.practice_type: Fourth Amendment Law Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Dustan is a skilled and strategic criminal defense attorney known for his precision, courtroom presence, and passionate advocacy. A cum laude graduate of Marquette University Law School, he began his career in civil litigation at a firm specializing in medical malpractice, where he built a strong foundation in case management and legal analysis.

His interest in criminal law deepened during law school through a Trial Advocacy course with the Honorable Laura Crivello, followed by an internship in her courtroom. He also served as a research assistant to Professor Gregory O’Meara, S.J., contributing to scholarship on political white-collar crime and democratic institutions.

Dustan launched his legal practice as a prosecutor in the Milwaukee County District Attorney’s Office, where he gained invaluable experience handling a broad range of criminal matters. This dual perspective—having worked both as a prosecutor and a defense attorney—gives him a powerful advantage in building effective defense strategies.

He has developed particular expertise in Fourth Amendment law, including unlawful searches, arrests, and suppression motions. Known for his attention to detail and unwavering commitment to his clients, Dustan brings both technical skill and genuine dedication to every case he handles.

attorneys.name: Katherine J. De Lorenzo
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Katherine Jochman De Lorenzo is a partner with the Gagne McChrystal De Lorenzo & Burghardt law firm in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. A top-rated attorney with nearly 15 years of legal experience, Ms. De Lorenzo focuses her practice exclusively on family law, and she provides exceptional representation to clients throughout Milwaukee and across the state who are going through a divorce or have some other serious legal issue affecting their families.

As an attorney, Ms. De Lorenzo strives to provide the highest level of counsel and support possible through experienced, dedicated, and compassionate advocacy. Well-versed in mediation and other alternative dispute resolution techniques, she prefers to help her clients resolve their conflicts and reach agreements on child custody and support, property division, spousal maintenance, and other related matters without having to resort to costly, stressful, and adversarial court proceedings.

A staunch advocate for her clients and their children, Ms. De Lorenzo routinely serves as guardian ad litem in contentious child custody cases, and she has extensive experience assisting with paternity actions and fighting for the rights and interests of parents. Whether inside or outside of the courtroom, she maintains an unwavering focus on her clients' needs and goals, and she aggressively pursues the most favorable outcomes to help them face this new chapter in their lives with confidence.

A 1995 graduate of the University of Wisconsin-Madison with degrees in psychology and women's studies, Ms. De Lorenzo obtained her Juris Doctor from Marquette University Law School in 2007. While there, she volunteered with the Task Force on Family Violence and then participated in the International Chamber of Commerce Commercial Mediation Competition and the American Bar Association Representation in Mediation Competition.

Highly active in her legal community, Ms. De Lorenzo is a member of the Waukesha County and Milwaukee Bar associations, the State Bar of Wisconsin, the American Bar Association, and the Divorce Cooperation Institute. She is also a member of the Collaborative Family Law Council of Wisconsin and the Eastern District of Wisconsin Bar Association as well as the Justinian Society of Lawyers.

attorneys.name: T. Alexander Dee
attorneys.practice_type: Life and Estate Planning Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Alek is a thorough and earnest advocate for our families and businesses. He believes that detailed and methodical planning should be accessible to all families and businesses. In his practice, Alek looks to put his clients’ wishes first and understands that everyone’s circumstances are unique and deserve personalized attention. There are no templates churned in his practice. He is committed to taking the time to listen to his clients’ concerns, answer their questions, and give them the information they need to make informed decisions about their future and the future of their loved ones and businesses. Alek and The Law Center have a particular interest in serving military and law enforcement families in their life and estate planning needs.

Alek is a double Badger: he graduated with distinction from the University of Wisconsin-Madison with a B.S. in Political Science, and his law degree from the University of Wisconsin Law School.

While in law school, Alek interned for Justice Ann Walsh Bradley of the Wisconsin Supreme Court and clerked for the Wisconsin Department of Revenue. He also volunteered at the Milwaukee Justice Center, working with their Civil Legal Helpline to connect members of the community to legal resources that could address their legal needs, and was a member of the Business and Tax Law Association and Real Estate and Investments Society. Alek was also honored to serve as an intern in the Wisconsin State Assembly as an undergraduate student.

attorneys.name: Renee L. Dehn
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in La Crosse, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Renee L. Dehn is a seasoned trial attorney whose practice focuses on family law, employment matters, criminal law and civil litigation. Renee has 12 years of litigation experience and has tried dozens of cases.

Renee represents clients in family law matters involving divorce, custody, placement, child support, property division and paternity issues. Renee understands that these matters are often very complex and difficult emotionally and she guides her clients through their case process with care and understanding.

Renee also assists clients with a variety of employment matters such as drafting and reviewing severance agreements, personnel handbooks and personnel policies, as well as litigating wrongful termination, discrimination claims and unemployment insurance appeal issues.

In the area of criminal law, Renee has tried many serious and high profile felony cases. She spent many years as a prosecutor and has extensive knowledge and expertise in the area of O.W.I./D.U.I. law. While serving in the Winnebago County State’s Attorney’s Office (Rockford, IL) Renee was named as an “Outstanding Assistant State’s Attorney” by AAIM (Alliance Against Intoxicated Motorists). Renee has taught on a variety of topics related to impaired driving for the Illinois Department of Transportation through the University of Illinois-Springfield.

Renee also assists clients in resolving monetary and contractual disputes. Renee’s attention to detail and tireless work ethic delivers outstanding results for her clients.

attorneys.practice_type: Divorce & Family Law Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Sarah DeKraay's legal practice focuses on family law matters, which includes divorce, legal separation, pre-nuptial and post-nuptial agreements, maintenance (alimony), custody, child support, placement, paternity, grandparents' rights, child removal cases, adoptions and guardianships. She also handles post-divorce matters regarding children, child support, relocation and out-of-state custody issues, maintenance modifications, and contempt of court issues. A shareholder with Murphy Desmond, Sarah has served clients in family law matters in Madison, Dane County, and throughout southwestern Wisconsin since 2001. She earned a Master of Business Administration (M.B.A.) in 2002. Sarah has presented on divorce topics at seminars sponsored by the Wisconsin State Bar. An avid golfer, Sarah is a board member and past president with the Executive Women's Golf Association. In college, Sarah was a member of the women's golf team at Indiana University, where she was a three-time All-American and Big Ten Champion golfer.

attorneys.name: Patrick S. DeMoon III
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Elkhorn, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Patrick S. DeMoon III began his legal career in 1997 when he accepted an appointment as an Assistant Attorney General in the Illinois Office of the Attorney General. For the next five years, Attorney DeMoon represented the state and its elected officials as the lead attorney on a number of high-profile cases, several of which were featured on television and the front pages of Chicago area newspapers. He then served for two years as the Senior Regulatory Attorney for the Chicago Stock Exchange, helping to protect the integrity of the national securities markets. In 2004 Attorney DeMoon moved to his family's historic farm in Wisconsin and began practicing law in Walworth County. He now represents clients on a variety of corporate and real estate related matters.

Attorney DeMoon earned his B.A. from Northwestern University and his J.D. from DePaul University's College of Law. He is licensed to practice law in the federal and state courts of both Illinois and Wisconsin.

attorneys.name: Cathleen A. Dettmann
attorneys.practice_type: General Business Law Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Cathleen is an associate in the firm whose practice is concentrated on business litigation, including franchise disputes, copyright and trademark issues, business break-ups, non-compete and trade secret litigation as well as general contract disputes. She also does a considerable amount of work on transactional matters: Cathleen is experienced in representing clients who are buying and selling businesses, working with business start-ups and in drafting various kinds of contracts including licensing agreements and operating agreements, among others.

Additionally, Cathleen focuses on providing estate and succession planning for both businesses and individuals and particularly enjoys working with family farms to resolve the complex planning issues presented by the farming business. She works regularly with individuals and families to help achieve their planning goals, including advanced tax and trust planning for families who need these services.

Prior to joining Haley Palmersheim, Cathleen worked for several years as a lobbyist and public policy analyst, representing a variety of clients’ interests before the Wisconsin State Legislature. As a lobbyist and as an attorney, Cathleen has gained a great deal of experience in analyzing complex issues, in resolving multifaceted disputes efficiently, and in advocating for the best interests of her clients and their businesses. Cathleen is adept at analyzing a client’s situation and determining a strategy that can range from forceful advocacy to a delicate balancing of issues requiring a collaborative approach.

Cathleen graduated from the University of Wisconsin Law School cum laude and achieved Order of the Coif. In law school, she was active on the Moot Court Board and produced the school’s popular annual comedy sketch show, Stuart’s Law Revue. She also obtained her undergraduate degree from UW-Madison, graduating with a bachelor of arts in political science. While in college, Cathleen studied abroad at Trinity College in Dublin, Ireland, studying Irish poetry and literature.

attorneys.name: B. Harper Dickerson
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney B. Harper Dickerson is passionate about defending workers’ rights, about uncovering and litigating fraud, and about social justice more broadly. Harper focuses on complex matters involving discrimination on the basis of sex, sexual orientation, and gender identity, including matters of sexual harassment, as well as discrimination on the basis of race, national origin, age, religion, and more. He also focuses on False Claims Act work, using his keen eye for detail to take allegations of fraud from investigation to filing and pursuing qui tam actions.

For Harper, the goal is always to attain justice for his clients and to vindicate and enforce their rights. He works hard to obtain resolutions whenever possible—that way, his clients receive the relief they’re seeking more quickly—which often allows him to obtain remedies for his clients that wouldn’t be available in court. But when settlement proves not to be an option, he is a confident and effective litigator.

During law school, Harper worked with the Neighborhood Law Clinic, defending community members against eviction actions and other actions based in housing discrimination; was recognized as an Outstanding Note and Comment Editor for his service to the Wisconsin International Law Journal; and completed the Labor and Employment Law Concentration with Honors.

Also during law school, Harper worked with the nonprofit Environmental Law and Policy Center, helping to shape its legal response to federal efforts to conserve old-growth forests on public lands; and with Lac Courte Oreilles Band of Lake Superior Ojibwe, performing extensive employment-law research and writing in matters of state, federal, and tribal law.

Harper is a proud Wisconsin transplant. He comes to Milwaukee by way of Austin, Texas; he earned his B.A. in English from UT-Austin (hook ‘em, Horns!), where he also worked as an undergraduate tutor at the University Writing Center, before earning his law degree at the University of Wisconsin in Madison.

Before he took up the law, Harper also worked as a copy editor for a local newspaper and as an insurance advisor for a small-business insurance startup. In his free time, Harper enjoys writing and making music: He plays piano and guitar and sings, and he has self-produced and released several albums of songs. He also loves going to the movies, cooking, running, and spending time with his cat, Stirfry.

Charlie also volunteered at the Marquette Legal Clinic and is a founding Board member of Kids' Chance of Wisconsin, a non-profit providing scholarships for the children of seriously injured workers. Charlie's educational allegiance is to the Badgers. He received a B.S., with honors, as a Phi Beta Kappa, from the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He earned his J.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, graduating magna cum laude, and a member of Order of the Coif.

attorneys.name: Tom Domer
attorneys.practice_type: Worker's Compensation Law Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Thomas M. Domer has over 35 years of experience representing injured workers in Wisconsin. He is listed in Best Lawyers in America, and his peers continually recognize him as a Wisconsin Super Lawyer. Tom was named the 2011 Milwaukee Workers' Compensation Lawyer of the Year in Best Lawyers. In 2012, he received the Lifetime Achievement Award for his service and advocacy from the Workers Injury Law & Advocacy Group (WILG).

Tom taught the worker's compensation course at Marquette University Law School, providing the instruction and training for many other lawyers. He lectures frequently around the state and nation (including the State Bar of Wisconsin, UW-Milwaukee, and the University of Wisconsin School for Worker's Compensation Institute). His national and international presentations on worker's compensation practice and ethics for lawyers and law students and long-term advocacy for injured workers earned him election as a Charter Member of the ABA's College of Worker's Compensation Lawyers. He also was elected a member of the National Academy of Social Insurance (NASI), a national organization of leading worker's compensation experts. He also is a prolific writer, editing the national magazine Workers' First Watch, co-authoring over two dozen texts (including West's treatise Wisconsin Workers' Compensation Law), and is regularly quoted in the Milwaukee Journal/Sentinel.

He belongs to numerous professional organizations: Workers Injury Law & Advocacy Group-WILG (Board of Directors and Lifetime Achievement Award Recipient); Wisconsin Association of Justice (Worker's Comp Cmte); American Association of Justice (Past Chair, Workers' Comp Section); Wisconsin Association of Worker's Compensation Attorneys; and the American, State and Milwaukee Bar associations. Tom also remains an active community member, tutoring GED students at Milwaukee's Adult Learning Center and has served on the Board (as past chair) at Dominican High School. Tom earned all his degrees in Wisconsin: B.A.(St. Norbert), M.A.(UW-Milwaukee), Ph.D.(Marquette), and J.D.(UW-Madison).

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Appleton, WI
attorneys.bio:
Personal Injury Attorney Robert J. Domol joined Hupy and Abraham in 2014 after he represented serious personal injury victims in Illinois for nearly a decade. Attorney Domol was promoted to shareholder in 2021. He earned his Juris Doctor in 2004 from DePaul University College of Law and is licensed to practice in Wisconsin, Illinois, and the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Wisconsin.

Attorney Domol is a member of several respected legal organizations, including the American Association for Justice, Wisconsin Association for Justice, and Brown County Bar Association. He has also been a member of the Chicago Bar Association, Illinois Trial Lawyers Association, American Bar Association, and Illinois State Bar Association.

He gives back to the legal community by mentoring law students and new attorneys. He has lectured at various continuing legal education programs and judged student moot court competitions. He and his wife, Krista Seidl, also established a charitable foundation to fund research for treatments for Rett Syndrome, a rare genetic neurological and developmental disorder. He also serves on the Board of Directors of Big Brothers Big Sisters of Northeast Wisconsin.

Attorney Domol has been widely recognized for excellence in personal injury law, including honors from Wisconsin Super Lawyers, Illinois Super Lawyers, a 10.0 Superb Rating from AVVO, and multiple Top 100 Trial Lawyer and Top 40 Under 40 distinctions from The National Trial Lawyers. He has also been recognized by the Wisconsin Law Journal and the National Academy of Personal Injury Attorneys.

Since joining Hupy and Abraham, he has recovered over $110 million in verdicts and settlements for his clients and has resolved several cases for $1 million or more.

attorneys.name: Colin A. Drayton
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Colin represents those going through divorce. He is well-versed in dealing with financial issues such as property division, child support, maintenance, and children’s issues. Additionally, he has drafted and negotiated over 100 prenuptial agreements and postnuptial agreements, and has several published works on this topic.

Colin also has experience with family-law appellate cases, including drafting briefs to the Wisconsin Court of Appeals and the Wisconsin Supreme Court. This included serving as co-counsel in a successful appeal to the Wisconsin Supreme Court in Siech v. Schwab (Wisconsin Supreme Court, published opinion June 22, 2021).

He publishes and presents on family law issues, and on prenuptial agreements. This includes multiple articles in the Wisconsin Journal of Family Law, the American Journal of Family Law, and a co-authored chapter on Wisconsin Prenuptial Agreement Law that was published by Wolters Kluwer.

He is a member of the State Bar of Wisconsin Family Law Section, the Leander J. Foley Society of Family Lawyers, the Association of Family Conciliation Courts, and the Waukesha Bar Association. He also devoted time as part of a task force that revised the Milwaukee County family court rules.

attorneys.name: Thomas W. Durkin
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Racine, WI
attorneys.bio:
Tom has been helping people for over 25 years in the areas of social security disability/ssi, personal injury, and work-related injuries. He has helped thousands of people with their legal cases. He has handled well over 1,000 disability/ssi hearings, hundreds of worker’s compensation hearings, and several jury trials. He has argued cases in Federal Court in the Eastern District of Wisconsin and had cases in the Wisconsin Supreme Court. To say he has extensive experience is an understatement.

But it is not only that, he is always very well prepared and treats your case with compassion, understanding and competent representation, with leads to highly successful results. He will always be in your corner, be your voice, and fight to get you everything that you deserve.

He has published guides to understanding social security disability/ssi and children’s ssi cases. He is on several national organizations for social security disability. In fact, he helped re-write the rules for the Eastern District of Wisconsin for social security disability cases. He has been recognized as an elite lawyer for his work in social security disability. He has also been recognized as one of the national top 100 trial lawyers.

He is very active in community organizations that help people. He has served as a City Planning Commissioner in Racine, been on the Board of Directors for the Health Care Network, the ARC of Racine County, and a member of Rotary.

attorneys.name: Michael A. Edwards
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Michael A. Edwards is a Partner/Shareholder at Galanis, Pollack, Jacobs & Johnson, S.C., who represents clients in family law related matters including divorce, post-judgment disputes and modifications, paternity actions, child custody and placement actions, child support and spousal support actions, and restraining orders/injunctions. Michael attended Drake University in Des Moines, Iowa and graduated in 2014 with University Honors after earning a Bachelor of Arts degree in Law, Politics & Society and Rhetoric & Communication Studies. He attended Marquette University Law School, graduating in 2017. While in law school, he was an editor for the Marquette Sports Law Review. Michael also graduated with a certificate in Sports Law as well as Pro Bono Society Honors for volunteering nearly 400 hours of his time to pro bono legal services.

Prior to joining Galanis, Pollack, Jacobs & Johnson, Attorney Edwards has gained experience practicing law in southeastern Wisconsin and beyond including Wisconsin's Fox Valley region. Attorney Edwards has chosen to solely practice family law as he is strongly interested in working with individuals to address their needs while also successfully guiding them through their family law matters. He firmly believes a collaborative attorney-client approach is crucial, and strives to maintain open and honest communication with his clients, as well as to establish realistic expectations. He diligently endeavors to achieve the best results for his clients, whether through amicable resolution or litigation.

As Michael's clients know, his passion is to make a positive impact on everyone who walks into his office. An avid researcher and learner, he is constantly learning and honing his skills to better serve families across Wisconsin. In the courtroom, he fiercely defends his clients to get the best possible results. He is a caring lawyer who makes every client a priority, building successful cases around their genuine concerns and long-term goals. His exceptional service, compassionate style, and positive results earned him multiple awards including a spot in Wisconsin Super Lawyers.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Baraboo, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Jay M. Englund of Englund & Associates Law Office LLC in Baraboo, Wisconsin

For nearly two decades, Attorney Jay M. Englund's devotion, commitment and advocacy for clients have made him stand out among central Wisconsin's legal professionals. Assertive, experienced and tenacious, Mr. Englund is the founder of Englund & Associates Law Office LLC located in Baraboo, Wisconsin. The law firm serves clients throughout the state with a focus on Sauk, Juneau, Columbia, Adams, Richland, Iowa, Monroe, Vernon and Marquette Counties.

Mr. Englund is a criminal defense attorney who has spent his career protecting people's constitutional rights. Through the decades, he has represented thousands of clients who have faced an assortment of criminal charges, including:

• Homicide

• Assault and battery

• Drug possession

• Domestic violence

• Embezzlement

• Drunk driving

A skilled litigator and advocate, Mr. Englund leverages his experience and vast legal knowledge to gain favorable outcomes for clients. His record of acquittals, dismissals, favorable settlements and plea bargains has created a reputation of excellence.

Mr. Englund has long been recognized for his outstanding work inside and outside the courtroom. His legal peers have honored him for being one of central Wisconsin's top criminal defense attorneys. Mr. Englund was chosen for the region's Super Lawyers Rising Stars list and one of the Top 100 Trial Lawyers in Wisconsin.

His experience in law began in 2000 as an undergraduate, when he served as an intern for the Eau Claire County Public Defender's Office. While in law school, he worked for the Waukesha District Attorney's Office. He began his career as an attorney in 2004 soon after earning his law degree from Marquette University Law School in Milwaukee, joining the law firm Curran, Hollenbeck & Orton S.C. in Mauston, Wisconsin.

In 2011, Mr. Englund became a co-founder of Pemberton & Englund Law Office LLC. The law firm split in 2022, and Englund & Associates Law Office was born.

Mr. Englund is licensed to practice law in Wisconsin as well as the U.S. District Court for the Eastern and Western Districts of Wisconsin.

attorneys.bio:
Attorney Jeremy Evans earned his undergraduate degree in Philosophy from the University of Wisconsin. He then attended the University of Wisconsin Law School, where he earned his Juris Doctor in 2013. During law school, Attorney Evans interned at the Legal Assistance to Incarcerated Persons project and the Public Defender’s project.

Over the course of the past ten years, Attorney Evans has litigated hundreds of criminal and municipal cases ranging from ordinance violations to misdemeanor and felony matters. He also has years of research, document review, and consultation experience in a wide variety of other legal matters, including family, civil, estate planning, real estate, personal injury, copyright, trademark, landlord-tenant, consumer-finance, automobile-accident, insurance, bankruptcy, and collections.

As a criminal defense attorney, Jeremy Evans is fiercely committed to achieving exceptional results for his clients, whether by trial or negotiation. In addition to his jury trial experience, Attorney Evans has successfully negotiated for significant reductions in charges and penalties as well as outright dismissals.

Attorney Evans has a deep understanding of the emotional turmoil and uncertainty that come with navigating the complex and often intimidating landscape of criminal law. He is deeply committed to serving as a compassionate guide and unwavering ally through each stage of the legal process. With an aptitude for translating seemingly incomprehensible legal concepts and terminology into plain language, Attorney Evans empowers clients to make informed decisions, ensuring that they never feel marginalized, overwhelmed, or unheard.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Brookfield, WI
attorneys.bio:
Before coming to Grieve Law, attorney Lauren Evans started her career as an Assistant Wisconsin State Public Defender in Racine. Law school taught her the legal information, but here she learned people–real people, with real problems, facing a system that doesn’t always play fair. She is passionate about her work and understands that she is advocating for people who are often navigating the most difficult moments of their lives.

Attorney Evans is an Arizona native who graduated from Barrett the Honors College at Arizona State University with a bachelor’s degree in justice studies, with minors in both political science and music. She then received her Juris Doctor from Creighton University School of Law. While at Creighton Law, she was awarded membership to the Order of the Barristers, a national honorary organization that recognizes graduates who have demonstrated exceptional skill in oral advocacy, brief writing, and overall advocacy. She was also a law clerk for the prosecutor’s office for two years, gaining valuable litigation experience through trials, motions, and appeals.

Now Attorney Evans has litigated hundreds of criminal cases and has a proven track record of successfully negotiating reductions of charges and dismissals, as well as fine-only or time-served dispositions when necessary.

Grounded in her belief that everyone deserves a strong defense, Attorney Evans is committed to guiding her clients through each step of the legal process with care and confidence.

attorneys.name: Elizabeth C. Fahrlander
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Elizabeth C. Fahrlander specializes in creating personalized estate plans for individuals of all ages and families of all compositions. She passionately believes that everyone should be prepared for the unexpected.

Elizabeth found her calling after experiencing a brush with her own mortality in 2019 at the age of 35 when she was diagnosed with and underwent surgery to remove a brain tumor. At the time, she did not even have powers of attorney in place despite, as a lawyer, knowing that she should. Elizabeth had been working in banking, and when Covid hit the following year, she was struck by how many of her banking clients lacked advanced planning documents, and by how many of her contemporaries who worked as doctors, nurses, and teachers – traditionally not jobs considered “high risk” – were suddenly posting on social media looking for recommendations for estate planning. The clear need for this kind of legal service led Elizabeth to start her own small law practice, before joining Capital Law Group, S.C. in 2025.

After receiving her Bachelor’s Degree from the University of Iowa, with majors in Political Science and Philosophy, Elizabeth went on to attend The George Washington University Law School in Washington, DC. During law school, she was active in various clubs, including the Hispanic Law Student Association (HLSA), completed a summer fellowship with The Human Rights Campaign, and worked for a lobbying firm specializing environmental issues and the representation of nonprofits.

A Madison native, Elizabeth returned home after graduation to put down roots closer to family. In her free time, she enjoys cooking and baking, ballroom dancing, watching history documentaries, and attending temple. She lives in Madison with her husband, Brian, and their menagerie of pets.

attorneys.bio:
Nicholas E. Fairweather has represented labor unions, employees and small businesses for eleven years.

Mr. Fairweather grew up in Northeastern Wisconsin. He graduated from Lawrence University, in Appleton, and received his law degree from Case Western Reserve University School of Law in 2000. He was admitted to the State Bar of Wisconsin later that year. Mr. Fairweather was admitted to practice before the United States District Court for the Western District of Wisconsin in 2000 and the Eastern District of Wisconsin in 2003.

Mr. Fairweather's work spans several areas of law. He has represented individuals, labor unions and small businesses before the state and federal courts of Wisconsin and administrative agencies throughout the state. Mr. Fairweather has represented Wisconsin consumers in debt collection harassment, misrepresentation and housing lawsuits. His labor and employment practice focuses in the areas of employment discrimination, contracts, professional licensure, and public employee and public-sector union litigation.

Mr. Fairweather currently serves on the Board of Directors of the State Bar of Wisconsin's Solo & Small Firm/General Practice Section. He volunteers his time with the Dane County Bar Association's Small Claims Assistance Program and the Wisconsin Lawyers Assistance Program. He served on the Board of Directors of the Tenant Resource Center in 2009.

Mr. Fairweather has been selected for inclusion on the list of Rising Stars in the 2008, 2009, 2010 and 2011 editions of Milwaukee Magazine and Law & Politics Magazine.

Mr. Fairweather focuses his practice in labor, employment and consumer litigation.

attorneys.name: David Ferguson
attorneys.practice_type: Employment law Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney David Ferguson has a passion for labor and employment law. He represents Unions and employees in organizing, negotiating, mediating, arbitrating, litigating, and providing education in Stewards' Schools. He also represents employees against retaliation for protected concerted activity, such as Union organizing, Union representation, and advocacy for safety and health, wages, hours, and working conditions. David represents employees in all other areas of employment law as well, such as wage theft and non-compete agreements. He also handles partnership and micro business matters.

David earned his Juris Doctorate with a concentration in Labor and Employment from the University of Wisconsin Law School. While in law school he externed the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) where he was responsible for analyzing and drafting final investigative reports and briefs related to unfair labor practices. His responsibilities also included recommending cases for deferral and Non-Board settlements based on General Counsel guidance. His direct advocacy for workers has included everything from claiming tax credits for low-income meatpackers to negotiating settlements for migrant beekeepers.

As a law student, David also gained practical experience through the Unemployment Appeals Clinic and served as a Managing Editor for the Wisconsin International Law Journal. He also externed at Legal Action Wisconsin, where he conducted legal research, prepared tax returns for migrant laborers, victims of financial crimes, and refugees, and helped develop a standardized reference manual on tax concerns for settlements, negotiations, and appeals with the IRS.

Attorney Ferguson's legal experience also extends to the judicial branch. He previously interned for Judge Blanchard of the Wisconsin Court of Appeals, where he researched United States and Wisconsin State Constitutional law for appellate opinions. Additionally, he has served as a trial clerk for the United States Tax Court Article I and Special Trial Judges, assisting them in hearing cases during trial sessions around the country.

David grew up in Southeast Michigan, where he was on his high school swim team and developed a love of contemporary American fiction. David served in the Navy at Pearl Harbor and achieved the rank of Petty Officer Second Class. As an undergraduate, he attended Wayne State University and interned for the Wayne County Prosecutor’s Office.

attorneys.name: Nicole Ferch
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Born and raised in Cudahy, Wisconsin, Nicole Ferch is deeply proud to serve as an advocate for the community that shaped her. As a personal injury attorney, Nicole is passionate about supporting individuals during their most vulnerable times. Building genuine, trusting relationships with her clients is at the core of her practice, and her priority is ensuring they receive the care and attention they deserve. Motivated by her unwavering passion for justice and strong community ties, Nicole is dedicated to making a meaningful impact on the lives of her clients.

Nicole has devoted her entire legal career to personal injury law, representing individuals across Wisconsin with care and commitment. She approaches each case with empathy, determination, and a profound sense of responsibility to those she serves, always striving to achieve the best possible outcomes for her clients.

Outside of her legal practice, Nicole enjoys walking her blind rescue dachshund, Happy, through Milwaukee’s neighborhoods, grabbing coffee at local spots, and attending community events.

If you or a loved one has been injured and need trusted legal representation, contact Nicole today for a consultation. She’s here to help guide you through your legal journey with the care and dedication you deserve.

attorneys.name: Roy N. Fine
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Appleton, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Roy Fine's legal practice emphasizes business transactions, real estate, finance, estate planning, probate, mergers and acquisitions, and intellectual property. Fine has helped guide numerous start-up businesses and medium-sized companies to the next level through sound business planning, trademarks and copyright, contract negotiations and drafting, buy-sell agreements, employment issues, and real estate matters. He has also worked with mature companies and family businesses to successfully transition to the next generation or to new ownership through proactive business succession practices and mergers, and he has facilitated the resolution of numerous shareholder disputes.

Fine, who is a shareholder at Murphy Desmond and rated AV (top rating) by Martindale-Hubbell, has helped couples and individuals prepare uniquely crafted wills and trusts that effectively transfer legacies and belongings to their heirs, with special attention to tax implications. He is able to assist with prenuptial and postnuptial agreements, charitable gifting, special needs trusts, real estate and property matters, fiduciary disputes and other probate matters.

In addition to over 35 years of assisting business and estate planning clients, Fine has been active in business organizations throughout the Fox Cities, as well as with organizations related to his personal interests and talents. He is active with the Multiple Sclerosis Society-Wisconsin Chapter, has been a musician with the Fox Valley Symphony since 1986, and he frequently participates in 5K charity runs.

Fine serves clients in the firm's Appleton and Madison offices.

attorneys.name: Mary Flanner
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Contracts Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Mary Flanner advises clients in matters involving employee and employer relations. She assists clients in evaluating, negotiating and litigating, if needed, matters involving severance agreements, non-competes and other employment related torts, restrictive covenants and employment contracts. She helps clients obtain compensation due for unpaid or underpaid wages, overtime, commissions, bonuses, benefits, deferred compensation and stock. She also represents individuals in claims under ERISA plans and employment contracts and represents clients in matters involving wrongful discharge, including retaliatory terminations, licensure proceedings and regulatory matters. She advises employees about their rights and their employer's obligations including in matters involving discrimination or the need for accommodations of a disability or leave under the FMLA.

Her clients include a broad range of people, from workers earning minimum wage to highly paid professionals.

She also represents individuals in cases brought under the False Claims Act for fraudulent billings presented to the government and other fraud claims and whistleblower claims.

She resolves disputes with various settlement mechanisms including direct negotiation, arbitration and mediation to achieve desired goals. If settlement cannot be achieved, she presents the case through the appropriate administrative process such as the Wisconsin Equal Rights Division (ERD) or the federal Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) or the courts through trial if needed.

She also advises business start-ups and represents small businesses on transactional matters, including collection, contract disputes and commercial litigation.

Mary has represented clients for the Cross Law Firm since 2013. She is a native Wisconsinite. In her free time, she participates in a book club and especially enjoys reading historical fiction, mysteries and well written books. She enjoys hiking, traveling and spending time with her family.

attorneys.name: Elisabeth Fletcher
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce, Annulment, and Legal Separation Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Elisabeth enjoys family law because it gives her the chance to truly make a difference in people's lives. Elisabeth is a logical and facts-oriented person. This is especially helpful in family law, as legal proceedings involving one's family is an emotional time. The important details are sometimes lost in the moment if you do not have an advocate that is paying attention to the facts that will help win your case.

Elisabeth is professional and focused on results, both in the courtroom and when negotiating with the other side. She wants her clients to be happy and works very hard to assist them in achieving their desired outcome. Further, she strives to ensure that her clients understand the applicable statutory and case law as well as all their options, so that they can make informed decisions and work with her as a team throughout the course of their case. As a parent, Elisabeth understands how very important custody and placement matters are to her clients and can empathize with how they are feeling as their case progresses. In addition to the practice areas noted below, Elisabeth also accepts Guardian ad Litem and Parent Coordinator appointments.

Elisabeth graduated from the University of Wisconsin Law School in 2013. She worked for Holevoet & Hanna until December 2016. From December 2016 until April 2019, she was employed by Cordell & Cordell. She joined Musial & Fletcher, S.C. in April of 2019, and as of January 2023, she became a partner and the firm's name was changed to Friedrich & Fletcher, S.C.

Elisabeth believes that it is important to give back to her community, and volunteers monthly for the Free Family Law Clinic at the Vera Court Neighborhood Center in Madison. The monthly clinic, which takes place on the second Thursday of each month, serves low-income individuals, providing a valuable service for people that need assistance but can't otherwise afford to hire an attorney. This year, Vera Court Neighborhood Association received the Community Partner Award for their administration and support of a legal clinic staffed by volunteer Attorneys, including Elisabeth. The State Bar of Wisconsin did a feature on her pro bono work in June of 2020, which can be reviewed at https://www.wisbar.org/NewsPublications/Pages/General-Article.aspx?ArticleID=27771.

When she is not working, Elisabeth enjoys spinning, gardening, reading, tending to her flock of chickens, and watching the Packers while sampling craft beers with her sister. She has been known to raise the random orphan squirrel or pick up a stray cat (or two) from the side of the road and is doing an excellent job of teaching her son that life is better with more animals in it.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Elisabeth enjoys family law because it gives her the chance to truly make a difference in people's lives. Elisabeth is a logical and facts-oriented person. This is especially helpful in family law, as legal proceedings involving one's family is an emotional time. The important details are sometimes lost in the moment if you do not have an advocate that is paying attention to the facts that will help win your case.

Elisabeth is professional and focused on results, both in the courtroom and when negotiating with the other side. She wants her clients to be happy and works very hard to assist them in achieving their desired outcome. Further, she strives to ensure that her clients understand the applicable statutory and case law as well as all their options, so that they can make informed decisions and work with her as a team throughout the course of their case. As a parent, Elisabeth understands how very important custody and placement matters are to her clients and can empathize with how they are feeling as their case progresses. In addition to the practice areas noted below, Elisabeth also accepts Guardian ad Litem and Parent Coordinator appointments.

Elisabeth graduated from the University of Wisconsin Law School in 2013. She worked for Holevoet & Hanna until December 2016. From December 2016 until April 2019, she was employed by Cordell & Cordell. She joined Musial & Fletcher, S.C. in April of 2019, and as of January 2023, she became a partner and the firm's name was changed to Friedrich & Fletcher, S.C.

Elisabeth believes that it is important to give back to her community, and volunteers monthly for the Free Family Law Clinic at the Vera Court Neighborhood Center in Madison. The monthly clinic, which takes place on the second Thursday of each month, serves low-income individuals, providing a valuable service for people that need assistance but can't otherwise afford to hire an attorney. This year, Vera Court Neighborhood Association received the Community Partner Award for their administration and support of a legal clinic staffed by volunteer Attorneys, including Elisabeth. The State Bar of Wisconsin did a feature on her pro bono work in June of 2020, which can be reviewed at https://www.wisbar.org/NewsPublications/Pages/General-Article.aspx?ArticleID=27771.

When she is not working, Elisabeth enjoys spinning, gardening, reading, tending to her flock of chickens, and watching the Packers while sampling craft beers with her sister. She has been known to raise the random orphan squirrel or pick up a stray cat (or two) from the side of the road and is doing an excellent job of teaching her son that life is better with more animals in it.

attorneys.name: Matthew J. Frank
attorneys.practice_type: Environmental Law, Renewable Energy & Sustainability Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Matt Frank's practice focuses on environmental, energy, and natural resources law. He provides experienced counsel to businesses, start-ups, municipalities, utilities, organizations and individuals in a wide range of environmental and energy matters, helping clients successfully navigate regulatory and legal challenges. In addition, Frank assists clients in achieving their goals in areas such as renewable energy development, energy efficiency, green building, natural resource protection and sustainability.

Frank is a former Secretary of the Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources (DNR) and Assistant Attorney General with the Wisconsin Department of Justice (DOJ). During his tenure as DNR Secretary from 2007 through 2010, he oversaw the DNR's regulatory and permitting programs, including air and water quality, waste and recycling, wetlands, groundwater, environmental clean-ups and brownfields restoration. Frank worked closely with businesses and communities on sustainability initiatives such as the Green Tier program and the Green Tier Legacy Communities Charter. He also worked closely on environmental and natural resource issues with officials in the Environmental Protection Agency, other federal agencies, states across the country, and Wisconsin tribal and local governments.

Frank's environmental achievements at the DNR include the start of full-scale clean-up of PCB's in the Fox River, passage of the Great Lakes Compact, initiatives to reduce mercury emissions from coal-fired power plants by 90% and reducing phosphorous in Wisconsin's lakes and streams. He also created a new DNR partnership with the University of Wisconsin to research and understand the future impacts of climate change on Wisconsin's environment and economy, including business, agriculture, tourism, and urban and rural communities.

Prior to serving as DNR Secretary, Frank served for 22 years as an Assistant Attorney General at the Wisconsin Department of Justice (DOJ). An accomplished prosecutor and litigator, his tenure at DOJ included serving as the Director of the Criminal Litigation, Antitrust and Consumer Protection Unit. During his last six years at DOJ, he led the Legal Services Division, the largest public law firm in the state, providing legal representation to state agencies, the legislature and the Governor. Frank also served for four years as Secretary of the Department of Corrections, the largest agency in state government.

Clients value Frank's unique blend of experience as a lawyer and executive in the public sector. He combines strong advocacy and litigation skills, an understanding of local, state and federal governments, and extensive pragmatic and problem-solving experience to help clients achieve their goals.

attorneys.name: Mark A Frankel
attorneys.practice_type: Arbitration and Mediation Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Mark A. Frankel is an acclaimed mediator/arbitrator whose knowledge, experience, skill, and track record of success have garnered state and national recognition including:

Best Lawyers in America in ADR, 2006 - 2011, 2025

1st Annual Distinguished Service Award, ADR Section, State Bar of Wisconsin

Selected for listing by the American Arbitration Association (AAA) Panel of Arbitrators and Mediators, National Arbitration Forum, and CPR Institute, among others.

President of Wisconsin Association of Reserve Judges

Board of Directors of Group Health Cooperation – HMO

Mark has been practicing law since 1973, when he received his J.D. from the UW Law School. After working for U.S. District Judge James E. Doyle, he helped to establish the Madison law firm of Frankel, Langhammer & Pines. In 1979, he was elected to the Dane County Circuit Court, becoming one of the youngest judges in Wisconsin history. Mark currently serves as a Wisconsin Reserve Judge.

During his 20 years on the bench, Mark pioneered the use of mediation in the courtroom. He earned a reputation as a judge who not only adjudicated cases, but also afforded litigants an opportunity to resolve their disputes in an informal yet binding manner. He was invited to join the faculty of the Wisconsin Judicial College, where he taught judges across the state about how, when, and why to use mediation in court proceedings, and became an Assistant Dean of the Judicial College. He also authored and edited the Wisconsin Benchbook, a desktop reference guide for judges. As his reputation as a judicial educator grew, Mark was asked to join the faculty of the National Judicial College in Reno, Nevada, where he taught advanced evidence to judges from around the country for a number of years.

In 1999, Mark left the bench to become vice president, general counsel, and secretary to Madison Gas & Electric Co. In 2001, he became a partner with the law firm of Godfrey & Kahn S.C., where he built a successful ADR practice. With the benefit of both large and small law firm practice, corporate law practice, and 20 years of judicial experience, he established Frankel ADR in 2007.

A prolific writer, Mark has authored numerous articles in professional and law journals. He recently was selected to author the State Bar ADR Section's amicus brief in Borst v. Allstate Insurance Co. (2006 WI 70, 291 Wis. 2d 361, 717 N.W.2d 42), a case that gave the Wisconsin Supreme Court an opportunity to clarify several ill-defined aspects of the tripartite arbitration process. In its unanimous opinion, the Court adopted much of the reasoning presented in the amicus brief, providing clarity to lawyers, litigants, and arbitrators about the rules that govern arbitration in Wisconsin.

attorneys.name: Lisa Friedrich
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce, Annulment, and Legal Separation Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Lisa Friedrich believes that family relationships can and should continue to grow and be protected in whatever new form the family takes after a break-up. Providing these services to clients, educating them in the process and doing so in a compassionate, cost-effective manner is at the forefront of her work. Lisa focuses her practice on family law, including mediation, custody litigation, and divorce and paternity actions. She also assists clients in non-traditional family issues, premarital agreements, wills, health care powers of attorney and residential real estate transactions. Lisa has extensive experience as a mediator of family disputes and is a trained practitioner of collaborative family law, but she is also an effective litigator. She has taught lawyers at continuing legal education courses for the State Bar of Wisconsin and lawyers-to-be at the UW Law School. Lisa joined the firm in 1988, after working for one year as a law clerk for then Dane County Circuit Court Judge Moria Krueger. She became a partner in 1992.

attorneys.name: Amy Fry
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Amy Fry-Galow has been practicing law since 2003. She has been admitted to practice in three states and has worked in a variety of litigation areas over her career, including family law, elder law, employment law, and general practice. In her two decades of practice, Amy’s range of experience includes handling all phases of civil litigation in state and federal courts, working as an attorney-editor for several legal treatises, providing legal support for business consultants and serving as an adjunct professor at Carroll University. Since 2019, Amy has narrowed her practice so that she can focus exclusively on divorce and family law cases in Wisconsin state courts. In doing so, she has found that her breadth of legal experience is ideal for serving family law clients, who often have financial and business issues that are a part of their divorce and family law cases.

As an associate at Nelson, Krueger & Millenbach, LLC, Amy represents clients in all areas of family law including divorce, paternity, child support, maintenance, post judgment matters, and legal separation.

Amy is a passionate advocate who strives for the best possible outcomes for her clients and their families. Amy employs a cooperative approach and believes that educating her clients about their legal rights is the best way to help achieve resolution without resorting to trial. Her focus on education helps clients make choices more confidently and saves time, money, and tears. Where an amicable resolution cannot be reached, Amy is also a tough and experienced litigator. Amy is a strong advocate and will use her experience to fight for her clients.

attorneys.name: Erik L. Fuehrer
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Neenah, WI
attorneys.bio:
Erik L. Fuehrer has spent his career in the field of civil litigation. This includes all facets, from preparing a case for trial, the trial, and appeals. He has litigated cases involving insurance claims, personal injury, business matters, property damage, interpretation of insurance policies, insurance claim denials, issues related to residential and commercial construction, easements, trespass, and landlord/tenant matters.

Erik is a native of Minneapolis, Minnesota. He graduated from the University of St. Thomas, summa cum laude, with a B.A. in Russian, and minors in philosophy and history. He attended the University of Wisconsin Law School where he graduated with a J.D. in 2008.

Erik most enjoys the thorough research and writing associated with appeals and is often brought into cases by other lawyers needing assistance on a case at the appeal stage. He has worked on over 20 appeals before the Wisconsin Court of Appeals and the Wisconsin Supreme Court. Erik serves on the Amicus Committee for the Wisconsin Defense Counsel.

Erik is a member of the State Bar of Wisconsin, the Outagamie County Bar Association, the Wisconsin Defense Counsel, DRI, and the Western and Eastern Federal District Courts of Wisconsin, and the 7th Circuit Court of Appeals. He has authored articles for the WDC Journal and Behind the Bar.

Erik maintains an interest in Russian history and literature, world history, philosophy, art and fiction from the 1890’s – 1930’s, movies, football and road biking. He enjoys watching a Wisconsin Timber Rattler game on a warm summer day. Most of all, Erik enjoys spending time with his children.

attorneys.name: Steven C. Gabert
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury -- Plaintiff Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Steven C. Gabert is a graduate of Marquette University (B.A. 1983) and West Virginia School of Law (J.D. 1986). He is admitted to the West Virginia Bar and Wisconsin State Bar. He was commissioned as an officer in the United States Marine Corps in 1983. Following law school he served to the rank of Captain in the United States Marine Corps where he practiced as a Judge Advocate General (JAG) officer. After TBS at Quantico, VA he attended Naval Justice School (1987-Honors) in Newport, RI. He then continued his military service at Camp LeJeune, NC where his practice was primarily the representation of Marines and Sailors facing Special and General Courts Martial and pre-deployment legal services for Marines. Since completing his active military service in 1990, he has concentrated his practice on representing the personally injured. He practiced as a trial attorney for 10 years as an associate at Kondos Law Offices in Milwaukee, WI until he co-founded Action Law Offices, S.C. with Attorney Michael D. Leffler in the Fall of 1999.

Attorney Gabert is a member of the American Association for Justice, Wisconsin Association for Justice and the West Virginia and Wisconsin Bar Associations. He has been admitted to practice law in the United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit, United States Eastern and Western District Courts of the State of Wisconsin and all other courts in the State of Wisconsin. He is also a member of the American Legion.

attorneys.name: Martin P. Gagne
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
For more than 35 years, Marty Gagne practiced Family Law exclusively, including complex financial and custody cases. His experience included dealing with the valuation of closely-held businesses, stock options, executive compensation, employee benefits, trusts and gifted and inherited property. He represented parents in local, interstate and international child custody disputes. As a family law attorney, he offered cooperative divorce and collaborative divorce as well as traditional divorce (with or without litigation). Mr. Gagne also mediated dozens of Family Law cases since 1990. He practiced throughout southeastern Wisconsin, including Milwaukee, Waukesha, Ozaukee, Washington, Sheboygan, Racine and Manitowoc Counties.

Mr. Gagne was selected a Wisconsin Super Lawyer in the area of Family Law every year from 2005 to 2019; that publication selected him as one of the Top 50 Lawyers in Wisconsin and one of the Top 25 Lawyers in Milwaukee in 2018. He was AV rated by Martindale-Hubbell and was listed in that publication's Bar Register of Preeminent Lawyers from 2005 to 2019. He was also named in The Best Lawyers in America every year from 2008-2019; he was selected as Best Lawyers in America 2018 Lawyer of the Year in the Area of Family Law in Milwaukee. He presented at seminars and classes to judges, court commissioners, attorneys, law students, mental health professionals, and community members on various Family Law issues.

Mr. Gagne was a Court Commissioner and former member of the State Bar of Wisconsin Board of Governors. He was formerly Chairperson of the Board of Directors of the Family Law Section of the Milwaukee Bar Association, a former member of the Board of Directors of the Divorce Cooperation Institute, Inc., and was a member of the Leander J. Foley Matrimonial Inns of Court, Milwaukee Bar Association and the State Bar of Wisconsin Family Law Section.

Mr. Gagne is a 1978 graduate of Clark University and a 1981 cum laude graduate of Boston University Law School.

attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices of Benske, Gatzke, McFadden and Rose
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in New Berlin, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney John Gatzke specializes in Personal Injury and Worker’s Compensation Law and Litigation. Gatzke has been chosen for the Wisconsin Super Lawyers Rising Stars list on eight occasions, including seven consecutive years (2018-2024). Only 2.5% of attorneys in Wisconsin receive this distinction.

Gatzke has litigated personal injury and work comp cases in nearly every county in the State of Wisconsin and has handled federal tort claim matters in the Eastern District of Wisconsin. He has won numerous cases against large insurance companies in matters ranging from motor vehicle accidents and worker injuries to complex business litigation.

Attorney Gatzke, whose immediate family includes physicians and physician’s assistants, has an intimate understanding of medical issues and terminology, which serves him well in dealing with accident and work-related injuries and treatment. In jury trials, John has shown a unique ability to reduce technical medical data to a level which is understandable to a juror, and his history of significant awards in jury trials and hearings is a testament to his courtroom presence.

Attorney Gatzke rounds out his practice representing individuals in social security claims and in probate work.

John currently lives in Brookfield with his wife and their three children. He has undergraduate degrees from the University of Wisconsin-Stevens Point and received his law degree from Marquette University (cum laude), where he finished near the top of his graduating class. John received the Dean’s Honor Rating during his undergraduate years at UW and was an Honor student at Marquette Law. He received the CALI Excellence Award as the top ranked student in Negotiable Instruments and also in Law and PC. He has been a member of the Waukesha County Bar Association, the State Bar of Wisconsin, the Wisconsin Academy of Trial Lawyers and the American Trial Lawyers Association. He continues to be active in several Brookfield and New Berlin organizations and regularly volunteers his time on behalf of children and youth sports.

attorneys.name: Mark A. Gauthier
attorneys.practice_type: Debtor's Rights Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Mark is skilled and experienced in all options available to help eliminate your debt or save your home or vehicle. While bankruptcy might be the best option for some, Mark will analyze your individual situation and tailor a plan to effectively resolve your debt issues with the least amount of stress. Mark has experience in bankruptcy, debt negotiation, foreclosure defense, loan modifications, and Wisconsin Chapter 128. Additionally, Mark's previous family law experience enables him to guide clients through the unique challenges related to handling debt in pre-petition and post-petition divorce situations.

As the son of a service member, Mark spent his youth moving from one military base to the next. Mark has previously called Arizona, Guam, Oklahoma, Ohio, and Michigan home. In 1999, Mark and his wife finally decided to plant roots in Milwaukee and have made Wisconsin their home ever since. When not spending time with his Wife and 3 young children, Mark enjoys fishing the great rivers and lakes of Wisconsin and well as cheering on his Denver Broncos!

attorneys.name: Amanda K. Gennerman
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Amanda K. Gennerman has been practicing immigration law exclusively since 2004. Prior to joining Pines Bach, LLP she was the founder of Gennerman Law Group located in Madison, Wisconsin (2004-2020).

Amanda's practice focuses on multiple areas of immigration law, including family-based petitions (adjustment of status applications and consular processing and removal of conditions); humanitarian petitions (VAWA Self-Petitions and U Non Immigrant Visas Petitions, Asylum applications, TPS and DACA); Naturalization applications and Removal Defense. She advises on the immigration consequences of criminal convictions.

Amanda represents clients before USCIS Field Offices and the EOIR/Immigration Courts and BIA. She has litigated immigration matters in both the Western and Eastern District of Wisconsin. She is a licensed to practice in the 7th Circuit Court of Appeals.

Amanda is not only dedicated to her practice but is committed to supporting immigrant communities. She is a cofounder, board member and volunteer of the Community Immigration Law Center (CILC) in Madison. She trains volunteers for CILC's bi-weekly "walk-in" legal clinic. She has presented on immigration topics to community organizations through-out Wisconsin, local middle/high schools, the University of Wisconsin (Madison and Eau Claire), Waukesha County Technical College and the Wisconsin State Bar. She has been a mentor to several Department of Justice Board Accredited Representatives, and she has mentored in the Dane County Bar Mentorship program.

Her work has been published in the Immigrant Legal Resource Center, "U Visa Manual." She was voted a Rising Star Attorney of Wisconsin in 2006, 2008, 2009 and was awarded the Dane County Pro Bono Award for Legal Services in 2010. She is a member of several immigration professional organizations including National Immigration Project/National Lawyers Guild, ASISTA and American Immigration Lawyers Association (AILA) and the American Constitution Society (ACS).

On a personal note, Amanda is the mother of two boys. She enjoys her yoga practice, hiking and biking with the boys. She always makes time for March Madness.

attorneys.name: Michael S. Georg
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Law Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
My name is Attorney Michael Georg, and I have successfully represented thousands of people through the bankruptcy process since 1997. I have filed Chapter 7 and Chapter 13 bankruptcy petitions for people throughout the State of Wisconsin. I have helped homeowners save their homes from foreclosure, saved consumers' cars from repossession, and protected their wages from garnishment.

I grew up in Fond du Lac, WI and earned my B.A. from the University of Wisconsin at Madison and I earned my law degree from DePaul University College of Law. While studying law, I clerked for the Cook County Public Defender's Office. I also worked for a law firm that helped people obtain social security disability benefits. This experience sparked in me a desire to use my education to help people deal with life's problems they simply cannot control. It is my job to help you deal with crushing medical debt, overwhelming credit card late fees, and the payday loans that were supposed to get you out of a pinch, but are now squeezing your family's budget.

With a Juris Doctor and MBA from Marquette University, Liam brings a unique blend of legal expertise and business strategy our practice at Murphy Desmond S.C. Outside of his professional life, Liam enjoys exploring new cooking recipes and the natural beauty of Madison, especially kayaking on Lake Monona in the summer. During the colder months, he enjoys discovering new coffee shops and restaurants in the area.

attorneys.name: Steven B. Goff
attorneys.practice_type: Plaintiff's Personal Injury Lawyers in River Falls, WI
attorneys.bio:
“I assure my clients from the outset that their case is very important to me, and that they will receive my very best efforts. Additionally, I assure them that I will always be available to answer their questions and that their case will receive the attention it deserves.”

As an experienced personal injury trial lawyer, Steven Goff stresses the word “personal” the most. With his practice focused entirely on plaintiffs’ personal injury, he enjoys developing professional relationships with his clients and really getting to know them. “You can’t do the best job for your client unless you talk to them, get to know them, and fully appreciate how the accident and injuries have affected their lives, and those close to them,” stresses Steve. Steve takes immense pride in standing up for the “little guy” against big companies. When you work with Steve, you can take the weight of the world off your shoulders and try to focus your entire attention on receiving medical treatment and recovering as best you can from your injuries. Steve will make sure you are treated fairly and will fight to get you the settlement you deserve or take your case to trial.

Steve graduated from Iowa State University with honors in 1976. He was a member of the scholastic fraternities of Phi Beta Kappa and Phi Kappa Phi. He moved from Ames, Iowa to Minneapolis, Minnesota in 1976, where he pursued his law degree from the University of Minnesota. He graduated from the University of Minnesota Law School in 1979 and immediately became a member of the Bar in both Wisconsin and Minnesota that same year. Steve was also admitted to practice in the federal courts of those states and in the Supreme Court of the United States.

In 1979, Steve moved from Minnesota to River Falls, Wisconsin, where he has spent the ensuing 44 years practicing in the small town he loves. “I would never have moved too far from the Twin Cities metropolitan area, but River Falls offers the perfect complement of a wonderful small town and outdoor life, and with the Twin Cities so close, the amenities only those cities can offer.” Steve has been very active in the River Falls community, where he served as City Attorney for the first 20 years of his practice, and has been a member of numerous civic organizations such as Kiwanis and Rotary. He has also been active on several conservation groups for the protection of the Kinnickinnic River, a Class A trout stream, which runs through the city of River Falls.

Steve is an avid fisherman and enjoys annual trips to Canada, local trout fishing, and spending time with his friends and family at his cabin in northern Wisconsin. I have gotten some of my best fishing tips and fishing spots from my clients, and it is always a fertile area of discussion, says Steve. “I love the people of western Wisconsin, and I knew this was going to be home from the first day I came here.”

attorneys.name: Lisa C. Goldman
attorneys.practice_type: Appeals Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Lisa C. Goldman provides legal services to clients in a number of fields, such as criminal defense, civil litigation, and election recounts. She also has experience litigating issues pertaining to health insurance and pension benefits under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA).

Lisa has a commanding presence, as seen by her successful track record in both trials and appeals. She has been successful in getting her clients off on all criminal charges, from felonies to misdemeanors to traffic violations. She won a verdict in civil court that exceeded $400,000. She has also settled many personal injury matters, some for more than a million dollars. She successfully used a recount method to overturn the results of a Wisconsin election in the state's northern region. In a first for Wisconsin, she successfully represented the Democratic Party in circuit court to get voting hours extended at a polling place that had been temporarily closed. She assisted Senator Clinton's campaign for president. At the 2008 Democratic National Convention in Denver, she was appointed to serve on the Rules Committee.

For six years, Lisa was an active member of the State Bar of Wisconsin's Professional Ethics Committee. She is also frequently appointed by the Wisconsin Supreme Court to act as a referee in attorney discipline matters. She also belongs to the American Bar Association, the Dane County Bar Association, the Wisconsin Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, and the Inns of Court.

Lisa interned for Representative Spencer Coggs of the Wisconsin State Assembly during her college years at the University of Wisconsin, and she also spent a summer working for the United Nations. Later, she was a reporter for Al-Fajr based out of East Jerusalem, Israel. She joined the Peace Corps after completing her degree in political science, and she worked as an Agricultural Extension Officer and Small Business Development Officer in Lesotho, Africa.

Lisa clerked at the Wisconsin Department of Justice and was a student attorney in the Legal Defense Program, a semi-finalist in the Heffernan Oral Advocacy Competition, a quarter-finalist in the Rendigs National Products Liability Moot Court Competition, and a new mom all while attending law school.
