attorneys.name: Jason Goldstein
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in La Crosse, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Jason Goldstein is a trial attorney whose practice focuses primarily on family law, civil litigation, business/employment, and criminal law.

Jason has significant experience in all phases of civil litigation, including business, collection and employment matters. He zealously advocates for his clients in all stages of each case in his multifaceted practice (from the drafting of initial pleadings through the negotiation/mediation stages and ultimately at trial, if deemed necessary).

The La Crosse Family Court Commissioner’s office has often asked Jason to educate individuals in the process of divorce in its Families First classes. Additionally, Jason has served as guardian ad litem for children and as a court-appointed guardian ad litem and as adversary counsel in guardianship and protective placement proceedings involving adults.

Jason has litigated a multitude of cases involving family law matters such as divorce, paternity, child custody, physical placement, child support, maintenance (alimony), property division, prenuptial agreements, and a myriad of post-divorce related matters. His extensive knowledge and vast experience as a civil litigator also serve him well in representing his divorce clientele who are burdened with complex business, real/personal property, monetary and/or contractual entanglements. In short, Jason’s acquired skills via his comprehensive legal practice, along with his consistent work ethic, fastidious attention to detail, zealous advocacy, understanding and empathetic nature, and decades of experience in the “legal trenches” provide his divorce clients with that sought-after edge in obtaining a successful outcome in their respective cases.

As an essential component of his thorough and developed divorce practice, Jason has honed his expertise in dividing up retirement plans via Qualified Domestic Relations Order (QDRO) over his 20 years of family law practice. Jason drafts all of the QDRO’s for the family law attorneys at Bosshard Parke LTD. Further, Jason has been hired by other law firms in the La Crosse area to draft and/or review proposed QDRO’s pursuant to both pending and completed divorce cases.

Jason has represented Bosshard Parke clients, including juveniles, at all levels of the criminal justice process, including all types of misdemeanor and felony level offenses.

In his spare time (when he is not working or raising two teenage sons with his wife of 20 years), Jason volunteers as the chairperson for the Duke University Alumni Admissions Advisory Committee for the western region of Wisconsin; in this capacity over the past 15 years, Jason interviews high school students applying for admission to his beloved alma mater, and serves as a liaison/ambassador for Duke University with both prospective applicants as well as with public and private high schools throughout western Wisconsin.

Jason has been recognized in 2017 as an AV Preeminent® rated attorney by Martindale-Hubbell® Peer Review Ratings™, the gold standard in attorney ratings. AV Preeminent is the highest possible attorney rating by the prestigious Martindale Hubbell Law Directory, an achievement earned by less than 5% of attorneys nationwide. An AV Preeminent rating reflects the confidential opinions of bar members and the judiciary, and attests to both Jason’s outstanding legal ability and steadfast adherence to professional standards of ethics. This significant accomplishment is a testament to the fact that Jason has earned the respect of his peers/adversaries who rank Jason at the highest possible level of professional excellence.

attorneys.name: Colin B. Good
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Colin Good's practice focuses on representing clients in various areas of civil litigation. Specifically, Mr. Good represents clients in several areas, including claims for personal injury, wrongful discharge, harassment, discrimination, breach of employment contract, and violations of the Americans with Disabilities Act, and the Family and Medical Leave Act. Mr. Good has represented or assisted in the representation of numerous clients in local, state, and federal courts as well as administrative agencies.

Mr. Good received his undergraduate degree from Lawrence University with honors in 1997. He received a Masters of Letters in Theology from the University of St. Andrews, Scotland, in 1999. He graduated from the University of Montana School of Law in 2004, where he participated in National Moot Court. Mr. Good clerked for Justices Jim Regnier and Brian Morris of the Montana Supreme Court from 2004 to 2005 before beginning practice in Wisconsin.

Mr. Good currently serves on the Board of Directors for the State Bar of Wisconsin's Public Interest Law Section and is a member of the State Bar of Wisconsin and the Dane County Bar Association.

attorneys.name: David M. Gorwitz
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney David Gorwitz advises business clients in all phases of operations from business formation and business planning to succession planning, buy-sell agreements, and mergers and acquisitions.

Dave’s experience includes representing corporations, partnerships, and other business entities of all sizes in a wide range of business transactions. He assists in strategic business planning, contract drafting and negotiations, commercial leasing matters, and buying/selling commercial real estate. Dave serves as outside general counsel to numerous businesses, where he advises on day-to-day business legal matters as well as complex business transactions involving millions of dollars. Dave’s background in mergers and acquisitions is national in scope.

Recognized for his legal knowledge, Dave is included on lists for Best Lawyer® in America in Corporate Compliance Law, was named "Madison Lawyer of the Year" in Corporate Compliance Law in 2023, and he is a Fellow of the Wisconsin Law Foundation.

Dave's background also includes business ownership of an electronics import/wholesale company and a boat dealership. He served in the banking industry where he held insurance and securities licenses. Dave's experience as a business owner and in banking provide first-hand insight into the needs of his business clients, including necessary legal protections and business regulation compliance.

In addition to his legal practice, Dave is actively involved in the community through his many interests that include sailing competitions, the arts, music, UW Marching Band alumni events, and the Madison Elks Lodge 410.

Dave is available to assist his clients in Murphy Desmond’s Madison office and remotely.

attorneys.name: Stephen M. Govin
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Stephen M. Govin, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Stephen M. Govin formed the Law Office of Stephen M. Govin, LLC after practicing law with the law firm of Reddin, Singer & Govin for ten years. Stephen’s practice is dedicated exclusively to criminal defense in state and federal courts across Wisconsin. He decided to form the Law Office of Stephen M. Govin, LLC to provide clients with the highest level of legal services while being personally involved with every aspect of the client’s case from start to finish. Stephen has always been recognized for his personable and professional demeanor in court and has achieved extraordinary results for his clients for over a decade by aggressively defending his client’s rights.

Stephen was raised in Waukesha, Wisconsin by his parents Charles and Beatrice. The youngest of four boys, Stephen was raised in a very competitive environment which has served him well on the athletic fields and in the courts. Stephen was a highly decorated athlete, competing in both soccer and wrestling as a youth before attending Catholic Memorial High School (CMH) in Waukesha. While at CMH, Stephen earned eight varsity letters (four in soccer and four in wrestling) while competing on three separate state championships teams. In soccer at CMH Stephen was a prolific goal scorer, he was recognized as a first team all-conference player twice, the conference player of the year once, and as a senior was one of the most recruited players in the Midwest. In wrestling at CMH Stephen was tenacious, he was recognized as the wrestler of the year twice at CHM, was a four year state tournament place winner (freshman-4th, sophomore-3rd, junior-2nd, senior-1st), and as a senior was an undefeated state champion with a record of 30-0. Because of his accomplishments athletically at CMH, Stephen was voted the CMH male athlete of the year as a senior and was honored by the Waukesha Freeman newspaper as the Waukesha County male athlete of the year that same year. Following high school, Stephen accepted an athletic scholarship to attend Marquette University and played Division I soccer at Marquette while majoring in criminology and law studies. Athletically at Marquette, Stephen was a starting forward each year and helped Marquette reach its first ever NCAA Division I soccer tournament in 1997. As a senior, Stephen led Marquette in goals scored and total points. Stephen’s name still appears in the all-time record books for Marquette soccer in a number of categories.

Following his undergraduate graduation from Marquette, Stephen turned down playing professional soccer and decided to attend Marquette University Law School and pursue his passion for criminal law. He put himself through law school by bartending on the eastside of Milwaukee for three years and coaching numerous youth soccer teams in southeast Wisconsin including with Waukesha Spring City Soccer Club, Brookfield Soccer Club and four years as a head coach for the Wisconsin Olympic Development Program (as a player, Stephen was selected to play for the Olympic Development Program and competed for the Olympic Development Program at various national and international competitions). A number of the players Stephen coached went on to play Division I soccer in college and some even represented their county’s national teams at youth World Cups and other international matches. While at Marquette University Law School, Stephen focused on criminal law from his first day; unlike many law students who don’t know what area of the law they want to practice, Stephen knew going into law school he was going to be a criminal defense attorney. Because of his focus on criminal law from the beginning of law school, Stephen was able to tailor his experience at Marquette to take advantage of coursework that would prepare him for the criminal courts. He excelled in courses on evidence law, criminal procedure, federal criminal procedure, trial advocacy, the constitution and criminal investigation and many others. Stephen not only focused his coursework on criminal law but he applied for and received a number of clerkships while in law school that gave him real world legal experience even before graduating from law school. Stephen clerked for the Honorable Victor Manion in Milwaukee County Circuit Court, the Honorable Chief Judge of the Wisconsin Court of Appeals Richard Brown, and spent his last year of law school practicing law at the Milwaukee office of the State Public Defender. By the time Stephen graduated from Marquette University Law School he had more courtroom experience than many second or third year lawyers.

After being admitted to the bar, Stephen began working as a trial attorney at Reddin & Singer which would later become Reddin, Singer & Govin. From his first day of practice Stephen was solely responsible for his client’s files from start to finish and began trying cases in criminal courts throughout Wisconsin immediately. Because of Stephen’s unique background both athletically and academically, Stephen was quickly recognized as a formidable opponent in the criminal courts. For over a decade Stephen has aggressively defended his clients in cases involving a wide array of charges from misdemeanor offenses to the most serious felony offenses in both state and federal courts throughout Wisconsin. Stephen has won numerous acquittals for his clients at jury trials and has successfully argued for the suppression of evidence in his client’s cases on a regular basis. Stephen has built solid relationships within the Wisconsin legal community and is known for his quiet confidence and personable demeanor. Not every case requires litigation or is appropriate for litigation and Stephen has the experience to know what is best for each case; however, Stephen’s competitive nature is on full display while litigating trials and he has never shied away from a tough fight when that is what is required. Year after year Stephen has been named as a Super Lawyer by Milwaukee Magazine, recognizing him as a top criminal defense attorney in Wisconsin as voted on by other attorneys and judges.

Stephen is a member of various professional organizations and legal bodies. Stephen has lived in the Milwaukee and Waukesha County area since his first birthday and is deeply engrained in the southeastern Wisconsin community. Stephen is married and has one daughter and his family presently lives in Waukesha County. In his free time Stephen enjoys traveling the world with his family, music, playing soccer, surfing, and food and wine.

Stephen M.

Govin

A number of the players Stephen coached went on to play Division I soccer in college and some even represented their county’s national teams at youth World Cups and other international matches. While at Marquette University Law School, Stephen focused on criminal law from his first day; unlike many law students who don’t know what area of the law they want to practice, Stephen knew going into law school he was going to be a criminal defense attorney. Because of his focus on criminal law from the beginning of law school, Stephen was able to tailor his experience at Marquette to take advantage of coursework that would prepare him for the criminal courts. He excelled in courses on evidence law, criminal procedure, federal criminal procedure, trial advocacy, the constitution and criminal investigation and many others. Stephen not only focused his coursework on criminal law but he applied for and received a number of clerkships while in law school that gave him real world legal experience even before graduating from law school. Stephen clerked for the Honorable Victor Manion in Milwaukee County Circuit Court, the Honorable Chief Judge of the Wisconsin Court of Appeals Richard Brown, and spent his last year of law school practicing law at the Milwaukee office of the State Public Defender. By the time Stephen graduated from Marquette University Law School he had more courtroom experience than many second or third year lawyers.

After being admitted to the bar, Stephen began working as a trial attorney at Reddin & Singer which would later become Reddin, Singer & Govin. From his first day of practice Stephen was solely responsible for his client’s files from start to finish and began trying cases in criminal courts throughout Wisconsin immediately. Because of Stephen’s unique background both athletically and academically, Stephen was quickly recognized as a formidable opponent in the criminal courts. For over a decade Stephen has aggressively defended his clients in cases involving a wide array of charges from misdemeanor offenses to the most serious felony offenses in both state and federal courts throughout Wisconsin. Stephen has won numerous acquittals for his clients at jury trials and has successfully argued for the suppression of evidence in his client’s cases on a regular basis. Stephen has built solid relationships within the Wisconsin legal community and is known for his quiet confidence and personable demeanor. Not every case requires litigation or is appropriate for litigation and Stephen has the experience to know what is best for each case; however, Stephen’s competitive nature is on full display while litigating trials and he has never shied away from a tough fight when that is what is required. Year after year Stephen has been named as a Super Lawyer by Milwaukee Magazine, recognizing him as a top criminal defense attorney in Wisconsin as voted on by other attorneys and judges.

Stephen is a member of various professional organizations and legal bodies. Stephen has lived in the Milwaukee and Waukesha County area since his first birthday and is deeply engrained in the southeastern Wisconsin community. Stephen is married and has one daughter and his family presently lives in Waukesha County. In his free time Stephen enjoys traveling the world with his family, music, playing soccer, surfing, and food and wine.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Waukesha, WI
attorneys.bio:
ReAnna C. Grabow is a partner at D’Angelo & Grabow. She graduated form Marquette University Law School in 2005. She concentrates her practice on Family Law. She is experienced in divorce, child custody, child placement, child support, paternity and post-judgment matters. ReAnna also serves as a Guardian ad Litem in Waukesha County. She has served as a Guardian ad Litem in both pre and post-judgment divorce and paternity actions.

ReAnna is a strong proponent of alternative dispute resolution. She is a trained divorce mediator. She has received training at the University of Wisconsin, along with training through the Mediation Center in Waukesha County. ReAnna serves as a divorce mediator for unrepresented parties.

ReAnna's achievements in family law are frequently recognized by her peers. She has been selected to Super Lawyers from 2015 to 2023.

Attorney Grabow is a member of the State Bar of Wisconsin, the Waukesha County Bar, the Milwaukee County Bar, the Collaborative Family Law Council and the Justinian Society. ReAnna over the years has volunteered her time as a Board of Director for Safe Babies Healthy Families; as a volunteer attorney for the Waukesha County Court Self-Help Family Legal Clinic, as a volunteer mediator for the Waukesha County Mediation Center, and as a teen court Judge in the City of New Berlin.

From 2009 to 2014, ReAnna has been recognized as a "Rising Star" by Wisconsin Super Lawyers, as published in Milwaukee Magazine.

Attorney Grasswick’s legal experience over the last several years has ranged from family law to juvenile law to adoption law. This experience has proved invaluable in preparing her for any family-type case presented to her. She has successfully won motion hearings and trials for her clients.

Attorney Grasswick is passionate about the local communities in southeastern Wisconsin. She is ready and willing to fight for you during confusing and stressful times.

attorneys.name: Christina M. Green
attorneys.practice_type: Land Use, Zoning and Development Law Lawyers in Elkhorn, WI
attorneys.bio:
Christina is the newest attorney in the law firm of Sweet & Maier, S.C Christina practices primarily in the areas of business and commercial and residential real estate, law in both Wisconsin and Illinois.

Christina M. Green began her legal career in the Lansing, Michigan office of Dickinson Wright PLLC and then moved with Dickinson Wright to Chicago, IL. After leaving Dickinson Wright she practiced at Holleb & Coff and Vedder Price both in Chicago IL until she left Vedder Price to become one of the founding members of Stahl, Cowen Crowley & Addis, LLC. Most recently, Christina worked with Godfrey, Leibsle, Blackbourn & Howarth, S.C. in Elkhorn, WI.

Christina M. Green graduated from the University of Wisconsin-Whitewater in 1991 with a major in Business Administration and earned her Juris Doctorate from the University of Wisconsin Madison in 1995.

Christina began her legal career in the Lansing, Michigan office of Dickinson Wright PLLC and then moved with Dickinson Wright to Chicago. After leaving Dickinson Wright, she practiced at Holleb & Coff and Vedder Price, both based out of Chicago until she left Vedder Price to become one of the founding members of Stahl, Cowen Crowley & Addis, LLC. Before becoming President of Sweet & Maier, S.C., Christina worked with Godfrey, Leibsle, Blackbourn & Howarth, S.C. in Elkhorn, Wisconsin.

Christina is an experienced real estate attorney in a wide variety of real estate and business law matters. Christina focuses her practice in commercial and residential real estate, including zoning & land use, acquisitions & development, leasing and condominiums and in commercial and corporate finance, acting as lender’s and borrower’s counsel. She has represented financial institutions in middle market loans, including general commercial loans, asset-based loans, real estate acquisition loans and construction loans. Christina’s clientele includes residential and commercial real estate developers, real estate management companies, financial institutions and borrowers, and sellers and purchasers of real estate and businesses.

Christina’s large firm expertise and small-town practice combine nicely to provide quality legal services with a personal touch throughout Wisconsin and Illinois. Christina is a member of the State Bar of Michigan, Illinois, and Wisconsin.

In her free time, Christina enjoys horseback riding, boating, and spending time with her family.

Christina M. Green, may be reached at (262)723-5480 or emailed at cgreen@wisclaw.com.

attorneys.name: Tom Grieve
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Brookfield, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Tom Grieve founded Grieve Law, LLC in October of 2013, which now ranks among the largest and most award-winning criminal defense and drunk driving firms in Wisconsin. In 2019, Grieve Law added Divergent Family Law as a new wing to the firm to bring the same focus and proven aggressive strategies to represent clients in family law cases effectively. All of the attorneys at Grieve Law, 20 attorneys and growing across both criminal and family law, are proud and honored to be trusted by many thousands of the citizens of Wisconsin to represent them in extraordinarily difficult moments across the state.

Tom Grieve is recognized among the top Milwaukee lawyers. Recently named a top Wisconsin criminal defense attorney, Tom was inducted into the “Wisconsin Rising Star” category by Super Lawyers (a nationally acclaimed attorney rating organization). He was also chosen as a "Top 100 Trial Lawyers" in Wisconsin by the National Trial Lawyers Association. Tom was also chosen for the "Top Attorneys of Wisconsin" by both Milwaukee Magazine and Madison Magazine.

With an impressive record for dropping charges or reducing multiple felony charges to misdemeanor charges in Wisconsin, the esteemed accolades do not come as a surprise. Whether at trial or negotiating charges outside the courtroom, Tom has produced remarkable results for his clients.

Beyond the courtroom, Tom has been interviewed and appeared in numerous media outlets, ranging from the New York Times, CourtTV, Fox News, Reuters, Washington Post, National Public Radio, Milwaukee Journal-Sentinel, among many others. He is a frequent Continuing Legal Education course speaker to teach lawyers and judges in developments and the law, both in Wisconsin and nationally. Finally, Tom has also presented across the country, both online and in person, concerning the law and culture to the public.

In addition to speaking engagements, Tom has also contributed to the national conversation in writing on emerging legal topics and has been published in Conceal Carry Magazine and elsewhere on multiple occasions. He also edited the book and contributed legal input on various other publications, including the "Wisconsin Guide for Armed Citizens" on behalf of the National Association of Certified Firearm Instructors.

Tom graduated with a double major in Medieval European history and Theology from Marquette University and went on to earn his Juris Doctor from Marquette University Law School. Tom is a lifelong Wisconsin resident and graduated high school from University School of Milwaukee.

When not in the office, attorney Grieve enjoys spending time with his wife and kids, reading, and playing ice hockey.

attorneys.name: Stephannie Guzy
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Brookfield, WI
attorneys.bio:
With over a decade of experience handling Family Law cases, Stephannie has the knowledge to work creatively for her clients both inside and outside the courtroom. After graduating in 2004 from the School of Law at Loyola University Chicago, Stephannie began her career as a prosecutor with the Illinois Attorney General’s Office where she was a Medicaid Fraud prosecutor and cross designated as a Special Assistant United States Attorney. In 2008, she became a prosecutor with the State's Attorney’s Office. In 2010, she started her own practice. She trained as a Mediator, and has served as a Child Representative and Guardian ad Litem for children caught in their parent’s litigation. Stephannie shines in detail oriented financial matters, where parties have sophisticated finances involving retirement accounts, annuities, stock options, closely held corporations, royalties from music or book deals, and or workers' compensations settlements. In cases that require judicial intervention, including emergency motion hearings and trial, Attorney Guzy is able to zealously advocate for her clients.

Stephannie has a proven track record of achieving positive outcomes for her clients. In the majority of cases, Stephannie was able to help the parties maintain control over the outcome by working out an agreeable solution to allow her clients to heal and grow in their lives.

Stephannie and her Husband, have two awesome kids. You can find them sailing on Lake Mendota or riding horses in Sun Prairie.

attorneys.name: Scott R. Halloin
attorneys.practice_type: Construction Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Scott is a shareholder attorney and the founding attorney Halloin Law Group, S.C., licensed in both Wisconsin and Illinois. For more than two decades, Scott has focused his practice on complex construction, construction-related insolvency, and insurance litigation.

Scott is an experienced construction and real estate litigator in Wisconsin. He has logged thousands of hours handling construction, insurance, and real estate related hearings, trials and arbitrations, and has handled hundreds of motions and witness examinations in the field.

Scott was one of the first and is one of a select handful of lawyers in the Midwest to practice in a narrow subset of commercial and residential construction, insurance, and real estate litigation concerning toxigenic mold issues. He has handled mold-related cases extensively since the first significant cases were filed in the late 1990s. Since then, he has dramatically helped shaped the law governing such cases. Scott has become a regular speaker on toxigenic mold issues and related topics of insurance, construction contract, design, and code compliance at legal and construction industry seminars.

Scott also has handled a substantial number of construction-related insolvency issues, including foreclosure, bankruptcy, and receivership claims. In particular, he has developed significant experience with priority issues, frequently speaking on and suggesting changes to the governing law.

Irrespective of his extensive trial experience, Scott’s passion long has been legal writing. He strongly believes that a good lawyer should be able to effectively communicate complicated factual and legal matters in an easy-to-understand (and when possible, enjoyable) manner. If you ask Scott about what he is most proud in his professional career, he will respond that it is the large numbers of judges and lawyers who highly have commended Halloin Law Group, S.C.’s brief-writing abilities.

attorneys.name: Aaron N. Halstead
attorneys.practice_type: Labor Law Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Aaron Halstead is a Phi Beta Kappa graduate of the University of Iowa (B.A., with honors and high distinction, 1987) and of Brigham Young University Law School (J.D., with honors, 1990). Mr. Halstead's practice is focused on labor and employment litigation, as well as on worker's compensation, where he devotes a substantial portion of his practice to representing injured Spanish-speaking employees. He also has served as a private mediator and arbitrator to parties involved in employment-related litigation.

Mr. Halstead has been a Member of the Board of Directors for the State Bar of Wisconsin's Labor and Employment Section (1998-2005, 2007 to 2010), and served as the Board's Chairperson in 2003-2004. He has been listed in The Best Lawyers in America in the area of Labor and Employment Law each year since 2003, and in Worker's Compensation each year since 2009.

Mr. Halstead has represented employees and labor organizations before the Wisconsin Supreme Court, the Wisconsin Court of Appeals, the United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit, and the United States District Courts for the Western and Eastern Districts of Wisconsin, as well as before various state and federal administrative agencies.

Among the labor organizations Mr. Halstead represents, either as counsel or co-counsel, are District Council 40, AFSCME; American Federation of Teachers-Wisconsin; Ashwaubenon Public Safety Officers' Association; and Ashwaubenon Public Works Employees' Association.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Neenah, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney William J. Hammett is a founding member and partner with Hammett, Bellin & Oswald, LLC. Established in 1997, the law firm has offices in Neenah and Appleton, Wisconsin. Serving clients throughout the Fox Valley region and surrounding areas, Mr. Hammett represents the rights and interests of those who are going through a divorce or other serious family issue.

Attorney Hammett graduated from UW-Madison in 1986. He received his Juris Doctorate from Marquette University in 1989. Mr. Hammett is a member for the Winnebago County Bar Association and served as President in 1997-98. Mr. Hammett is licensed to practice in the State of Wisconsin and the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Wisconsin.

Widely regarded as one of the leading family law attorneys in his region, Mr. Hammett has achieved notable success counseling and guiding client through the divorce process assisting in reaching agreements and resolving their conflicts concerning custody, placement, support, spousal maintenance, the division of the marital estate, and other related matters. Approximately 80% of Mr. Hammett's practice consists of representing clients in divorce actions, paternity actions, adoptions, and termination of parental rights proceedings. The remaining 20% of his practice consists of mediating family law disputes to help parties come to terms in the most amicable and efficient manner possible. As noted, Mr. Hammett has significant experience with paternity actions, adoptions and termination of parental rights cases. In all cases, he treats his clients with the compassion and respect they deserve as he works to help increase their chances of obtaining the favorable outcomes they seek for themselves and their children.

Recognized for his success, Mr. Hammett holds a Martindale-Hubbell Distinguished Peer Review rating and has earned numerous other accolades from his peers. He also received many five-star reviews and heart-felt testimonials from his satisfied clients as well as 10 Best in client satisfaction award from the American Institute of Family Law Attorneys. His AVOO rating is 10.

attorneys.name: Ryan Harrington
attorneys.practice_type: Accidents Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Ryan J. Harrington has been in practice for over 20 years, having worked in both Wisconsin and Illinois while focusing on criminal defense, personal injury, bankruptcy, traffic, and temporary restraining orders due to domestic abuse or harassment.

Mr. Harrington joined D'Angelo & Jones as an associate in June of 2002, and was elected partner in January of 2007. He has practiced throughout southeastern Wisconsin in more than 20 counties, and was praised for his trial work by the Wisconsin State Public Defender in an issue of its monthly publication after winning an acquittal in his very first felony jury trial in 1998. Mr. Harrington has won acquittals at jury trial for clients facing a wide range of criminal charges, including Reckless Homicide, Delivery of Cocaine, Reckless Endangerment, and Battery to a Police Officer. Mr. Harrington has also obtained millions of dollars in verdicts and settlements on behalf of individuals and families injured or killed by the negligent acts of others and has successfully assisted many hundreds of individuals and families get back on their feet financially through bankruptcy.

Attorney Harrington is a former adjunct instructor in the Criminal Justice program at Bryant & Stratton College and has been recognized as a "Rising Star" by Wisconsin Super Lawyers, as published in Milwaukee Magazine. In addition, Attorney Harrington has been listed among the best criminal defense, bankruptcy and personal injury lawyers by the Shepherd Express in its annual Best of Milwaukee - Readers' Choice Awards.

Attorney Harrington is AVVO Rated as "Superb" and has been selected as a Leading Lawyer, Criminal Defense, in 2014 and 2015 in M Magazine's Leading Lawyers list. AVVO selects roughly the top 2% to 5% of lawyers in each practice area for inclusion on M Magazine's Leading Lawyers list.

In 2012, Attorney Harrington received the Client Distinction Award from Martindale-Hubbell, which is given to no more than 4% of the over 900,000 attorneys listed on martindale.com and lawyers.com., and in 2014, the American Society of Legal Advocates selected him as one of the ‘top 100' criminal defense lawyers in Wisconsin; inclusion comprises less than 1.5% of lawyers.

Mr. Harrington was born and raised in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, as the first of two children. He attended Marquette University and received a bachelor of arts degree in English and history in 1992, graduating as a member of both the English and history National Honor Societies. Mr. Harrington obtained his doctor of jurisprudence in 1995 from Marquette Law School, where his grandfather, Kenneth K. Luce, had taught as a law professor for over thirty years. Mr. Harrington accepted a nomination to serve as a member of the Moot Court Board and, during portions of both his undergraduate and law school studies, worked as an intern at the Milwaukee County District Attorney's Office. In addition, Mr. Harrington was employed by Marquette's Educational Opportunity Program as a university tutor for economically underprivileged students during his final three years of undergraduate study and also for one year while in law school.

Attorney Harrington is licensed to practice in the Eastern and Western Districts of Wisconsin, as well as the Northern District of Illinois, and is a member in good standing of the State Bar of Wisconsin and the Eastern District of Wisconsin Bar Association as well as the Milwaukee and Waukesha County Bar Associations. He is also a current or former member of the Milwaukee Young Lawyers Association, the private bar panel for the Wisconsin Association of Trial Lawyers of America, the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, and the Justinian Society. Mr. Harrington is married with two children.

attorneys.name: Michael F. Hart
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Michael F. Hart has practiced in the areas of criminal defense, civil litigation, and personal injury matters for twenty years. During that time, he has distinguished himself as a trial lawyer with an imposing courtroom presence. Court TV has identified Michael as one of the state's most prominent criminal defense attorneys, and he has been recognized by judges and lawyers throughout the state as a Wisconsin Super Lawyer.

Over the last two decades, Michael has obtained successful results in a large number of serious felony cases, including homicides, sexual assaults, and drug conspiracies, and has achieved notable results in a variety of white collar cases. Michael's successes have also included one of the largest defamation awards in state history against a private individual, which included a six-figure punitive damage award.

Michael has successfully represented a wide variety of high-profile clients, including members of the National Basketball Association, National Football League, Major League Baseball, as well as law enforcement officers and corporate executives. Many of Michael's most satisfying courtroom victories, however, have come from cases that don't make the evening news - the cases where hardworking people face the harsh consequences of being investigated and prosecuted by a government with unlimited resources and no mercy.

Michael maintains a strong legal presence locally and nationally. He is a member of the State Bar of Wisconsin, the State Bar of Michigan, the American Association for Justice, the Wisconsin Association for Justice, and the National Criminal Defense Association of Defense Lawyers. In addition to his active litigation practice, Michael is a former member of the Bradley Center Sports and Entertainment Corporation.

Michael earned his Bachelor's degree from the University of Wisconsin in 1985 and his law degree from the Michigan State University College of Law in 1988. A native of Flint, Michigan, he practiced in the Detroit area prior to moving to Wisconsin, where he founded Kohler & Hart, SC in 1993. Michael Hart is licensed to practice before Wisconsin State and Federal District Courts, as well as Michigan State and Federal District Courts.

Roberta attended Marquette University Law School, Milwaukee, Wisconsin, including study abroad at the University of Queensland, T.C. Berne School of Law, Brisbane, Queensland, Australia. attorneys.practice_type: Car Accident Lawyers in River Falls, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Martha Heidt is a dedicated litigation attorney with over 25 years of experience practicing in Wisconsin’s courts. She has honed her skills in legal research and writing, appellate practice, insurance coverage litigation, and drafting specialized discovery requests. Martha’s experience in insurance coverage and summary judgment briefing has helped her clients to achieve winning results in their cases.

Martha graduated cum laude from the University of Minnesota Law School and is licensed to practice law in Wisconsin. Her appellate experience includes briefing and oral arguments in both the Wisconsin Court of Appeals and the Wisconsin Supreme Court. Before pursuing a career in law, Martha worked in land conservation, dairy farming, and sheep farming.

At Bye, Goff & Rohde, Martha works with each of the trial attorneys to provide the best possible legal support to the clients. Her focus is on combing each file for the best available evidence, searching the law for sound authority applicable to the case, and providing a first-class work product that gives each client the best possible chance for a winning result.

Outside of work, Martha enjoys reading, gardening, bicycling, or riding her horse. She has lived on a working farm with her husband for over 35 years and spends her free time visiting her two adult children, their spouses, and her grandchildren whenever possible.

Martha’s experience in insurance coverage and summary judgment briefing has helped her clients to achieve winning results in their cases.

Martha graduated cum laude from the University of Minnesota Law School and is licensed to practice law in Wisconsin. Her appellate experience includes briefing and oral arguments in both the Wisconsin Court of Appeals and the Wisconsin Supreme Court. Before pursuing a career in law, Martha worked in land conservation, dairy farming, and sheep farming.

At Bye, Goff & Rohde, Martha works with each of the trial attorneys to provide the best possible legal support to the clients. Her focus is on combing each file for the best available evidence, searching the law for sound authority applicable to the case, and providing a first-class work product that gives each client the best possible chance for a winning result.

Outside of work, Martha enjoys reading, gardening, bicycling, or riding her horse. She has lived on a working farm with her husband for over 35 years and spends her free time visiting her two adult children, their spouses, and her grandchildren whenever possible.

attorneys.name: Jason J. Heinen
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Pewaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
My grandfather's great grandfather came to Milwaukee in 1867, the same year Jacob Leinenkugel and John Miller started a brewery in Chippewa Falls. However, instead of being skilled at brewing beer, Grandpa Heinen had a passion for woodworking. He started a cabinet shop out of his home and ran his small business off Market Street for over 15 years. Many people throughout Wisconsin have a passion for the skills and talents God gave them; they pour their lives into families and businesses they cherish. My passion is legal counseling and advocating for those brewers, woodworkers, and business owners—not only as hard workers who take pride in what they do, but as fathers, mothers, grandfathers, and grandmothers. I use my skills and talents to assist clients in navigating our legal system in a way that will help them protect their businesses and see that their family is provided for into the future.

Jason J. Heinen is originally from Neenah, Wisconsin. He graduated from the University of Wisconsin–Madison in 2008, obtaining a bachelor's degree with honors in the major of history. Attending Liberty University School of Law in Virginia, he gained an appreciation for property, estates, and transactional law. He graduated magna cum laude in 2011.

After admission to the Wisconsin bar, Jason practiced law in Delafield by day and volunteered with Lake Country Fire and Rescue by night. In 2016, he began practicing with the Law Offices of Mark S. Knutson, S.C., in Brookfield. Both in Delafield and Brookfield, he was mentored by experienced attorneys, while advising numerous clients through the complexity of estate planning, trust and probate administrations, and various kinds of corporate or real estate transactions.

Jason's passion is advocating and counseling individuals and business owners in the areas of estate planning, probate and trust administration, residential and commercial real estate transactions, corporate and business law, and adult guardianships. He skillfully assists clients in navigating our legal system in a way that will help them protect their businesses and see that their families are provided for in the future.

Jason and his wife, Jean, live in Lisbon and have six children. In his spare time, Jason enjoys everything outdoors: hunting, fishing, camping, etc.

attorneys.name: Timothy J. Helbing
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Law Lawyers in Appleton, WI
attorneys.bio:
I was born and raised in Janesville, WI, and received my undergraduate degree from Edgewood College in 1996. I earned my law degree from Hamline University School of Law in 2000.

I own and operate the Helbing Law Office, with offices in both Appleton and Green Bay, where my practice is dedicated to representing individuals and small business debtors in Chapter 7 and Chapter 13 bankruptcies and other debt relief programs.

I chose this area of practice because I truly believe that bad things happen to good people. I want to help those individuals in the Fox Valley and Northeast Wisconsin community who are struggling with financial problems and provide much needed assistance to begin a happier and healthier financial life.

When I am not in the office, you will most likely find me spending time with my two amazing sons, Tyler and Alex, or at an area youth soccer game or the dojo, where I have earned the rank of Nidan (second degree black belt) in Shuri Te Jujitsu and certified instructor in Inayan System 3 Eskrima.

Background

David has specialized in the practice of Family law for over 35 years. Over his career, David has participated in thousands of trials and hearings in the field of Family law. He has developed and continues to develop an emphasis toward Collaborative Family Law and mediation related to Family Law issues, including but not limited to legal custody and placement issues, maintenance (alimony) issues, and all financial issues presented in the numerous Family Law cases he has handled.

Credentials/Education

David earned a bachelor's degree from Georgetown University, graduating cum laude. He earned his law degree from Marquette University Law School.

Memberships

David is a member of the Wisconsin Bar Association. He has served on the Board of Commissioners of the City of Waukesha Housing Authority and the Waukesha County Ethics Board of Commissioners for 28 and 12 years respectively. He is presently the chair of both. David has also been an Arbitrator on the Wisconsin State Bar Fee Arbitration Panel for over 15 years.

Personal

David participates in a number of pro bono activities, including, but not limited to his contribution at the Waukesha County Family Law Clinic.

attorneys.bio:
@beckerhickey

Margaret Wrenn Hickey practices in the areas of divorce, family law, and elder law including trusts for the disabled, title 19 and guardianship. She is a shareholder in the law firm of Becker, Hickey & Poster, S.C., Milwaukee, and received her B.A. from Marquette University (1982, summa cum laude), where she was Phi Beta Kappa, and her J.D. from the University of Wisconsin Law School (1986, cum laude).

Margaret is a past Chair of the State Bar of Wisconsin Elder Law Section Board of Directors and a past Chair of the Family Law Section Board of Directors. She is a past President of the Milwaukee Bar Association (President 2004-05) and served on the Board of Directors from 1999-2005. Margaret currently serves on the State Bar of Wisconsin Board of Governors (District 2, 2005-09, Chair 2006-07) and will serve as Treasurer of the Board from 2009-11.

Margaret also serves on the Board of Directors of the Legal Aid Society and public radio station WUWM. Margaret lectures frequently at local, state and national bar meetings and to community groups and other professionals on elder law and family law topics. She has served on the board of Aurora Family Service, Rosalie Manor and the Village of Shorewood.

Margaret is a member of the American Bar Association, the State Bar of Wisconsin, the Milwaukee Bar Association, the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys, and the Association for Women Lawyers and she is a Fellow of the American Bar Foundation and the American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers (President for the Wisconsin Chapter, 2005-06.) She is named in the Best Lawyers in America for family and elder law and has been named as a "Super Lawyer" in elder law. She was also named in the top ten lawyers in Wisconsin by Super Lawyers (2012).

She is a member of the State Bar of Wisconsin, the Family Law section of the State Bar of Wisconsin, and has held her real estate broker's license from 2006 - 2014.

Attorney Hildebrand founded Hildebrand Law Firm, LLC in 2001 with the goal of providing compassionate service to her clients in a resourceful, efficient, and fair manner. Hildebrand Law Firm, LLC is dedicated to providing the highest quality services in a friendly but professional atmosphere.

The passion Kirsten exhibits for her clients is also evident in her community involvement. She is actively involved in teaching both children and adults through various Christian organizations. She also serves on the board of directors for the Scholaris Gifted Academy and is a member of the City of Mequon Festivals Committee.

With her husband Lee, Kirsten is a proud parent to three children.

attorneys.name: Paisley S. Hoffman
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Paisley Hoffman is an Associate Attorney with Nicholson Goetz & Otis, S.C., where she represents clients in a variety of areas of law including criminal defense, divorce, paternity, post-judgment custody and placement disputes, child in need of protection or services, delinquency, and injunctions. In addition to her role as advocacy counsel in these types of cases, Attorney Hoffman regularly is asked by multiple judges to serve as Guardian ad Litem representing the best interests of children in Dane County and surrounding counties. She has been asked to serve as advocacy counsel by a Dane County Judge.

Attorney Hoffman is a compassionate advisor and a strong legal advocate in court. Attorney Hoffman understands that the Court process can be confusing, and she takes time to understand her client’s concerns and explain the legal process. Attorney Hoffman appreciates the opportunity to help clients through the most difficult times in their lives.

Prior to obtaining her J.D., she worked for the Wisconsin Innocence Project reviewing serious criminal convictions for errors and obtained a Master of Social Work with a concentration in mental health. Attorney Hoffman’s background serves her clients in all areas of her practice. In criminal matters, Attorney Hoffman understands interpersonal relationships and is aware of the potential rehabilitative needs and resources for clients. In addition, she uses this background for creative resolutions to cases. In her family law practice, Attorney Hoffman is child-focused based on her understanding of children’s developmental needs and family dynamics.

In one of the fastest turnaround times after law school, Attorney Hoffman was named as one of Super Lawyers, Wisconsin Rising Stars in 2020. Attorney Hoffman obtained her J.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2017. She received her Bachelor of Arts in Legal Studies and Social Welfare in 2012 and her Master of Social Work in 2014 from the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

attorneys.practice_type: Business Lawyers in Elkhorn, WI
attorneys.bio:
Kim A. Howarth is a shareholder, vice president and secretary of Godfrey, Leibsle, Blackbourn & Howarth, S.C. Kim joined the firm shortly after earning his law degree from the University of Wisconsin in 1980. Kim earned his B.B.A., summa cum laude, from University of Wisconsin-Whitewater in 1977.

Kim's law practice concentrates on business, commercial, construction, and creditors rights law, including business organizations, condominium associations, and municipalities. Kim frequently speaks to business groups on the many issues that confront privately owned companies, and is an instructor for dwelling contractor certification classes. Beyond the needs of business, Kim represents and speaks frequently to homeowner and condominium associations. Kim's focus as an attorney is to first identify the best interest of the client and then assemble the best team to serve that client's needs.

Kim is licensed to practice in all courts in the State of Wisconsin, including the Federal District Court, Eastern and Western Districts of Wisconsin.

Kim is currently serving a three-year term on the Walworth County Economic Development Alliance, and was previously its President. He is a member of the State Bar of Wisconsin and the Walworth County Bar Association.

attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Michael F. Hupy graduated from Marquette University Law School in 1972, and has practiced personal injury law for over 35 years. He has tried and settled numerous Million Dollar personal injury cases including the largest verdict, at that time, in a slip and fall case in the State's history - $9.5 Million, a $5 Million structured settlement in a well known accident in which a large truck crashed through the wall at the House of Peace in Milwaukee and a $20 Million dollar award to an injured child in June 2006.

Attorney Michael F. Hupy is a Certified Civil Trial Specialist by the National Board of Trial Advocacy, has the highest rating in Martindale-Hubbell and is included in the Bar Register of Preeminent Lawyers, is Past President of the Wisconsin Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, a member of the Association of Trial Lawyers of America, a former member of the Wisconsin Academy of Trial Lawyers Board of Directors, a member of the Million Dollar Advocates Forum,selected for inclusion in Super Lawyers in Wisconsin in 2005, licensed in Wisconsin, in Illinois and an author and lecturer in trial practice. Mr. Hupy practices exclusively in the area of personal injury law.

Attorney Michael F. Hupy has taken a leading role in having our law firm give back to the community. We have supported worthwhile causes including America's Second Harvest of Wisconsin, the YMCA, the Boy Scouts, scholarship programs, safety programs for bikers, fingerprint programs, and have donated many hours and hundreds-of-thousands of dollars to various worthwhile causes.

attorneys.name: Stephen P. Hurley
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Steve Hurley is a trial lawyer. People come to him when they have a serious problem that needs to be fixed; whether it's a criminal charge or a civil complaint. Highly regarded for his ability to solve problems and to try cases, Steve was nominated and elected by his peers to the prestigious American College of Trial Lawyers and, for a decade, has been selected as one of the Top 10 Lawyers in Wisconsin by Superlawyers®. His reputation earns him many referrals from colleagues for both criminal and civil cases. Since 1989 he has also been an Adjunct Professor at the University of Wisconsin Law School teaching evidence and trial advocacy.

When it comes to appearing in court Steve says, "First, I care about my client. It's the only way one can accomplish anything. Second, I prepare. What you see in court is a show-not one line is unrehearsed. Liken it to a play written, produced and performed by one person for one show. One can't be successful without preparation.

attorneys.name: Gayle B Jebbia
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Gayle Jebbia is a divorce and family law attorney based in the firm’s Dodgeville office. For over 20 years, she has provided legal counsel to clients in Southwest Wisconsin in the following counties: Iowa, Grant, Lafayette, Richland, Sauk, and Crawford.

Gayle’s practice concentrates on all phases of divorce, custody, placement, property division, prenuptial agreements, postnuptial agreements, post-divorce matters, grandparents’ rights, step-parent adoptions, guardianships, co-habitation agreements, and paternity. She is experienced in property issues related to farms and businesses, as well as other complex legal issues which frequently arise in rural Wisconsin divorces.

Currently the Iowa County Bar President, Gayle previously served on the District 12 Office of Lawyer Regulation Investigative Committee for nine years. She was appointed by the Wisconsin Supreme Court to the Appointment Selection Committee, serving a three-year term. Gayle was on the “Through the Eyes of a Child” Guardian Ad Litem Planning Committee for child advocacy, and taught a seminar on Guardian Ad Litem Processes.

Originally from Montana, Gayle is licensed to practice law in the Wisconsin, Oregon and Montana. She received an undergraduate degree in History from Oregon State University in 1984 and her J.D. from the University of Oregon School of Law in 1991.

attorneys.name: Katherine A. Jens
attorneys.practice_type: Municipal Law Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Katherine (Katie) Jens is a member of the firm’s municipal, real estate law, and environmental law teams. Katie assists Murphy Desmond’s municipal clients with drafting ordinances, contract review, negotiations, special assessments, and open meetings requirements. In real estate, Katie handles matters related to titles, deeds, zoning, property disputes, and transactional work such as buying and selling a home. Katie also works with the firm’s environmental practice group on issues related to land use, climate factors, renewable energy, and sustainability.

A 2024 graduate of Florida State University College of Law, Katie worked as a law clerk where she assisted with real estate matters in estate planning, including transfer-on-death deeds. Katie also served as a student volunteer where she advised indigent clients on their rights and remedies in home ownership and renting matters. As an intern with a Wisconsin title company, Katie reviewed title insurance policies, examined closing statements for accuracy, and assisted at numerous closings.

While in law school, Katie served as an editor for the Florida State University Business Review, where she earned the 2022-2023 “Staff Editor of the Year” award.

Katie is available to assist clients in the firm’s Madison, Janesville, and Dodgeville offices.

attorneys.name: Erik C. Johnson
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Oshkosh, WI
attorneys.bio:
Erik has been licensed to practice law in the State of Wisconsin since 2004. Upon licensure, Erik quickly found his home with Gregory R. Wright Law Offices, S.C. in Montello, Wisconsin. Erik’s areas of focus are personal injury matters and criminal defense. Erik prides himself on his diligent and aggressive approach to his criminal defense practice. Since 2004, Erik’s criminal defense practice has grown exponentially. Erik skillfully defends various criminal matters ranging from traffic citations to drunken driving matters to violent felonies. Erik has extensive experience having litigated numerous issues at the trial level and has advocated for his clients’ cause in the Wisconsin Court of Appeals when needed. Erik’s success for his criminal clients ranges from multiple dismissal and acquittals after jury trials.

Erik’s skilled and effective trial strategies, as well as his personable and down-to-earth demeanor, have spread his loyal client base statewide. Erik has experience litigating criminal defense matters in the following counties: Marquette, Green Lake, Waushara, Portage, Adams, Columbia, Fond du Lac, Winnebago, Waupaca, Outagamie, Dane, Sauk, Milwaukee, and Ozaukee Counties. His personal Injury practice is statewide.

Erik prides himself on helping his clients in any way he can. He will always treat people with dignity and respect and take the time to help them navigate an uncertain and intimidating legal world. Be it personal injury or criminal defense, Erik’s clients consistently praise him as a person and an excellent attorney.

attorneys.name: Genelle Johnson
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Appleton, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Genelle Johnson earned her undergraduate degree from Loyola University Chicago with a major in Criminal Justice, as well as minors in Psychology and Political Science. Upon graduation, she attended Marquette University Law School, where she earned certificates in Alternative Dispute Resolution, Real Estate, and Sports Law. Attorney Johnson earned her Juris Doctor in May of 2007, and has ever since been practicing in the Fox Valley.

Immediately after completing her law degree, Attorney Johnson began her career locally in the Fox Valley as a Special Prosecutor for the Outagamie County District Attorneys Office. Realizing early on her passion lies with client service, she began her private practice with a focus on Criminal Defense. Attorney Johnson served as defense counsel for nearly 11 years, all while building her general private practice to include Family Law, Small Claims, Guardianships, Juvenile Defense, and Guardian as Litem service in CPS cases.

Attorney Johnson has always had a distinct passion for Family Law practice, and feels strongly that the divorce process and parties’ experiences in the courtroom will permanently impact their lives—and the lives of their family members. Since 2018, Attorney Johnson has focused her practice solely on Family Law, from mediation to trial litigation, and everything in between. Her practice has expanded to include Counties throughout the State of Wisconsin, and mentoring other attorneys who share in that passion.

Attorney Genelle Johnson is ready to serve our Fox Valley clients and is located in our Appleton, Wisconsin office.

attorneys.name: Russell J. A. Jones
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
I am a trial lawyer. I love trials. A jury trial is when the legal system is at its best. The Constitution grants every citizen the right to trial by jury, and that is a right we all should exercise when necessary. I have been lead counsel on hundreds of jury trials, both at the State and Federal level.

However, at times, negotiating a settlement is the right course of action. My reputation for zealous representation results in the best negotiated results. I have the respect of the opposition and the trust of the judges.

I have tried and won cases ranging from first-degree intentional homicide to disorderly conduct. I have successfully argued to protect constitutional rights and have engineered favorable results for clients in all aspects of litigation. In short, I am the lawyer you want when you need to fight for your freedom, your family, or your rights.

I am a four time winner of the Martin Hanson Memorial Prize, awarded by the Wisconsin Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers. In 2023 Jones Law Firm was named best solo practice law firm in Wisconsin by the Wisconsin Law Journal. In 2021 I was named a Top 100 Criminal Defense Trial Lawyer by the National Trial Lawyers Association. I was named a Leader in the Law in 2020 by the Wisconsin Law Journal; along with being named as a Rising Star in 2010 by Super Lawyers. My firm, was named The Best of Milwaukee in 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2023 by The Shepard Express.

I graduated with honors from Marquette University Law School in 2002 and I founded Jones Law Firm in 2008. I am licensed to practice law by the Supreme Court of Wisconsin, the Eastern and Western Districts for the Federal Court of Wisconsin, and the 7th Circuit Court of Appeals.

attorneys.name: Brett T. Kaehne
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Sheboygan, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Brett T. Kaehne has been exclusively practicing in the field of criminal defense for over a decade. For the first six years of his career, he founded and grew a successful criminal defense firm in Sheboygan. In 2014, he joined Kirk Obear & Associates becoming a member of a team of like-minded defense attorneys taking on the government in counties across the State. In 2019, Attorney Kaehne joined Attorney Barrette in establishing their own criminal defense law firm to better serve those accused of crimes throughout Wisconsin.

Throughout the years, Attorney Kaehne has obtained dismissals of countless Misdemeanor and Felony charges by means of constitutional challenges, negotiations, and not guilty verdicts at jury trial. He is grounded in the understanding that on a daily basis he is not simply dealing with criminal cases, he is dealing with the future and livelihood of people and their families.

Because of his passion for criminal defense and results in the courtroom, Attorney Kaehne has presented at several seminars throughout the State educating other defense attorneys on a variety of topics. As a NORML legal committee member, he is also dedicated to reforming the outdated laws on cannabis use to make cannabis legal medicinally, and for responsible adults for recreational use.

attorneys.name: Emily Kehl
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Emily Kehl joined Hart Powell, S.C. in 2025 after earning her Juris Doctorate from Marquette University Law School. Emily’s practice focuses on defending people accused of crimes in state and federal courts. Emily has a strong passion for helping those entangled in the criminal justice system. Her interest in the criminal justice system began at the University of Wisconsin Madison where she earned her Bachelor’s degree in 2022 in legal studies, psychology, and criminal justice. Since joining the firm, Emily has shown a strong work ethic and determination that has shaped her into a zealous advocate for her clients.

While attending Marquette University Law School, Emily clerked for prominent criminal defense attorney Michael Steinle, interned for Milwaukee County Circuit Court Judge Laura Crivello, served as President of First Generation Professionals, worked as a Research Assistant for Dean Anna Fodor, the Assistant Dean of Students, competed in the National Criminal Procedure Moot Court competition, was inducted into the Pro Bono Honor Society, and received the CALI award for excellence in Legal Analysis, Writing and Research. Emily is a member of the Wisconsin Bar Association, Young Lawyers Division, the Milwaukee Bar Association, and the Eastern District of Wisconsin Bar Association. Outside of work, Emily loves to be outside, whether that be going for a walk, or out on the lake back home in Oconomowoc. She is licensed to practice in the Federal District Courts of Wisconsin and Wisconsin State Courts.

attorneys.name: Katie E. Kelly
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning & Probate Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Katie Kelly is a member of the firm’s estate planning and probate team, where she works with individuals, couples and families in all stages of life. Katie drafts wills, powers of attorney documents, and marital property agreements that help provide peace of mind for her clients. She prepares and updates trusts that allow clients to dictate specific handling of assets and care for heirs, and she assists with trust administration.

Katie has a particular interest in working with nontraditional relationships and families in estate planning, to ensure her clients’ wishes are met if they become disabled or when they pass. She proactively helps clients with unique estate planning situations that can occur with non-married couples, as well as with those co-parenting children in which only one parent is biological.

In probate matters, Katie assists clients with transfer of property, disputes among heirs, and guiding personal representatives through the probate process. She prepares estate plans that bypass the need for probate whenever possible.

Katie previously served as a law clerk at Murphy Desmond S.C. while in law school, and as a legal assistant prior to attending law school. As a law clerk, she assisted various practice groups, but spent significant time working on litigation matters, including assisting with discovery, proofreading, drafting briefs and arguments, and helping with pre-trial preparations.

Katie serves clients in the firm’s Madison, Janesville, and Dodgeville, Wisconsin offices.

attorneys.name: Cristina M. Kerr
attorneys.practice_type: Car Accident Lawyers in Eau Claire, WI
attorneys.bio:
Cristina is a board-certified Civil Trial Specialist and shareholder with BGR. She practices in the firm’s River Falls office. Cristina has an exclusive focus on helping injured individuals in a variety of cases including premises liability claims and automobile collisions. Cristina takes immense pride in serving her clients who are often facing new and confusing circumstances following an injury. She understands that injuries can be life-changing, and that clarity, guidance, support, and understanding are crucial when dealing with uncooperative insurance companies.

Cristina is a formidable force in the realm of personal injury law and has been recognized both locally and nationally for her work. In 2023, she was awarded the Outstanding Young Trial Lawyer of the Year Award from the Wisconsin Association of Justice, given to a single recipient each year who demonstrates a strong commitment to the honor and dignity of justice for the public good and the right to trial by jury. In 2024, Cristina was inducted into the American Board of Trial Advocates, an invitation-only national association of experienced trial lawyers and judges dedicated to preserving and promoting the Seventh Amendment right to trial by jury.

In 2025, Cristina was invited to become a Fellow of the American Bar Foundation, a global honorary society of attorneys, judges, law faculty, and legal scholars whose public and private careers have demonstrated outstanding dedication to the highest principles of the legal profession. ABF Fellows membership is by invitation only and is limited to only 1% of licensed attorneys nationwide.

Cristina’s experience in personal injury law began when she joined BGR as a clerical assistant in 2012. She returned to the firm during law school as a law clerk, assisting attorneys with case preparation for trial. Cristina’s early exposure to litigation and trial work allows her to leverage her extensive experience to guide clients through complex legal processes, ensuring they receive the compensation they deserve.

Cristina attended law school at the University of Wisconsin Law School, where she graduated magna cum laude. She served on the Law Review senior board and was inducted into the Pro Bono Society. After law school, Cristina clerked for Chief Judge Edward J. Cleary at the Minnesota Court of Appeals.

Born and raised in Western Wisconsin, Cristina’s commitment to her community extends beyond her legal practice. She actively volunteers as an attorney coach for the River Falls High School Mock Trial program, inspiring young minds and fostering a love for the legal profession. When she’s not working or volunteering, Cristina enjoys spending time with her husband and rescue dogs, as well as pursuing an active lifestyle through strength training, hiking, kayaking, and skiing.

attorneys.name: Joshua J. Kindkeppel
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Joshua J. Kindkeppel practices law primarily in the areas of business, real estate, and employment. He represents individuals and a wide range of businesses in these areas, and Josh especially enjoys working on renewable energy projects.

Josh handles business start-ups, represents clients in business acquisitions and guides owners through break-ups and dissolutions. Josh prepares, negotiates, and advises clients on contracts, and he enjoys representing clients in real estate transactions. He also frequently provides employment advice to business owners, human resource departments, and individuals. Josh's practice also includes business, real estate, and employment litigation, representing professionals in licensing appeals, and appearing before a variety of regulatory agencies.

Josh is a native of Wisconsin and has been practicing in Dane County since 2003. One of his favorite things about being an attorney is the long-standing relationships he has with many of his clients. Some of his clients date back to his first year of practice. Clients appreciate Josh’s troubleshooting abilities, his hard work ethic, responsiveness, and easy-going nature.

Josh is an active member of the Dane County legal community and served as president of the Dane County Bar Association, co-founded the Dane County Bar attorney mentorship program, and co-founded a free legal clinic in Sun Prairie, the Sunshine Legal Clinic.

attorneys.name: Jeffrey Kippa
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Appleton, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Jeffrey P. Kippa has been practicing law in Wisconsin since 2001.

With dozens of criminal defense attorneys already practicing in the Fox Valley, why did I start my own firm?

Simply put, I try to put myself in my client's shoes, to understand their fears, frustrations and concerns.

When people find themselves in the position of needing a criminal defense attorney, often times they are at extreme low points in their lives. While every case is different, each person charged needs a guide – someone to show the criminal justice system (the prosecutor, the judge, sometimes the public) that they are not the person they are being portrayed to be. And, that's what I want to be: their guide.

Choosing the Right Approach

Saying that I am an aggressive trial attorney who will take your case to trial is true. But, it is only part of the whole picture.

Pre-trial and sometimes pre-charging tactics and techniques can often times spare someone the uncertainty, emotional stress and financial burden of a trial. Having the insight and tact to deal with prosecutors, being able to develop a rapport with not only judges but also prosecutors, while coupling that with a sense of compassion for my clients, a sensitivity for the sense of uncertainty they feel, will help my clients reach the appropriate outcome, and leave them with a sense that their voice was heard and not swallowed by the system.

Here's the Truth

Like many good criminal defense attorneys, I love to take cases to trial. It is easily the best part of the job. That doesn't mean it is the best thing for my clients.

Unfortunately, I often hear of other, unscrupulous attorneys promising potential clients certain outcomes. To me, this defines the word "unethical." There are so many variables that affect the outcome of a case (such as the prosecutor, the wishes of the alleged victim, the judge and, most importantly, the facts of the case), that no attorney can promise you an outcome.

Promises to My Clients

These are the promises I make to my clients:

I will be compassionate, understanding with what they are going through;

I will be available if an emergency arises;

I will be prompt in addressing concerns;

I will litigate the case to the fullest extent that benefits them;

I will keep them apprised of the status of their case during each step of the process;

I will be approachable and accessible (you will not get stuck voicing concerns to a staff person, but rather with me directly);

And, should the day come, I promise that I will gladly present their case to a jury and fight my hardest to prevail.

Not many defense attorneys will give you their cell phone number. That's just one example of the fresh approach I bring to my criminal defense clients. And, just one of the reasons I decided to start J. Kippa Law Office.

attorneys.name: Zachary J. Kluck
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Zachary J. Kluck grew up in the small farming community of Rosholt, Wisconsin, which is near Stevens Point. Zachary did his undergraduate work at Marquette University where he was an integral member of the Marquette Band, serving as President, Vice-President, and Small Ensembles Director. After graduating from Marquette in 2004, he worked for a personal injury firm in Milwaukee for two years.

Soon he decided that he wanted to pursue his interest in the law and was accepted to the University of Dayton School of Law (UDSL) in Ohio, a law school renowned for its Legal Profession courses involving legal research and writing. While at UDSL, Zachary served as a member of the student-operated Honor Council and was involved in various volunteer programs, including the Volunteer Income Tax Assistance program through the Internal Revenue Service, which resulted in a Pro Bono Commitment Community Award. He was also a member of a civil trial practice team, was a law clerk in Milwaukee, and held his intern license, enabling him to represent indigent clients in county court.

After graduating from UDSL in 2009 with a JD, Zachary returned to his roots in Wisconsin and passed the Wisconsin bar exam. He spent a year in Tomah, after which he joined DeVos & Zerbst in September 2010 and moved to the Madison area. In March 2015, he and Attorney Jessica Zerbst, who passed away in December 2017, started Zerbst & Kluck, S.C., which is now Capital Law Group, S.C.

Attorney Kluck has been practicing bankruptcy, debt collection, and consumer rights for 10+ years. Debt is hard on individuals. The strain and pressure of debt creates a huge weight on a person's shoulders and can negatively impact many aspects of daily life. Our services offer a chance to relieve that pressure. Many of our clients state that the hardest part of the process was the decision to retain an attorney. Once that was decided, they felt the pressure being lifted. Attorney Kluck has helped clients through every step of the process and explained the bankruptcy so that they can get the fresh start they need.

Attorney Kluck is licensed to practice in all state courts in Wisconsin, as well as the Wisconsin federal district courts. He is married to his wonderful wife who is a teacher. In his spare time, Zachary enjoys golfing, reading, volleyball, playing with his two dogs, and watching the Packers.

Attorney Todd R. Korb has practiced law since earning his Juris Doctor from the University of Wisconsin Law School in 1996. He is licensed to practice in Wisconsin, Iowa, the United States District Courts for the Eastern and Western Districts of Wisconsin, and the Seventh Circuit Court of Appeals.

Attorney Korb is actively involved in the Wisconsin Association for Justice, the American Association for Justice, the Milwaukee Bar Association, and he is a lifetime member of ABATE of Wisconsin. His professional achievements include lifetime membership in the Million Dollar Advocates Forum and Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum, as well as recognition by Elite Lawyers of America.

He remains deeply involved in his community as a member of his town’s government and serves on the board of The Food Pantry Inc. in Port Washington and is an active member of BMW Motorcycle Club of Wisconsin.

Attorney Korb has been recognized for excellence in personal injury law, including selection to the Wisconsin Super Lawyers List (2022–Present) and recognition as a Leader in the Law by the Wisconsin Law Journal (2018, 2025). He holds a Superb 10.0 AVVO Rating and has been named a Top 100 Trial Lawyer: Civil Plaintiff by the National Trial Lawyers.

Over nearly a decade of practice, Attorney Korb has recovered millions for his clients and has frequently lectured on legal and insurance coverage issues in Wisconsin.
