attorneys.name: Elizabeth D. Reeths
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Defense Lawyers in Wausau, WI
attorneys.bio:
Elizabeth has spent her entire legal career defending insurance companies and insureds in personal injury and other tort claims, litigating insurance coverage disputes, and defending municipalities. She has represented clients in both state and federal court. Her practice includes all aspects of civil litigation and civil appeals.

Elizabeth is a contributing author of the Wisconsin Law of Damages. She has been recognized in Wisconsin Super Lawyers magazine as a Rising Star in Insurance Coverage for 2018-2023.

In 2021, Elizabeth was elected Treasurer of the State Bar of Wisconsin and also served on the State Bar's Board of Governors from 2021-2023. Elizabeth has also been a member of the State Bar of Wisconsin's Continuing Legal Education Committee (2014-2020, Committee Chair 2018-2020), Finance Committee (2018-2020, 2021-2024), and the Member Services Committee (2020-2021.) She is a member of the Wisconsin Defense Counsel, the WDC's Women in the Law Committee and was President of the Marathon County Bar Association's Young Lawyers Division from 2012-2015.

Born and raised in Muskegon, Michigan, Elizabeth earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in English literature and political science from the University of Michigan in 2008. Elizabeth obtained her Juris Doctor degree in 2011 from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where she was a member of the Moot Court board. While in law school, Elizabeth worked as a law clerk for the University of Wisconsin-Madison Office of Administrative Legal Services and had internships at the Wisconsin Department of Justice and with Judge John Albert of the Dane County Circuit Court.

Elizabeth is is licensed to practice law in the State of Wisconsin, State of Michigan, Eastern District of Wisconsin, Western District of Wisconsin, the Seventh Circuit Court of Appeals, and the United States Supreme Court.

attorneys.name: Rosemary Reniero
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce/Legal Separation Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Rosemary Reniero is an associate in the firm’s Family Law Practice Group.

Rosemary is a dedicated advocate for individuals navigating complex and emotionally challenging family law matters. Her practice is grounded in a commitment to providing thoughtful guidance and strong representation during some of the most difficult moments in her clients' lives.

Her practice encompasses all areas of family law, including divorce, legal custody, physical placement, child support, maintenance, paternity, and grandparent rights. She is experienced in guiding clients through these matters, whether they are isolated actions or related to other proceedings, such as injunctions or criminal cases. Rosemary approaches each case with an understanding that the family court action is often just one component of a broader situation.

During law school, Rosemary clerked for Pines Bach and participated in the Wisconsin Law School Family Court Clinic, where she represented clients in divorce actions, post-judgment custody and placement disputes, and special immigrant juvenile status proceedings. She also supported pro se litigants through the Dane County Family Law Assistance Center and continues to volunteer with DCFLAC to this day.

As Symposium Editor for the Wisconsin Journal of Law, Gender and Society, Rosemary helped to shed light on how society’s shifting social and moral values have impacted and complicated the law of paternity, facilitating scholarship and debate within the field of family law.

Prior to attending law school, Rosemary developed her passion for advocating for victims of domestic abuse as a WATCH court monitor in Hennepin County, Minnesota, where she observed criminal proceedings involving domestic violence to ensure victims were treated with the respect and empathy they deserve.

attorneys.name: Eliza Marie Reyes
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Eliza M. Reyes is an attorney in the Madison Office of Richman & Richman LLC. Since 2005, her practice has focused on financial matters, with a practice primarily focused on representation of debtors, creditors, trustees, landlords, tenants, investors and most other parties in interest with issues before the bankruptcy, federal and state courts; including individual and commercial bankruptcy filings under Chapters 7, 13, 12, and 11; objections to discharge; fraudulent transfer issues; asset valuation issues; adversary proceedings; defense of foreclosure actions; debt collection; contract disputes; real estate matters; and individual, agricultural and commercial reorganizations.

She is a member of the Bankruptcy, Insolvency, and Creditors’ Rights Section and the Solo and Small Firm Section of the State Bar of Wisconsin. Eliza has also been a presenter at conferences on various topics related to financial matters and bankruptcy and is the author of the Creditor/Debtor Chapter of the Wisconsin Attorney’s Desk Reference 2018, published by Pinnacle Books, and the Creditors’ Rights & Remedies chapter of Marital Property Law in Wisconsin, also published by Pinnacle Books. Eliza is a 1991 graduate of the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee with a degree in Mass Communication/Journalism, and she received her J.D. from The John Marshall Law School in 1997.

attorneys.bio:
Michael P. Richman focuses on representing Chapter 11 debtors and creditors' committees and advises on virtually every aspect of financial distress and bankruptcy.

Throughout his extensive career, Michael has appeared as counsel in state courts, federal courts and, in particular, bankruptcy courts in nearly 20 states and territories.

Michael focuses on the representation of Chapter 11 debtors and creditors' committees. He regularly advises and represents clients in virtually every aspect of financial distress and bankruptcy, including out-of-court restructurings, prosecution and defense of creditors' rights litigation (including preference and fraudulent conveyance cases), individual and group secured and unsecured creditors, landlords, purchasers of assets under Bankruptcy Code section 363 and other parties in interest.

An active member of the American Bankruptcy Institute, Michael has served as director (1996-2008), chairman of the board (2006-07) and president (2004-05) of that organization; and has been a member of its management and executive committees. Michael is also the founder and a performing member of ABI's house band, the Indubitable Equivalents, which regularly performs at bankruptcy conferences around the country. A frequent speaker and lecturer on bankruptcy law and related topics, Michael is a contributing editor to the American Bankruptcy Institute Journal and, while in law school, served as the managing editor of the Columbia Journal of Transnational Law.

Michael is admitted to practice before the U.S. District Court for the Districts of Arizona, Colorado, Connecticut, and District of Columbia; and for the Northern District of Illinois, the Western District of Michigan, the Eastern and Southern Districts of New York, and the Eastern and Western Districts of Wisconsin. He is also admitted to practice in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal, Second, Third, Seventh and Ninth Circuits.

Michael is an adjunct professor of bankruptcy law at the University of Wisconsin Law School.

Mr. Richman is a debt relief agent. He helps people file for bankruptcy relief under the Bankruptcy Code.

attorneys.name: Claire Ann Richman
attorneys.practice_type: Commericial Bankruptcy & Insolvency Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
As a partner in Richman & Richman LLC's bankruptcy and insolvency group, Claire Ann Richman handles cases of consumer and commercial bankruptcy and insolvency, litigation, debt collection, contract disputes and real estate. Located in Madison, Wisconsin, she is a popular lecturer on issues related to bankruptcy for Lorman Education Services, the National Business Institute, the University of Wisconsin Law School, the American Conference Institute, the State Bar of Wisconsin, the National Association of Bankruptcy Trustees, the American Bankruptcy Institute and the United States Trustee Training Program.

A graduate of Marquette University, Ms. Richman earned a Bachelor of Arts with a major in education in 1987. She then attended the University of Wisconsin Law School to obtain a Juris Doctor in 1993. She has published works for the National Association of Bankruptcy Trustees journal and is admitted to practice in Wisconsin state courts, as well as before the U.S. District Court for the District of Colorado, the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois, and the U.S. District Courts for the Western and Eastern Districts of Wisconsin.

Ms. Richman is a past chair of the State Bar of Wisconsin Bankruptcy, Insolvency and Creditors’ Rights section. A former member of the board of directors of the American Bankruptcy Institute, she is also a member of the Dane County Bar Association and the American Bar Association.

For several years, Ms. Richman served on the United States Trustee Program Chapter 7 bankruptcy panel. She represents a wide range of clients, including tenants, landlords, investors, creditors, debtors and creditors’ committees.

Ms. Richman is a debt relief agent. She helps people file for bankruptcy relief under the Bankruptcy Code.

attorneys.name: Lane Rideout
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Lane Rideout represents business clients in an array of legal matters, including entity formation, operating agreements, business planning, contracts, employment matters, and succession planning.

Lane has provided legal assistance to a variety of business industries, including significant work with tech start-ups. She counsels businesses on strategic planning, human resources matters, leases, regulatory matters, taxes, and more. Lane is experienced in drafting and negotiating contracts with vendors, employees, business landlords, and other third-party operations impacting a business.

In employment law, Lane has assisted independent contractors, employers, and employees with a range of issues including wages, classification, non-compete agreements, discrimination, harassment, and employment best practices.

Prior to joining Murphy Desmond in 2022, Lane served as Principal Attorney of her own firm in Colorado. In addition, she formed and oversaw operations of several tech start-ups. Earlier in her career, Lane practiced public pension law in Massachusetts.

Lane is available to assist clients in the firm's Madison, Janesville, and Dodgeville offices.

attorneys.name: Lynn M. Rider
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Lawyers in Prairie du Chien, WI
attorneys.bio:
Lynn M. Rider is a Of Counsel and has practiced law since 1985. She assists clients in estate planning, real estate, probate, and planning and decision making affecting older adults, Ms. Rider has also successfully represented clients in bankruptcy actions and family law actions.

Ms. Rider received her B.S. degree in Economics-Mathematics Emphasis from University of Wisconsin in 1982 and her J.D. degree from the University of Wisconsin School of Law in 1985. Ms. Rider served one term as the Crawford County District Attorney in 1986-87 before choosing to return to private practice. Ms. Rider is a member of the Children and the Law division and the Bankruptcy Law section of the State Bar. She has been a speaker at several meetings and conferences concerning estate planning, guardianship and bankruptcy issues. Ms. Rider has served on numerous local agencies and boards, and is actively involved at St. Peters Lutheran Church. When not at work, Ms. Rider's enjoys traveling, woodturning, quilting and spending time with her three boys.

Ms. Rider is a member of the Wisconsin bar and the following courts: United States District Court for the Western District of Wisconsin; and United States District Court for the Eastern District of Wisconsin.

attorneys.bio:
Criminal Defense Attorney Milwaukee Turns to achieve the best results for Dropped or Reduced Charges

Attorney Morgan L. Risseeuw graduated magna cum laude from the University of Wisconsin-Platteville with a degree in criminal justice. She then earned her Juris Doctor at Marquette University Law School. While attending law school, Attorney Risseeuw received CALI awards for achieving the highest grades in her Legal Research and Writing class, as well as in Constitutional Criminal Procedure. She also coordinated the domestic violence injunction pro bono project at Marquette Law School to provide legal representation to low-income victims of domestic violence. Morgan has experience working in the State Public Defenders' office in Sheboygan and Manitowoc Counties, the District I Court of Appeals in Milwaukee, and as a law clerk in a private criminal defense firm in Racine. Attorney Risseeuw prides herself on working hard to achieve the best results possible for her clients.

attorneys.name: Matthew Robles
attorneys.practice_type: Workers Compensation Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Robles joined Hawks Quindel as an Associate Attorney in 2014. His practice focuses on representing employees in worker's compensation matters, and criminal defense, representing individuals charged with crimes or violating traffic laws and municipal ordinances. Before joining the firm, Mr. Robles worked as a law clerk for the Honorable Frank. D. Remington and Honorable Stephen Ehlke at the Dane County Circuit Court. Mr. Robles handled a wide array of cases, including civil litigation, criminal law, and administrative law.

Mr. Robles graduated from the University of Wisconsin Law School with honors in 2013. During law school, Mr. Robles worked for a number of the law school’s clinical programs. Mr. Robles worked as a student attorney for the Legal Assistance to Institutionalized Persons Project (LAIP), where he represented incarcerated individuals in postconviction matters. He also worked as a law intern for the Dane County District Attorney’s Office, where he conducted a number of trials, including felonies. Mr. Robles received the Abner Brodie Award for his outstanding clinical work.

Mr. Robles completed his undergraduate education at the University of Wisconsin—Madison, earning a bachelor’s degree in Political Science.

Mr. Robles is a member of the State Bar of Wisconsin and the Dane County Bar Association. He is also admitted to practice in federal court in Wisconsin’s Eastern and Western Districts. Mr. Robles currently serves as an ad hoc member of the Wisconsin Judicial Council Committee on Appellate Procedure.

Julius – or Jay to his friends and colleagues - practices civil litigation as an associate attorney with Godfrey, Leibsle, Blackbourn and Howarth, S.C. Jay is a graduate of Marquette University Law School’s class of 2025.

While pursuing his legal education, Jay gained valuable hands-on experience working under the supervision of experienced practitioners pursuant to Wisconsin’s Student Practice Rule. Spong Moot Court Competition in Virginia. Jay also assumed a leadership role as the 2024-2025 Associate Justice for Education for the Marquette University Law School Moot Court program. Jay particularly enjoyed coaching his junior classmates in mock argument in his final year of law school.

Outside the law, Julius enjoys cycling Southeastern Wisconsin’s many bike trails, reading novels, and studying history.

attorneys.name: Dean R. Rohde
attorneys.practice_type: Car Accident Lawyers in River Falls, WI
attorneys.bio:
Dean is a trial attorney who is dedicated to representing clients in personal injury cases. His interest in the law began at a young age, when he read a book about lawyers at age 10. Born in Marshfield, Wisconsin, Dean comes from a family with deep roots in Wisconsin agriculture, including his grandfather, who was the President of the Wisconsin Farmers Union, and his father, who held the position of Wisconsin Secretary of Agriculture.

Dean pursued a degree in Agricultural Business Management and was a member of the Alpha Gamma Rho Agriculture fraternity at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where he met his wife, Laurie, and became a lifelong Badger fan. After working as a Bank Loan Officer, Dean returned to UW-Madison to earn an M.B.A. before obtaining his law degree. During law school, Dean and his wife served as "houseparents" for a sorority, providing housing for around 50 women on the shore of Lake Mendota.

Dean is an experienced trial attorney who is passionate about representing clients in court. He enjoys the challenge of presenting his clients' cases to a jury and counts Trials as the most exciting and satisfying aspect of his work. Dean takes pride in his attention to detail and is committed to helping his clients navigate the legal system with confidence. He loves getting good results for his clients and knowing he has helped them get through a difficult part of their life.

Outside of work, Dean enjoys many outdoor activities, including fishing, hunting, golf, tennis, boating, ATV'ing, snowmobiling, and gardening. He has been involved in many civic organizations, including serving as the President of the River Falls Chamber of Commerce, serving on the Foundation Board of the Chippewa Valley Technical College, and being on the Board of Directors of the River Falls Community Foundation. He loves to travel and counts Greece as his favorite destination so far. In his home office, he has a 48" Northern Pike caught in Manitoba, Canada, hanging on the wall.

attorneys.name: Michael J. Roman
attorneys.practice_type: Employee Rights -- Employer Lawyers in Wausau, WI
attorneys.bio:
Mike is a native of Waupaca, Wisconsin. He attended the University of Wisconsin - Madison, where he obtained a Bachelor of Arts - triple-majoring in political science, history, and international relations.

Mike attended Marquette University Law School in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, obtaining a Juris Doctor in 1994. While at Marquette, he served as a member of the Marquette Law Review, first as an associate and then as an executive editor.

After law school, Mike served as a law clerk with the Wisconsin Court of Appeals - District I, located in Milwaukee, working first for the Honorable Michael T. Sullivan and then later the Honorable Patricia S. Curley. As a law clerk, he gained significant experience in appellate procedure and practice, and he obtained valuable knowledge in effective legal argument and appellate advocacy.

Mike primarily defends municipalities and municipal insurers, and other liability insurers in a variety of civil litigation matters in Wisconsin state courts, administrative agencies, and the federal courts in Wisconsin. He has successfully defended and advised municipalities, law enforcement agencies, and their insurers in a variety of cases and lawsuits, including:

Constitutional and civil rights claims against municipalities

Employment and discrimination claims against municipalities

Wrongful arrest and excessive use of force claims against law enforcement agencies

First Amendment/Adult Business ordinance claims against municipalities

State open meetings and public records claims against municipalities

Insurance coverage issues

Mike has also developed a significant appellate practice, writing briefs and appearing in over 40 appeals in both the state and federal appellate courts, and he has successfully argued before the Wisconsin Supreme Court and the Wisconsin Court of Appeals.

In his free time, Charles loves traveling, golfing, spending time with his family and attending sporting events including rooting for the Marquette Golden Eagles and the Milwaukee Bucks. He is active in his church and has devoted time in judging the regional high school mock trial competitions.

Ashley received her Juris Doctor, cum laude, from Marquette University in 2021. During law school, Ashley served various Milwaukee organizations through the Marquette Volunteer Legal Clinic, including the Milwaukee Justice Center, the United Community Center, the House of Peace, and the Domestic Violence Clinic. In recognition of her services, Ashley was inducted into Marquette's Pro Bono Society.

While attending law school, Ashley also served as an associate editor on the Marquette Law Review and an associate justice on Marquette's Moot Court Board. She honed her advocacy skills by participating in the Jenkins Honors Moot Court Competition and the William B. Spong Moot Court Tournament. In the Jenkins competition, she and her team reached the semifinal round and were awarded second-place overall brief.

In her first year out of law school, Ashley worked at an insurance defense firm in Milwaukee. There, she learned a great deal about the procedure of a personal injury case from the perspective of an insurance company. She now focuses her practice on plaintiff-side personal injury. She is admitted to practice law in the State of Wisconsin and the federal Eastern and Western Districts of Wisconsin.

Ashley lives in Greenfield, Wisconsin, and enjoys listening to live music, reading, and exploring local parks.

attorneys.bio:
Attorney Randy Rozek has devoted his entire professional career to representing individuals against big corporations and insurance companies. Mr. Rozek is licensed in Wisconsin; however, he has handled cases throughout the United States. He has successfully represented injury victims from Alaska to Florida. Attorney Rozek graduated from the University of Wisconsin Law School in 1996 and has been representing personal injury victims since that time. In 2004, he founded his own office, Rozek Law Offices, and has focused his practice on the representation of victims of serious, life-changing injuries. Attorney Rozek takes great pride in the opportunity to help his clients rebuild their lives following their unfortunate injuries. Randy has worked with some of the leading experts around the world in fields of medicine and law. He currently serves on the Board of the Traumatic Brain Injury Litigation Group of the American Association for Justice and is the editor of the Journal of Traumatic Brain Injury Litigation.

Professional Associations

Attorney Rozek belongs to a number of diverse medical-legal professional associations. The majority of these associations involve the sharing of cutting-edge information among lawyers and physicians throughout the United States. Attorney Rozek is routinely asked to speak to these lawyers and doctors in order to educate them on such issues, particularly in the area of representing victims of Traumatic Brain Injury. •Brain Injury Association of America

Mr. Rozek is licensed in Wisconsin; however, he has handled cases throughout the United States. He has successfully represented injury victims from Alaska to Florida. Attorney Rozek graduated from the University of Wisconsin Law School in 1996 and has been representing personal injury victims since that time. In 2004, he founded his own office, Rozek Law Offices, and has focused his practice on the representation of victims of serious, life-changing injuries. Attorney Rozek takes great pride in the opportunity to help his clients rebuild their lives following their unfortunate injuries. Randy has worked with some of the leading experts around the world in fields of medicine and law. He currently serves on the Board of the Traumatic Brain Injury Litigation Group of the American Association for Justice and is the editor of the Journal of Traumatic Brain Injury Litigation.

Professional Associations

Attorney Rozek belongs to a number of diverse medical-legal professional associations. The majority of these associations involve the sharing of cutting-edge information among lawyers and physicians throughout the United States. Attorney Rozek is routinely asked to speak to these lawyers and doctors in order to educate them on such issues, particularly in the area of representing victims of Traumatic Brain Injury. The following are just some of the professional advocacy groups to which Attorney Rozek belongs:

•Brain Injury Association of America

•Brain Injury Alliance of Wisconsin

•North American Brain Injury Society

• American Association for Justice – TBI Litigation Group, Interstate Trucking Litigation Group, Complex Regional Pain Syndrome/Reflex Sympathetic Dystrophy (CRPS/RSD) Litigation Group

attorneys.name: Daniel H. Sanders
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Prior to joining the firm of Kohler & Hart, SC in May 2013, Daniel H. Sanders was a federal criminal prosecutor in the Eastern District of Wisconsin for 14 ½ years. Prior to becoming a federal prosecutor, Dan was a state criminal prosecutor in Columbus, Ohio for 7 years. As a federal prosecutor, Dan investigated and prosecuted a wide variety of federal crimes, including organized crime, public corruption, fraud, money laundering, RICO, immigration fraud, war crimes, drug trafficking, bank robbery, rape, kidnapping, and homicide. Many of Dan's federal cases required the use and analysis of complex financial documents, wiretaps, and other electronic surveillance. Dan has extensive experience in complex criminal pre-trial litigation and procedures, and sentencing issues. Dan was the lead counsel in dozens of federal and state jury trials with conviction rate over 95%. He has also argued numerous cases before 7th Circuit Court of Appeals.

During part of his tenor as a federal prosecutor in the Eastern District of Wisconsin, Dan was the Lead Attorney for the Organized Crime Drug Enforcement Task Force (OCDETF) and the Narcotics Chief who supervised the investigation and prosecution of all federal narcotics-related crimes emanating from the district.

Dan also worked on several immigration fraud cases in close coordination with the Human Rights Violators & War Crimes Unit of ICE, the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia (ICTY), and the Special Department for War Crimes of The Prosecutor's Office of Bosnia and Herzegovina (BiH). These cases involved U.S. immigration violations by individuals suspected of committing war crimes in the Balkans during the early to mid-1990s. To gather sufficient evidence for successful criminal prosecution and ultimate deportation, Dan worked closely with prosecutors at the ICTY and in Sarajevo, including investigative travel to the ICTY in The Hague, Netherlands and Sarajevo, BiH.

As a state court prosecutor in Ohio, Dan prosecuted all felony crimes, including capital offenses.

Dan earned his Bachelor's degree from Washington State University in 1987 and his law degree from the Moritz College of Law at the The Ohio State University in 1990.

Dan is licensed to practice before Wisconsin State and Federal District Courts, as well as the Seventh Circuit Court of Appeals and the Ohio State Courts.

Dan's professional accomplishments include the Director's Award for Superior Performance as an Assistant U.S. Attorney in 2008, the Wisconsin Association of Homicide Investigators Meritorious Service Award, 2010, and the Department of Justice Seal from U.S. Attorney General Janet Reno for prosecution of the Short North Posse in 1996.

attorneys.bio:
I am a solo practitioner with a passion for justice. I have been practicing law for over 30 years. I work hard on every case and approach each one, large or small, with a determination to get the best results possible. I relish representing the "Davids" against the "Goliaths" and have successfully taken on cases against large corporations, insurance companies, governments, and government officials, including police officers.

Communication between my clients and me is a priority, and I work together with my clients to master the details of their cases while always keeping the big picture in focus. I keep my clients informed at all stages of a case and take the time necessary to thoroughly prepare my clients and their witnesses for depositions and trial testimony.

Discriminatory treatment and harassment of employees, abuse by police and other governmental authorities, and negligent conduct that injures others—these are the wrongful acts that motivate me to pursue justice for those whose rights have been violated and who have been injured.

attorneys.name: Daniel J. Schlichting
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Across his practice areas, Dan Schlichting excels at finding solutions that work for all sides. He judges the range of possible outcomes, assesses where clients are in that range and helps to bring resolution. An empathetic - but matter-of-fact - manner and an ability to lay out the plain facts is an asset to business and family cases where emotion can cloud the best path.

On Hurley, Burish & Stanton:

"There's a certain feel here. We're down-to-earth. I think we're very good at discussing issues with clients, even in trying times. We communicate, then we review to be sure they understand."

On understanding:

"First, you need to really hear what people want. Having empathy helps for clients in hard times. Lastly, understand that people have common responses to situations – good advice is tempered with that outside perspective.

Emphasis

Dan has advised and assisted clients in a variety of areas, including:

Planning for business succession through the creation and use of shareholder agreements, split-dollar insurance agreements, family limited partnerships, cross-purchase and redemption agreements.

Negotiating business purchases and sales.

Preparation of wills and revocable living trusts to obtain a superior tax position.

Estate planning for disabled and elderly clients to protect assets.

Negotiating and drafting commercial real estate purshases and leases.

Creating limited liability companies and limited partnerships to transfer wealth to succeeding (younger) generations.

Preparing business to business contracts.

Creation and utilization of trusts to effectuate family wealth transfers to succeeding generations, including irrevocable insurance trusts and generation-skipping trusts.

Utilizing marital agreements in conjunction with living trusts to transfer wealth with minimum taxation exposure.

Planning for charitable giving through the use of charitable lead trusts and charitable remainder trusts.

Dan counsels a variety of corporate and individual clients with their business, estate planning and family law needs. His experience in business law enables him to provide estate planning that complements a person's business objectives.

attorneys.bio:
My practice is primarily litigation based, but whenever possible I strive to help my clients find alternatives to hashing out their disputes before the court. As an attorney I strive to first make sure that my clients understand all their options, and foreseeable outcomes, before we choose a plan for resolving their legal issues. Inevitably, there is frequently no workable alternative to litigation – and whether you need my assistance because you are charged with a crime or OWI, a party to a contested estate, in a dispute with a neighbor, or feel that you have been damaged by the acts of another – I will be there to assist you, advise you, and fight for you to obtain the best results we can as a team.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Sarah concentrates on two areas of practice: criminal and traffic defense and immigration law. In the area of criminal and traffic defense, Sarah has defended clients on all levels - from local municipal courts through the Seventh Circuit Court of Appeals.

Sarah handles many circuit court trials every year, successfully protecting client interests. Sarah handles all levels of appeal in criminal and traffic cases and has argued several cases in front of the Wisconsin Supreme Court.

Sarah frequently handles charges of drunk driving, sexual assault, substantial battery, theft from employer, delivery of controlled substances, and all types of criminal and traffic offenses.

In the area of immigration, Sarah frequently handles family petitions as well as defending those in removal proceedings. Sarah often consults to provide information to clients and other attorneys about immigration law and the best plan for moving forward.

attorneys.name: Scott A. Schmidlkofer
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Wauwatosa, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Scott A. Schmidlkofer is a lifelong resident of the State of Wisconsin who served in the United States Navy from 1988 to 1992 and saw active duty during operation Desert Storm/Shield. Schmidlkofer was highly decorated during his time in the Navy, including receiving the Southwest Asia Service Medal with a Bronze Star, the Armed Forces Expeditionary Medal for his role in rescuing victims of the Mount Pinatubo disaster, the Sailor of the Year Award for 1991, and a personal citation from the Admiral of the Seventh Fleet for outstanding performance during the Gulf War.

Upon the completion of his active military duty, Schmidlkofer attended the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee where he received a degree in 1998 (BA History). Attorney Schmidlkofer received his law degree from Marquette University (JD, 2001), where he was a Moot Court member and delivered the Valediction to his graduating class. Attorney Schmidlkofer has been involved in municipal traffic defense in nearly every community in southeastern Wisconsin. He is a member of the Waukesha County Bar Association and the State Bar of Wisconsin.

attorneys.name: Thomas J. Schneck
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Offices of Andrew C. Ladd, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Lawyers in Waukesha, WI
attorneys.bio:
Thomas J. Schneck is an associate with the law firm. He began practicing law in 1987, and has been practicing in Southeastern Wisconsin his entire career. He has been associated with Andrew C. Ladd since February, 2005. He is a general practitioner concentrating in the areas of family law, criminal law, traffic, bankruptcy and civil litigation. He has appeared in federal and state courts all over the State of Wisconsin, and has significant trial and courtroom experience.

While he possesses the technical expertise in the courtroom, he also approaches the practice of law in a holistic sense. He advises clients not only what they can do, but also on that they should do based on what is best for the client from a big-picture point of view. He understands that no one really wants to have an attorney involved in their lives, but would want an attorney who will candidly assess their matter and provide the necessary advice and services to achieve their goals in a cost-effective manner.

He has successfully represented clients charged with crimes and traffic violations. He has achieved client goals in custody and family law matters. He has successfully obtained debt relief for his bankruptcy clients. Because of his broad practice experience, he is able to advise clients whose matters are not solely limited to one area of the law (for example, a divorce client facing criminal charges or debt problems).

attorneys.name: Jolene D. Schneider
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce and Family Law Lawyers in Neenah, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Jolene Schneider brings a personalized touch and customized approach to the practice of family law. With nearly three decades of experience, she honed her focus, skills, and tenacity to help clients navigate through highly complex legal issues. Her extensive courtroom experience, coupled with her training as a Mediator and Arbitrator, allows her to utilize all available legal tools to secure the best possible outcomes for her clients.

She exclusively practices family law, meaning that her professional energy is solely devoted to maintaining the highest standards of excellence in assisting clients with issues related to divorce, legal separation, spousal maintenance, child support, child custody disputes, and other family law matters.

Attorney Schneider is proud to be recognized in "Super Lawyers" and "The Best Lawyers in America." Her commitment to the field extends beyond her practice; she is an active member of the State Bar of Wisconsin and serves on the Board of Directors for the Family Law Section. Additionally, she contributes as an Editor of the Wisconsin Journal of Family Law and previously served on the State Bar of Wisconsin Fee Arbitration Panel. Her role as a leader in the legal community includes authoring articles and presenting on various legal topics.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Attorney Amy C. Scholz has earned her reputation as one of the top rising criminal defense attorneys in Milwaukee and Waukesha. Named a “Wisconsin Rising Star” by Super Lawyers, and also recognized by The National Trial Lawyers Association as a “Top 40 Under 40” in Wisconsin and a “Top 100 Trial Lawyer”, she continues to earn accolades for the work she does for her clients.

Amy puts her experience as a State Criminal Prosecutor to work by aggressively representing her clients both inside and outside the courtroom. Whether through aggressive negotiations with the prosecuting attorney, filing pre-trial motions aimed at having evidence suppressed, or zealous arguments at trial, Amy is incredibly skilled at getting charges dropped or significantly reduced!

Amy Scholz has a proven track record of achieving positive outcomes for her clients. She has successfully negotiated reductions of both felony and misdemeanor charges, as well as outright dismissals. Where reductions in charges were not attainable, Attorney Scholz has achieved significantly reduced penalties for her clients, ranging from fines only on felony charges to time-served dispositions. She has also successfully earned findings of Not Guilty at trial on offenses ranging from OWIs to Sexual Assault. Amy Scholz is a well-respected trial attorney with a track record of success who is not afraid to fight for the results that her clients deserve.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Manitowoc, WI
attorneys.bio:
Joseph Schuh was born and raised in Manitowoc County. He grew up on a beef cattle farm in Francis Creek and milked cows in his teen years at his uncles dairy farm, also in Francis Creek. A graduate of Mishicot High School, Joe always had ambitions to give back to his community. Joe's legal practice is family law which includes, but not limited to, Divorce, Legal Separation, Child Support, Paternity Acknowledgment and Guardian ad Litem work.

In law school Joe worked as a clinical student in the Family Court Clinic for three semesters, assisting those in Dane and the surrounding counties with their family law matters. In Joe's free time he enjoys spending time with his family, cat and is a big fan of stand-up comedy.

Joe holds an Associate of Arts & Science Degree, Magna Cum Laude from the University of Wisconsin Manitowoc, a Bachelor of Arts Degree in Democracy & Justice Studies from the University of Wisconsin Green Bay, Cum Laude, and a Juris Doctor from the University of Wisconsin Law School.

Al devotes much of his practice to counseling employers on difficult day-to-day issues that span the vast array of employment laws – but is a zealous advocate once those issues become the basis of litigation.

attorneys.name: Sheila L. Shadman Emerson
attorneys.practice_type: Construction Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Sheila is an associate attorney at Halloin Law Group, S.C., licensed in both Illinois and Wisconsin. Her practice focuses on business, construction, and real estate litigation, and insurance recovery.

Sheila has achieved notable success advocating on behalf of her clients who are dealing with highly complex, pressing legal challenges. At all turns, she delivers the personalized attention her clients deserve while working aggressively to help them obtain the favorable results they expect for their legal matters as efficiently and cost-effectively as possible.

While attending Marquette University Law School, Sheila participated in the Street Law Program, in which she taught high school students substantive law and led her class to victory at a citywide mock trial competition in Milwaukee. Sheila then served as an Adjunct Assistant Professor at the Marquette University Law School, where she was as a Director of the Street Law Program for ten years.

Sheila has been selected by Super Lawyers to the 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, and 2023 Wisconsin Rising Stars list. Super Lawyers, part of Thomson Reuters, honors attorneys who exhibit excellence in the practice of law. Every year, attorneys are selected through a multiphase process based on nominations, independent research and peer evaluations. The Rising Stars designation from Super Lawyers represents only 2.5% of all licensed attorneys in the state of Wisconsin.

In her free time, Sheila enjoys traveling, running, and spending time with her family.

attorneys.name: Todd Simon
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Lawyers in Green Bay, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Todd Simon has been recognized as one of the top attorneys in Wisconsin for 5 of the past 10 years, representing clients in felony and misdemeanor criminal cases, as well as OWI cases. Online reviews of Todd Simon consistently call him one of the top defense attorneys in the area.

Attorney Simon has the knowledge and experience to represent clients in matters ranging from drunk driving or OWI cases to very complex domestic violence cases, property crimes, and drug related cases.

Having several years of experience handling hundreds of criminal cases, many of which have resulted in reduced charges, outright dismissals, and not guilty verdicts by juries, Attorney Simon has a reputation in the legal community as an aggressive advocate for his clients. His experience has even found him in the media handling a number of high profile cases.

Attorney Simon has also earned the distinction of "Top 100 Trial Lawyers" for the state of Wisconsin by the National Trial Lawyers along with "Top 40 Under 40" and "Rising Star" by Superlawyers magazine. Awards such as these are handed out to only the top attorneys in their field of practice and these awards recognize Attorney Simon as one of the top criminal defense attorneys in the state.

Todd Simon also represents clients in family law related matters including, custody, divorce, and placement cases. Mr. Simon has a great deal of experience in handling difficult family law matters and has experience as a Guardian ad Litem for Brown County. Attorney Simon is also an experienced advocate for grandparent rights.

Attorney Simon's previous experience was as an associate attorney with a well established law firm in Green Bay. Todd also served as an intern for a Wisconsin Circuit Court Judge prior to entering into private practice.

When Todd's not zealously advocating for his client's rights, he enjoys spending time with his wife and their two children, reading, playing golf, and cheering on the Green Bay Packers.

attorneys.name: Holly Slota
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Holly Slota is a Partner with the firm's Family Law Practice Group. She has been practicing law since 2003 and joined the firm in 2016.

Holly concentrates her practice in divorce litigation, collaborative divorce, appellate practice, international child abduction cases. She also serves as a Guardian ad litem in family law matters. Holly volunteers at the Dane County Family Law Assistance Center. Ms. Slota is licensed to practice in the State of Wisconsin.

Holly was recognized as a Rising Star in Wisconsin Super Lawyers in 2010, 2011, and 2013 and was selected to Super Lawyers 2019-2022. Recent publications include Eckhardt’s Workbook for Wisconsin Estate Planners (coauthor, 2014 and 2016) and Preventing and Responding to International Child Abduction, American Journal of Family Law, Vol. 23, No. 2 (Summer 2009). She also served as the Wisconsin delegate at the 20th Annual Symposium of the Family Law Council of Community Property States in Albuquerque, New Mexico, where she presented a paper entitled “Back to the Basics: Overview of Community Property in Wisconsin.” She has served as faculty for the Divorce Proceedings section of the UW Law School’s Lawyering Skills Program and has been a guest presenter at the law school’s Family Law I course and Domestic Violence Seminar. She has also trained domestic violence advocates about the role that guardians ad litem play in family law cases involving domestic violence at the Wisconsin Coalition Against Domestic Violence’s Family and Immigration Law Training.

Holly’s extensive appellate practice in the area of family law has yielded several published decisions including Chen v. Warner, 2005 WI 55, 280 Wis. 2d 344, 695 N.W.2d 758, and Wright v. Wright, 2008 WI App 21, 307 Wis. 2d 156, 747 N.W.2d 690. In 2015, she presented at the State Bar of Wisconsin’s Guardian ad Litem training regarding the role and duties of guardians ad litem on appeal.

attorneys.bio: Todd focuses on impaired driving (alcohol and drugs) and as well as other criminal matters. While in law school, Todd was a member of the Law Review. After graduating from law school, Todd was a law clerk for the Tennessee Court of Appeals where he worked for the Honorable David Farmer. After his clerkship, Todd worked for the firm of Hanover, Walsh, Jalenak and Blair, PLLC, in Memphis. The firm later merged to become Harris Shelton Hanover Walsh, PLLC. While working in Memphis, Todd practiced in both State and Federal Courts. Upon moving to Wisconsin, Todd continued his practice in both State and Federal Courts, shifting his focus to impaired driving defense. Todd is a member of the Wisconsin Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, and the National College for DUI Defense. Todd is a veteran of the United States Navy Submarine Force, and is retired from the Army Reserve JAGC. He has a proven track record of success in defending impaired driving cases. Todd is a rabid Memphis Tigers college basketball fan, with the Badgers coming in a close second. Todd also enjoys golfing in his free time.

attorneys.name: Ronald J Sonderhouse
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal/Traffic Law Lawyers in Waukesha, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Ronald Sonderhouse has over 25 years of legal experience. He is a well respected attorney within the Waukesha County Court system and was given the backing of many Judges, the District Attorney and the Sheriff of Waukesha County when he ran for a Waukesha County Judge position.

Ron graduated from the University of Detroit School of Law in 1990. He obtained a Bachelors of Arts Degree in Business from Michigan State University in 1987. While attending law school, Ron also received a Master's Degree in Business.

Ron began his legal career in Allegan, Michigan in 1991 where he worked as an Associate for the Allegan Law Offices. Ron represented a wide range of clients in business, family and criminal matters. In 1999 Ron moved to Pewaukee, Wisconsin and began working at Kay & Kay Law Firm, again representing a diverse client base. In 2008, Ron formed a partnership with Peter Wolff under the firm name of Wolff & Sonderhouse, LLP. Ron continues to represent clients in various matters including criminal, family, probate and juvenile law. Throughout his legal career, Ron has held various leadership positions and has been a member of legal and community organizations. Ron served as President of the Allegan County Bar Association, President of the Allegan County Chapter of Kiwanis and a Board Member of the Allegan County Substance Abuse Agency. Ron continued that practice here in Wisconsin, as he has held the position of President for the Waukesha County Bar Association and the Waukesha County Chapter of Kiwanis International. He has served as Supplemental Court Commissioner for the Honorable Linda M. Van De Water and is currently serving the same position for the Honorable Paul Bugenhagen, Jr. Ron also volunteers his time to the Mediation Restorative Justice Center and the Waukesha County Family Law Clinic.

Ron has been married to his wife, Debra, for over 22 years and has a step-daughter, Monica, who resides in New York. Ron's parents moved from Michigan to Delafield, Wisconsin a few years ago, where his father, Ron, is still residing. Ron has one brother, Randy, who resides with his wife in California. In his spare time Ron enjoys scuba diving, playing golf and volunteering in the community.

attorneys.bio:
I have argued cases before the Wisconsin Supreme Court; the Wisconsin Court of Appeals; the Illinois Court of Appeals; and the Federal Seventh Circuit Court of Appeals.

I was appointed by the Governor of Wisconsin five times to the Wisconsin State Elections Board and I served as its Chairman for a term. I was appointed to the City of South Milwaukee Police and Fire Commission where I served as Secretary and later President. I also was appointed to the City of South Milwaukee Housing Authority.

I was elected to five terms as the Chair of the Milwaukee County Democratic Party serving for ten years. I also was elected and severed as the First Vice Chair and later Chair of the Wisconsin Democratic Party. I served on the Democratic National Committee, as well as the National Chairs' Association. I chaired and led Wisconsin's Delegation to the Democratic National Convention in 1996.

I previously served on the Board of Directors for the Wisconsin Arthritis Organization. I also served on the Wisconsin Law School's Board of Visitors.

I enjoy photography. Along with my daughter Samantha, we designed and care for the flower displays and holiday decorations at the office. The office is active in the local Elkhorn Chamber of Commerce. We have entered and won for our floats in the city's annual Christmas parade. We help sponsor local teams, the recreation department, fire departments educational programs etc. We decorate our 150 year old office for Halloween and are active in the neighborhoods celebration of the event.

My wife and I have been married for over forty-five years. We have two adult children and we love pets. We usually have a large collie who is always my best friend and travels with me on weekends for errands, etc. Our current collie is "Flash." We have rescue cats as well.

attorneys.name: Scott Harold Southworth
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal and Civil Defense Lawyers in Wisconsin Dells, WI
attorneys.bio:
Scott Southworth graduated with Distinction from UW-Madison with a Bachelor of Arts degree in 1994 and received his Juris Doctor with Honors from the University of Wisconsin Law School in 1997 with emphases in Constitutional Law and Juvenile Justice.

In 2004, Scott Southworth was elected District Attorney for Juneau County, in Mauston, WI, where he prosecuted homicides, crimes against children and other major felonies. In 2010, Scott helped spearhead the effort to create Veterans Treatment Courts around Wisconsin to address criminal behavior by veterans directly connected to their combat service.

In 2000 Scott served as the lead plaintiff in the landmark U.S. Supreme Court decision in Southworth v. The Board of Regents of the University of Wisconsin.

Scott serves as a Military Police Officer with the Wisconsin Army National Guard in the rank of Major. Scott Southworth served as the commander of four separate units, to include the 32nd Military Police Company. He led the 32nd on a deployment to the Middle East in support of Operation Iraqi Freedom, maintaining responsibility for the rebuilding of the Iraqi Police Service (IPS) in northeast Baghdad in 2003-2004. Scott personally captured the commanding general of the Iraqi Army in charge of Baghdad during the war and established a new training program for Iraqi police investigators. For exceptional wartime service, he received the Bronze Star Medal, the Combat Action Badge, Military Outstanding Volunteer Service Medal, Iraq Campaign Medal and Global War on Terrorism Service Medal.

During his military service in Iraq, Scott met Ala'a Eddeen, a 10-year old boy with cerebral palsy at the Mother Teresa orphanage in Baghdad. In 2005, he returned to Iraq to bring Ala'a to the U.S. and later adopted him. In 2012, Scott adopted 7-year old Rumen, an orphan from Bulgaria.

Currently Scott Southworth works as a criminal defense lawyer and adoption lawyer in the Mauston / Wisconsin Dells area. He is willing to represent clients with criminal related issues in the counties of Juneau, Monroe, Marquette, Sauk, Jackson and Adams.

attorneys.name: David K. Sparr
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Oshkosh, WI
attorneys.bio:
Dave Sparr is a long time resident of Oshkosh. He attended Oshkosh High School (now Oshkosh West) and graduated from the University of Wisconsin Oshkosh before obtaining his law degree from the University of Wisconsin Law School. Dave has been practicing law in Oshkosh since 1978. He and his wife, Diane, live in Oshkosh. Their two children, Eric, who also graduated from law school at UW-Madison, and Jessica, who is a business analyst in Minneapolis also grew up in Oshkosh. Dave has been a member or chair of the Downtown Oshkosh Business Employment Improvement District since 2000.

Dave and his wife, Diane, fell in love with Madison while attending grad school and law school. We came to Madison many weekends over the years for activities, such as the Great Taste of the Midwest, arts events, sports events, and the Saturday Farmers market, for restaurants, and for bicycling on Madison's great bike trails. We purchased a condo in 2009 so we could spend more time in Madison versus traveling to other cities for bike trips and entertainment and operated a branch law office there for 10 years. We still handle personal injury claims from the Madison area.

Our firm consists of a team of lawyers and assistants who are dedicated to the principle of people helping people. Unlike many trial law firms, we do not represent insurance companies. Our firm is always available to provide information and advice to clients.

Dave serves as an arbitrator in personal injury cases and is a member of the Winnebago County Bar Association, the State Bar of Wisconsin, the City of Oshkosh Business Improvement District, the Wisconsin Association for Justice, and acts as local referral counsel for the National Education Association and the Wisconsin Education Association Council Attorney Referral program. Dave has testified as an expert in farm accident and legal malpractice cases.

Our motto of WE CAN HELP is taken seriously by all firm members. Contact our office to speak with a law firm that genuinely cares about you. We look forward to helping!

attorneys.bio:
I graduated from law school in 1983. I clerked for a Federal Judge. After clerking for a Federal Judge in the Eastern District of Missouri, I went to work for an insurance defense firm. I never felt comfortable in the insurance defense industry and knew my heart and my mind were not with the insurance companies.

In 1989, I started Stanford Law Offices, S.C. Since 1989 to the present, we have handled thousands of claims, lawsuits, hearings, arbitrations and trials, representing our clients.

Personally, I consider being hired an honor and a privilege. I cannot think of a higher honor than to have an injured person trust us with their case. I embrace their cause with passion and look forward to working for them.

My personal interests include bagpiping, hunting, bicycling and playing tennis.

I encourage everyone to view our testimonials, reviews and accomplishments.

For a free consultation, please contact us at 414-276-8269 or email directly at PAS@StanfordLawOffices.com.

attorneys.name: Marie A. Stanton
attorneys.practice_type: Mediation Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Marie Stanton is one of the most experienced and respected mediators/litigators in Wisconsin. She gained trial experience early, trying 30 jury cases to verdict as an Assistant District Attorney. Her civil litigation/trial work has included representing clients in injury claims, insurance disputes, business, health care, and property claims. Marie continues to represent licensed professionals before the Boards of Medicine, Nursing, Chiropractic, Insurance, and Psychology, as well as attorneys, in conduct and other administrative claims.

Since 1993, Marie has mediated cases statewide, working both with Wisconsin and out of state counsel. She receives over 100 requests annually to mediate or arbitrate disputed matters. Marie thrives on the challenge of complex, multi-party cases but is equally attentive to claims between private parties. She involves counsel in pre-mediation conferences to identify issues and organize the process to promote efficiency. She will continue her involvement in negotiations beyond the mediation day to reach settlement. Her success as a mediator is well known, with attorneys across the state returning to mediate a diverse range of cases in size, type and complexity.

Her career has many firsts, including Wisconsin's first woman admitted to the American College of Trial Lawyers and the first woman invited to join the Wisconsin Chapter of the American Board of Trial Advocates.

attorneys.name: Craig Steger
attorneys.firm_name: Craig Steger - The Trucking Lawyer - Hale Skemp Hanson Skemp & Sleik
attorneys.practice_type: Truck Accidents Lawyers in La Crosse, WI
attorneys.bio:
Craig Steger has been fighting for injured motorists, truck drivers, farmers, and their families for over 20 years. Licensed in Wisconsin, Minnesota, and Iowa, Craig focuses his practice on serious personal injury and wrongful death cases involving commercial trucks, farm equipment, and other heavy machinery. He understands the risks drivers and farmers face every day — both on the road and in the fields — and he is committed to holding negligent companies, manufacturers, and insurance carriers accountable.

Craig’s experience spans state and federal courts throughout the Midwest, and he has handled cases before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit and is admitted to practice before the U.S. Supreme Court. He knows how to stand up to large corporations and insurers, and he is not afraid to take a case to trial when justice requires it.

Craig’s connection to trucking and farming isn’t just professional — it’s personal. He grew up dairy farming and beef ranching, and now lives with his wife and nine children on their small farm in western Wisconsin, where he raises his own beef, cuts firewood, and works the land. He also holds a Class A Commercial Driver’s License, with air brakes and manual transmission endorsements, giving him firsthand knowledge of the challenges truck drivers face on the road.

When he’s not in the courtroom or on the farm, Craig enjoys deer hunting, fishing and doing CrossFit. His dedication to hard work and discipline in all areas of life carries over to how he fights for his clients: with grit, honesty, and relentless effort.

attorneys.name: Deborah A. Stencel
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Law Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Deborah is a Wisconsin Native (born to the grandchildren of immigrants who landed in Wisconsin just after statehood) and a Southern Transplant (having spent about 20 years in North Carolina earning her degrees and enjoying proper barbecue). Deborah returned to America's Dairyland in 2010 to practice law, grow vegetables, and to nag her fiancé to clean up after their 2 dogs and 2 cats (all rescues, of course).

Deborah enjoyed a college term in the Soviet Union at the end of the Cold War and brief study tour of the institutions of the European Union during law school. Before the law, she was employed as a comedian, an organizational consultant (i.e., closet designer), and freelance author.

Deborah's bachelor degree in political science qualifies her to say "hmm" and "interesting" during presidential debates (NC State, 1997) but her law degree -earned from the University of North Carolina in 2001 - enables her to help and to counsel Wisconsin consumers about their debts, their rights, and their options. She considers it her honor to guide her clients through the legal process to find the results which help them look forward to a better future after debt - be this through Bankruptcy, Chapter 128, or foreclosure defense.

Deborah has received awards for her pro bono work and volunteers her time at Wills for Heroes and the Volunteer Lawyers Project. She also supports the Becky Werner Meningitis Foundation and the Michael J Fox Foundation for Parkinson's Research. In her free time, Deborah likes to make clunky, beaded jewelry, rescue dying houseplants, and scour thrift shops for that last original copy of the Declaration of Independence.

attorneys.name: George B. Strother IV
attorneys.practice_type: General Civil Litigation Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
George B. (Gard) Strother IV has been a principal shareholder at Krekeler Strother, S.C. since shortly after joining the firm in 1995. Before this, he practiced law for 15 years as a shareholder at his previous law firm. He devotes a substantial portion of his practice to employment law, assisting clients with issues including employment discrimination, licensure, employment discipline and termination, workers compensation benefits, unemployment benefits, and employment contracts. He assists clients with general civil litigation involving business and other contract matters, and select family law cases. He also addresses the basic estate planning and probate needs of the firm’s clientele.

Mr.Strother has approximately 35 years of civil and criminal litigation experience. He has served as lead trial counsel in upwards of 90-100 cases tried to juries in Dane County and neighboring counties. He has tried a far greater number of cases to courts and administrative agencies. Cases tried, in addition to numerous employment-related disputes, have included first-degree murder, numerous felony and misdemeanor cases, divorce and family cases, traffic offences, personal injury, contract and other business disputes, contested probate, and juvenile court proceedings. He has served as lead counsel in upwards of 30 cases in the Wisconsin Court of Appeals and the Wisconsin Supreme Court.

The geographical reach of his practice has included counties throughout southern Wisconsin including Columbia, Dane, Dodge, Grant, Iowa, Jefferson, LaFayette, Milwaukee, Richland, Rock, Sauk, Walworth, and Waukesha, as well as numerous state and federal administrative agencies, including the Wisconsin Department of Workforce Development, the Wisconsin Department of Regulation and Licensing, the U.S. Merit Systems Protection Board, and the U.S. Tax Court.

attorneys.name: Jessica A. Swain
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
While traveling from her first job to her second job, a working mother of six children was t-boned by a truck in the middle of an intersection. In this moment, her life abruptly changed. When we first met, it was immediately evident this caring, productive, hardworking parent was broken and scared by her suddenly uncertain future. As she trusted me to restore her life, I quickly became a constant source of dependable emotional support and stability. As her case matured and her injuries healed, I forced the insurance company responsible to take her story seriously. Ultimately, by way of thoughtful and strategic representation, she was significantly compensated.

Dependable, reliable, efficient, effective, competitive, and results-driven—I pursue each case with these values in mind. From a young age, I chased competition. attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Waukesha, WI
attorneys.bio:
Kris grew up in the Seattle area. After graduating from the University of Washington in 1988, she attended law school at Marquette Law School in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, and obtained a Juris Doctorate in 1991.

​Kris began practicing law in Lansing, Michigan, but returned back to Wisconsin in 1994 and began growing her family practice. In 1997, she helped form the law firm of Brazil, Thelen & Benske, S.C. When the firm decided to take alternate paths, the law firm of Thelen & Flink, LLC was launched.

Kris practices in all of the courts of Southeastern Wisconsin handling all family law matters, including child support, custody, placement and visitation. She also handles cases involving alimony (maintenance), property division, pre-nuptials/ante-nuptial agreements and cohabitation. She has also handled numerous matters before the Wisconsin Court of Appeals and the Wisconsin Supreme Court.

Kris is a member of the family sections of the Wisconsin Bar Association, the Waukesha County Bar Association, Society of Family Lawyers and Wisconsin Association of Mediators. She was also named a "Wisconsin Super Lawyer" in an evaluation by her peers.

attorneys.name: Lydia N. Thompson
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Lydia Thompson’s background reflects a wide range of professional experiences from the legal, higher education, non-profit, and government industries where she focused on regulations, policies, and procedures. At Murphy Desmond, Lydia works on the litigation and professional licensing teams, handles collections, and assists with business law matters, including business-related contracts and review.

Earlier in her career, Lydia worked at the Wisconsin Department of Safety & Professional Services, where she served as a Prosecutor representing the state in disciplinary matters before administrative law judges and state boards and litigated disciplinary cases. She also provided legal counsel to the Department staff and 13 health and business professional state boards, which included drafting administrative rules, and assisting with credentialing/licensure and disciplinary determinations. In addition, she served victims of sexual abuse in a leadership role on the Kenosha County Sexual Assault Response Team.

Immediately following law school, Lydia served in the Dane County District Attorney’s Office as a Volunteer Special Prosecutor. Prior to receiving her law degree, Lydia served as a Judicial Extern to Wisconsin Supreme Court Justice Louis B. Butler, Jr., and as a law clerk in the Office of the City Attorney in Madison, Wisconsin.

Lydia is based in Murphy Desmond's Madison office but can assist clients throughout Wisconsin.

attorneys.name: Amanda K. Tisdale
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Prairie du Chien, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Amanda Tisdale is a native of Southwest Wisconsin, born and raised in rural Avoca. After graduating from Riverdale High School in 1999, Amanda attended UW Platteville earning a double major in Criminal Justice and Political Science. While at UW Platteville, Amanda completed an internship with the State Public Defender's office and was active with the Mock Trial team.

In 2007, Amanda earned her law degree from William Mitchell College of Law in St. Paul, Minnesota. While in law school, Amanda volunteered through the Minnesota Justice Foundation at Tubman Family Alliance and obtained certifications in Alternative Dispute Resolution and Mediation. After passing the Wisconsin Bar Exam, Amanda was hired to work in the Lancaster office of the Wisconsin State Public Defender as an Assistant State Public Defender. At the State Public Defender's Office, Amanda gained a tremendous volume of litigation experience defending criminal and OWI cases. In addition to criminal defense, Amanda's time with the State Public Defender exposed her to a wide variety of cases, allowing her to work with juveniles, assist the mentally ill in Chapter 51 proceedings, and represent wards in guardianships.

Amanda currently practices in the areas of criminal defense, OWI defense, family law, probate & estate planning, and real estate.

Amanda and her husband, Brent, live in rural Blue River with their two young daughters. Amanda enjoys spending time with her family, cooking, gardening, and running. Amanda volunteers with her church and is a member of the Prairie du Chien Rotary Club.

attorneys.name: Tracy N. Tool
attorneys.practice_type: Plaintiff's Personal Injury Litigation Lawyers in La Crosse, WI
attorneys.bio:
Tracy is a passionate and dedicated civil trial lawyer. He devotes his practice to people who have been injured or have had their rights violated.In more than thirty years as a lawyer, Tracy has learned that insurance companies and big corporations try to pay as little as they can, even on valid claims. Tracy uses the law to take the fight to the big companies, and to demand that they either settle claims fairly or face a jury trial.

Since law school, where he served as Articles Editor for the Minnesota Law Review, Tracy has firmly believed in the value of strong communication and teaching. He often lectures at seminars for other attorneys, makes presentations to college groups about liability and sports law, and has spent many years teaching as an adjunct professor at the University of Minnesota Law School. He received the NBI Outstanding Faculty award in 2022 and 2023. Tracy particularly enjoys helping coach the local high school mock trial team, which he’s done for over 20 years, helping young people learn how to think critically, to stand and argue in a competitive setting, and to emphasize teamwork and good communication skills as tools for success.

Tracy is a board-certified civil trial specialist who works in the state and federal courts of Wisconsin and Minnesota. Based on reviews by other lawyers, Tracy has been listed multiple times in Super Lawyers and Best Lawyers. Besides practicing law, he enjoys sports and outdoor activities such as running and golf, and often volunteers at fluid stations for the Twin Cities Marathon.He is a die-hard fan of the Minnesota Twins and the Minnesota Golden Gophers.

He represents businesses and individuals in contract and tort claims, including policyholders seeking coverage under insurance policies or employee benefit plans.

John has counseled clients and litigated ERISA and employee benefit cases in many areas, including life, health, and disability benefits, ESOP valuation disputes, COBRA rights and penalties, and severance and retirement disputes. John also represents licensed individuals involved in administrative actions before state and federal regulators, including the Wisconsin Office of the Commissioner of Insurance, the Department of Financial Institutions, and the U.S. Department of Labor.

attorneys.name: Ella Uylaki
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Uylaki, who comes from a proud Union background, has a passion for organizing and representing Unions and their members. Ella was a member of the Employment Law Society at Marquette Law School and she interned at the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) in Milwaukee where she aided in the investigation of unfair labor practices complaints and prepared finalized investigative reports regarding local labor issues.

In addition to her background with Union matters, Attorney Uylaki has a strong background in labor rights, contract drafting, and workplace disputes. Ms. Uylaki clerked with respected Chicago-based law firm, Arnold and Kadjan, LLC, where she focused on alter-ego labor law cases.

Selected for the Wisconsin Bar Association’s Diversity Clerkship Program in 2023, she clerked at Regal Rexnord where she focused on drafting third-party nondisclosure agreements and focused on contractual negotiations.

Ms. Uylaki was a writing tutor with the Norman H. Ott Writing Center while in school where she worked with students of a diverse background including, multilingual writers, advanced degree students, and community members entering academia.

Ella grew up in Northern Indiana where she became an avid painter and developed a deep appreciation for the arts. Both as an undergraduate and while at Marquette Law School, Ella hosted a weekly radio show.

attorneys.name: Becky N. Van Dam
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in West Bend, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Becky Van Dam has over 10 years of experience dedicated to litigating and protecting her clients’ rights. She focuses her practice in criminal defense, appellate law, traffic and restraining order/injunction cases. She understands the stress and uncertainty that individuals face when confronting legal challenges. She utilizes her background, skills, and comprehensive legal knowledge to guide clients through these difficult times. This guidance includes providing prompt communication, skillfully navigating the complexities of the legal system, and vigorously advocating on behalf of her clients.

Attorney Van Dam specializes in criminal defense. She has handled a wide range of criminal offenses, including: OWI’s, drug offenses, domestic violence, battery, robbery, theft, money laundering, fraud, property crimes, violent crimes, sexual assault and reckless homicide. She has a proven track record of success in obtaining favorable outcomes for her clients, including negotiating plea agreements, litigating legal issues and winning jury trials.

Her practice has a particular emphasis on handling OWI cases. She has successfully litigated a variety of issues on these types of cases, from challenging illegal traffic stops, blood draws and searches and seizures at motion hearings to presenting defenses and arguing proof problems at jury trials. Her efforts have resulted in numerous OWI cases being dismissed, amended or clients acquitted at trial.

Attorney Van Dam is also experienced in criminal appeals, where she has achieved success in both the circuit court and the court of appeals. She is skilled in legal research and writing. Her work has led to multiple clients being released from prison and having their convictions vacated. With a strong belief in fighting for her clients’ rights, Attorney Van Dam is dedicated to providing zealous legal representation.

In restraining order and injunction cases, she has attained a success rate of 76% in winning cases for her clients or reaching a favorable outcome. She has represented petitioners and respondents in domestic violence, harassment, child abuse and individual at-risk restraining orders. She has proven knowledge, skill, and experience in effectively handling these cases for her clients.

Attorney Van Dam has been consecutively selected to Wisconsin Super Lawyers’ Rising Stars List since 2021. This is a prestigious distinction that only the top 2.5% of attorneys in Wisconsin receive. Please call or email to request a consultation.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense and DUI Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Benjamin Van Severen is a criminal defense attorney who practices in Milwaukee and throughout the state of Wisconsin. He has experience handling all types of cases, from misdemeanors and OWI/DUI to serious felonies, including homicide, sexual assault, crimes involving firearms, and drug crimes. Focusing entirely on criminal defense, Attorney Van Severen has achieved an acquittal rate three times the state average.

Attorney Van Severen received his Bachelor of Arts degree from Marquette University in 2010, with majors in Political Science and Criminology, and a minor in Music. He then received his Juris Doctor from Marquette University Law School in 2013. While at Marquette, Attorney Van Severen amassed over 380 hours of pro bono work with the Marquette Volunteer Legal Clinic and the Wisconsin State Public Defender Trial Office in Green Bay.

Immediately upon his graduation from law school, Attorney Van Severen was hired at a local Milwaukee criminal defense firm. From his very first day, he displayed a passion for criminal defense inside the courtroom. His reputation of taking cases to trial has resulted in reduced charges and lower sentences in courts throughout Wisconsin.

In order to stay up to date on the constantly evolving legal landscape, Attorney Van Severen belongs to the Wisconsin Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, the Milwaukee Bar Association, the Milwaukee Young Lawyers Association, the American Bar Association, the Eastern District of Wisconsin Bar Association, and the State Bar of Wisconsin.

Van Severen Law Office, S.C. and Attorney Van Severen focus solely on criminal defense in Wisconsin. Based in Milwaukee, Attorney Van Severen defends cases throughout the state. Contact Attorney Van Severen today.
