attorneys.name: Christopher T. Van Wagner
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Christopher T. Van Wagner is one of the top all-around criminal defense attorneys in Wisconsin. He has nearly 35 years of legal experience (but maintains his youthful zeal – and a full head of hair).Van Wagner has a record of positive results for his clients. He has devoted the past 20+ years of law practice to defending people charged with serious crimes, including Sexual Assault, Homicide (DWI/OWI Homicide, Vehicular Homicide, Negligent Homicide), OWI (including Causing Injury by OWI, as well as First, Second, Third, or other repeat-OWI cases), Assault, Battery, Drug Charges, Controlled Substance Charges, Embezzlement, Wire Fraud, Bank/Mortgage Fraud, Criminal Damage to Property, and Theft.These cases can be difficult to defend, given the nature of the crimes and the instant and widespread negative public reaction to them. However, even if it means taking a false or unfounded case to a jury trial, Chris Van Wagner will do all in his power to ensure that justice is served for his clients.

Mr. Van Wagner brings a wealth of life experiences to his criminal law practice. As one of 11 children, Chris was raised in a middle-class Irish Catholic family in the grimy, working-class scrabble of Trenton, New Jersey. Those days in the streets gave him insights into how people act. He was always more interested in human nature than some heavy scholastic tome. Due to his East Coast roots, Chris remains an avid New York Yankees fan and Red Sox enemy. And yet, despite his hard knocks education in Trenton, where he learned how to think on his feet, Chris – like his father before him – paid his own way through college. He went to St. Lawrence (New York State), earning honors in English Literature (BA, 1978).After graduation, Mr. Van Wagner next paid and worked his way into an Ivy League law degree, at Cornell Law School, where he was named an Editor of the Law Review, a high academic honor reserved for the top ten percent of Cornell Law students. Then, after Cornell (JD, 1981), Mr. Van Wagner worked in as clerk for a federal judge, the late Hon. Dickinson Debevoise (US. District Court of NJ)

After one boring, uninspiring year in a large NJ firm, Chris worked as a county prosecutor (in Trenton, NJ). He cut his teeth there in the mid-80’s, where he tried more than 50 felony cases to final jury verdict.Then, after a brief stint at a downtown Chicago law firm (Mayer Brown on LaSalle Street), for the second time went back to his first love, criminal law, as a federal prosecutor in Madison, Wisconsin. He handled dozens of federal cases.

In 1994, Chris Van Wagner went back into private practice, this time to commit himself to the defense of ordinary, everyday people who are accused of crimes. He focuses on those people, handling felonies and misdemeanors in both state and federal court. He also defends many drunk-driving cases in every shape and size. Through all of this, Chris has earned a stellar reputation all over the “left side of the State of Wisconsin” as a trial lawyer, not a “plea lawyer.” Prosecutors know – or soon learn – that Chris will not fold when advised to do so by them.

As a result of his fearless approach, his professionalism, and his ethical state-wide reputation, Mr. Van Wagner has achieved many dismissals at the courthouse steps on the eve of trial, for clients charged with all sorts of crimes. He has managed to do so precisely because he has tried and won many jury acquittals, for clients who were wrongly accused of crimes, and for those whom the State sought to punish well beyond any logical need to do so.

Now, after more than 20 years successfully defending criminal charges and nearly 35 years of practicing law all told, Mr. Van Wagner has chosen to practice again as a solo practitioner. This allows him to spend all the time necessary to obtain the best possible result. Chris eschews the notion of a high-volume, fast-paced criminal defense practice, where a client thinks he has hired a seasoned lawyer but ends up in court with some younger, less experienced, less able and less feared “newbie”.Van Wagner, having devoted himself once again to the in-depth and professional practice of law one client at a time (rather than just the “business” of law or the money to be made), now makes it a point to spend time getting to know each client and each case. When you meet with him – which does not cost extra, unlike at some firms – you won’t be greeted by some junior partner, some wet-behind-the-ears lawyer. There are none here. Chris is your lawyer. Chris will handle your case. Chris listens.

Not only does he earn respect from prosecutors across the state, but Mr. Van Wagner also holds an “AV” rating with Martindale Hubbell, the highest peer rating available. This honor comes from lawyers across the state and across the spectrum of practice areas. He is known as a “lawyer’s lawyer.” He has also been recognized numerous times as a Super Lawyer, an honor given only to the top 5% of attorneys in Wisconsin. Additionally, Mr. Van Wagner has appeared as legal analyst and expert commentator on national shows such as Court TV, the Dan Abrams Report on MSNBC, the Today show, Good Morning America, ABC News as well as local shows such as ABC Madison Channel 27 and Madison Channel 3000 (C3K). He currently serves as the president of the Dane County Criminal Defense Lawyers Association, where he puts his experience and knowledge to use daily as he mentors the next generation of trial lawyers.

Chris loves his work, as you will see in his passion for your case and his love for the law. Chris does not golf or play cards; the law is truly his hobby. And he is thrilled to be your lawyer.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Sara has long been a strong advocate for children. Before attending law school, she was a social worker for the Bureau of Milwaukee Child Welfare. Now as an experienced attorney, recognized by Super Lawyers as a Rising Star in 2017 and 2019, Sara helps families involved in divorce and paternity proceedings, grandparent and foster parent rights cases, and in complicated CHIPS and termination of parental rights matters. She also serves as a mediator, as well as a guardian ad litem, representing the best interest of children. In all cases, Sara seeks creative solutions that work for families and protect children’s rights.

EDUCATION

Sara graduated with distinction from the University of Wisconsin-Madison with a B.S. in Human Development and Family Studies & Psychology. She earned her law degree from the University of Wisconsin Law School in 2008.

While in law school, Sara was a leader in the Children’s Justice Project. She was also active in the Wisconsin Journal of Law, Gender & Society, and Law Students for Reproductive Justice. She interned for the Honorable David Flanagan, Dane County Circuit Court, and was a student attorney with both the Rock County Public Defender’s Office and the Family Law & Restorative Justice Project of the Frank J. Remington Center.

COMMUNITY AND PROFESSIONAL ACTIVITIES

Sara serves as a member of the Board of the Divorce Cooperation Institute. She was formerly the President of the Board. She is also a member of the Collaborative Family Law Council of Wisconsin, the Dane County Bar Association, and the Legal Association for Women. Sara has served on the Board of the Children and the Law Section of the State Bar since 2017, an elected position.

Sara volunteers with the Dane County Family Law Assistance Center and the Dane County Case Mediation Program. She has been a coach for Dane County Girls on the Run, and while she has traded in her running shoes for a yoga mat, Sara is proud to have completed numerous charity runs, including a Madison Marathon and several half marathons across the country.

PERSONAL

Sara and her husband are the proud parents of their two young children, and they have two socially awkward cats, Monkey and George. Sara is an avid fan of the Badgers, Packers, and Brewers. She and her family love to travel, especially to tropical destinations, and they also regularly enjoy local trips to the zoo, parks, and the Farmer’s Market.

attorneys.name: Abigail M. Volberding
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Abby was born and raised in Wisconsin and has deep ties to Milwaukee and the surrounding communities. Abby practices almost exclusively family law since graduating from Vermont Law school and passing the Wisconsin Bar Examination in 2011. She has extensive experience in the traditional and collaborative divorce processes. Abby attended extensive training to act as a collaborative attorney and to act as a family mediator. Abby joined Burbach & Stansbury in December of 2021 after practicing in Milwaukee, Racine, and Kenosha for several years. Abby has litigation experience throughout South-Eastern Wisconsin including Racine, Kenosha, Milwaukee, Waukesha, Washington, and Ozaukee Counties. Abby also has experience acting as a Guardian ad Litem in Racine County.

Abby prides herself on her availability, quick responses, and open communication with her clients. Abby is always eager to assist individuals and families with paternity, child support, divorce, legal separation, and guardianship matters. Abby is very passionate about keeping children's best interests at the forefront of all negotiation and litigation. Abby has unique insight into children's best interests as acting as a Guardian ad Litem provided her the opportunity to speak with children of various ages and backgrounds about how their parent's litigation affected them.

Abby currently lives in Milwaukee with her husband, young daughter, and crazy Black Lab Gus. Abby seeks to be very engaged with the health of Wisconsin families and participated on the Lead Safe Advisory Committee and participates on the Board of Partners with Paws Service Dogs. Abby loves the outdoors and spends every moment she can outside with her family hiking and exploring Wisconsin. Abby and her husband are avid mushroom hunters, but she will not tell you where they find them.

Abby received the Wisconsin Law Journal's prestigious 2020 Leaders in the Law Award. An article written subsequently about Abby's practice of family law can be found here: https://wislawjournal.com/2020/09/16/volberdings-career-mushrooms-into-excellence/.

Abby's feelings on practicing family law:

"There are a number of reasons I choose to practice family law. At the top of the list is the opportunity it gives me to make a meaningful difference in the lives of others. Family law is unique in that it allows attorneys to work very closely with clients during a time in their life where they feel very little control over matters that are very near and dear to their heart. I enjoy practicing in an area of law that allows me to guide and assist clients through such a trying time in a way that makes them feel empowered again. I have a real passion for helping clients achieve their goals because it effects the most important aspects of their lives. I also care deeply about kids and sincerely want to make sure children's best interests are at the forefront of cases involving children."

attorneys.name: Jeffrey S. Ward
attorneys.practice_type: Chemical & Life Sciences Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
As a counselor and litigator, Jeff helps his clients navigate the complex patent and regulatory issues related to bringing generic drugs to market. He enjoys developing creative strategies for his clients and then executing those strategies in litigation.

Jeff is a partner in the Madison office. He has concentrated his practice on the representation of generic pharmaceutical companies, including Hatch-Waxman litigation, for more than two decades. His practice focuses primarily in the area of patent litigation, opinion work, and client counseling. Jeff has represented many generic pharmaceutical companies and API manufacturers regarding Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA) and 505(b)(2) submissions on a wide variety of products. He has acted as lead counsel and tried numerous Hatch-Waxman litigation matters to verdict.

Jeff has also litigated patent disputes relating to the pharmaceutical, chemical, and mechanical arts in federal courts throughout the United States and in the United States International Trade Commission. Jeff additionally has participated in many patent appeals, including arguing to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit.

Attorney Robert T. Ward grew up in Milwaukee and has lived in Wisconsin his entire life. He received his undergraduate degree from Marquette University. He is a member of the Wisconsin Academy of Trial Lawyers' Workers' Compensation Committee.

He was listed in The Best Lawyers in America. He was selected for inclusion in Wisconsin Super Lawyers, each year from 2005 through 2024.

In 2019, Domer Law and Ward Law Firm – two of Wisconsin’s premier workers’ compensation law firms – combined forces to provide enhanced services to injured workers in Wisconsin. Attorney Robert Ward, in 2020, transitioned to “of counsel” at Domer Law. This enhanced team of attorneys boasts over 100 years of combined workers’ compensation practice. Expanded offices and personnel in both Milwaukee and Waukesha now allow greater opportunities and resources for helping Wisconsin’s injured workers anywhere in the state.

The attorneys and team at Domer Law serve clients at both the Milwaukee and Waukesha locations.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Attorney Robert T. Ward grew up in Milwaukee and has lived in Wisconsin his entire life. He received his undergraduate degree from Marquette University. He graduated from the University of Wisconsin Law School in 1982. He has practiced workers' compensation law for nearly 30 years, helping injured workers across Wisconsin. Robert T. Ward has successfully pursued workers' compensation claims through all levels of appeal, including the Wisconsin Supreme Court. He is a member of the Wisconsin Academy of Trial Lawyers' Workers' Compensation Committee.

He was listed in The Best Lawyers in America. He was selected for inclusion in Wisconsin Super Lawyers, each year from 2005 through 2024.

In 2019, Domer Law and Ward Law Firm – two of Wisconsin’s premier workers’ compensation law firms – combined forces to provide enhanced services to injured workers in Wisconsin. Attorney Robert Ward, in 2020, transitioned to “of counsel” at Domer Law. This enhanced team of attorneys boasts over 100 years of combined workers’ compensation practice. Expanded offices and personnel in both Milwaukee and Waukesha now allow greater opportunities and resources for helping Wisconsin’s injured workers anywhere in the state.

The attorneys and team at Domer Law serve clients at both the Milwaukee and Waukesha locations.

attorneys.name: Wendy M. Ward
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
As a former Senior Director of Intellectual Property at a Minneapolis-based generic pharmaceutical company, Wendy knows what it's like to answer to a CEO who demands results within the constraints of a budget. Wendy's responsibilities included establishment of global processes related to all aspects of litigation, pre-initiation evaluation of potential products, and development and implementation of Paragraph IV challenge strategies in concert with senior management, regulatory, and scientific staff. Wendy also managed all Hatch-Waxman litigation for the company and was an active member of the trial team in several cases. Her experience has enhanced her ability to anticipate her clients' needs.

Wendy is a partner in the Madison office of Merchant & Gould, concentrating her practice on patent litigation. A significant portion of Wendy's practice includes counseling generic pharmaceutical companies with respect to ANDA filings, including preparing non-infringement, invalidity and freedom-to-operate opinions, and managing Hatch-Waxman litigation.

She also has extensive experience representing clients in connection with a variety of intellectual property evaluation issues, including due diligence investigations and patent validity, infringement, and freedom-to-operate analyses.

Wendy's technical background includes research in molecular virology, both during her undergraduate program in medical microbiology and immunology and as a research specialist in the Department of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences at the University of Wisconsin Medical School. Wendy's research included in vitro testing of putative antiviral compounds and development of a viral vector to deliver therapeutic genes to retinoblastoma tumors in animal models.

Wendy's pro bono service includes representation of Wisconsin prisoners alleging civil rights violations by prison officials.

In her spare time, Wendy enjoys spending time with her husband and daughter. Her favorite activities include cooking and baking, balanced by running and biking.

attorneys.name: David L. Weir
attorneys.practice_type: Wisconsin Worker's Compensation - Employee Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
David L. Weir was born and raised in Illinois, first venturing to Wisconsin to attend Beloit College. After graduating from Beloit College with a B.A. in Economics and Management (cum laude) in 1980, he went on to receive his law degree from Marquette University (cum laude) in 1983. He immediately began his law practice in Milwaukee, representing injured workers in claims for Worker's Compensation and Social Security Disability benefits, with the firm of Zubrensky and Weir. After nearly 25 years of practice in Milwaukee, he joined Stafford & Neal S.C. in 2007. Over the years, David has lectured extensively on the topic of Wisconsin Worker's Compensation benefits to a variety of audiences at union seminars, continuing legal education seminars, and the Wisconsin School for Workers. He has also been quite active in representing the interests of workers as a legal advisor to the Labor members of the Wisconsin Worker's Compensation Advisory Council, the body responsible for recommending changes to the Worker's Compensation Act to the state legislature.

David is married with two children. In his spare time, his hobby/passion is racing radio controlled cars, and enjoys competing at both local and national events with his teenage son.

attorneys.name: Nicole Wells
attorneys.practice_type: Car Accident Lawyers in River Falls, WI
attorneys.bio:
Nicole Wells is a compassionate and dedicated personal injury attorney with a strong commitment to achieving the best outcome for her clients. She understands that each case is unique and takes the time to educate her clients on the legal process and set expectations from the beginning. Nicole's area of focus is plaintiff's personal injury, and she is known for her ability to listen and relate to her clients.

Nicole was attracted to the practice of law because she wanted to make a positive impact on people's lives. She chose personal injury law after working at an insurance defense firm and realizing that helping injured people was her true calling. She balances empathy and compassion with a strong commitment to fair and diligent representation of her clients. Nicole's legal skills include thorough legal research and advocacy on behalf of her clients.

Outside of her legal practice, Nicole is actively involved in the community. She serves on the Board of Directors for the Kiwanis Club of New Richmond, where she volunteers her time for various youth-focused events. Nicole is also a member of several legal associations, including the State Bar of Wisconsin and the Minnesota State Bar Association. She is a fan of the Wisconsin Badgers basketball and volleyball teams and enjoys boating and traveling with her family. Nicole also enjoys baking and cooking with her children.

Clients of Nicole Wells can expect compassionate, diligent, and thorough representation throughout their case. She understands the importance of listening and relating to her clients to achieve the best outcome possible, and she is committed to fighting for their rights with compassion and tenacity.

attorneys.name: Diane M. Welsh
attorneys.practice_type: Appellate Litigation Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Diane Welsh is a Partner in the firm, and a member of the Litigation Practice Group and the Transactional Practice Group.

Diane has more than twenty-five years of experience in government, administrative, and health law. Her substantial experience advising top-level state officials allows her to evaluate regulatory and legal problems and recommend and implement strategic, pragmatic solutions for her clients, which includes health care providers, organizations, and individuals.

Diane is an experienced litigator, having handled matters ranging from administrative hearings to judicial appeals. She has litigated hundreds of cases before the Wisconsin Court of Appeals and the Wisconsin Supreme Court. Diane served as a United States Supreme Court Fellow with the National Association of Attorneys General. She has practiced in the United States Supreme Court, the Seventh Circuit Court of Appeals, federal district courts, state courts, and the Division of Hearings and Appeals.

Prior to joining Pines Bach LLP, Diane served as Chief Legal Counsel for the Wisconsin Department of Health Services and as assistant attorney general at the Wisconsin Department of Justice.

Diane is an active member of the community. She has served on the Board of Directors for the Wisconsin Democracy Campaign, Domestic Abuse Intervention Services, and Wisconsin Women in Government. She is currently a member of the Dean’s Advisory Board for the University of Wisconsin-Whitewater College of Letters and Sciences.

attorneys.bio:
Attorney Harvey Wendel has over 50 years of experience representing clients in real estate development and financing, including sales and acquisitions. He was ranked as a "Top Lawyer" in Alternative Dispute Resolution in Dane County as published by Madison Magazine in 2003.

Harvey has been and continues to be an active member of the State Bar of Wisconsin and Dane County Bar Association. He currently serves on the Board of the Dane County Bar Senior Lawyers Section and was past chairman, as well as past president of the Wisconsin State Bar Senior Lawyers Division. Harvey has been elected to serve on the Wisconsin Supreme Court Office of Lawyer Regulation (OLR) District 9 Committee as a member for a three-year term (January 2018 through December 2020). He is a Director of the Dane County Bar Association, and serves as a member of the Courthouse Committee. Harvey has also served as an arbitrator as a member of the Panel of Neutrals of the American Arbitration Association Board of Arbitrators. From 2005 to 2013, Harvey was a member of the Wisconsin Supreme Court Board of Administrative Oversight, which monitors the State of Wisconsin Attorney Regulation System.

In addition, Harvey has served on the boards of Madison-area banks and as a member and past president of the board of Friends of Madison School & Community Recreation (MSCR), where he also volunteers his time as a pontoon boat driver.

attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Elkhorn, WI
attorneys.bio:
Jacob R. Wendt is an associate attorney with Godfrey, Leibsle, Blackbourn & Howarth, S.C. Jacob earned his law degree in 2025 from Marquette University Law School where he served on the Marquette Sports Law Review.

During law school, Jacob earned a Certificate in Sports Law from the National Sports Law Institute at Marquette and gained business transactional experience through an internship with a Hackney Publication Top 100 Law Firm with Sports Practices.

Since joining Godfrey, Leibsle, Blackbourn & Howarth, S.C., Jacob has quickly demonstrated his ability to handle complex matters with skill and efficiency. Most recently, he guided a real estate development client through the complex regulatory maze of municipal regulations – conducting a detailed analysis of zoning requirements and developing a strategic plan for future planning commission proceedings to ensure the client could move forward with the development on schedule.

Jacob has also recently assisted in the acquisition of a privately held company, where he was involved in drafting and negotiating transaction documents, coordinating due diligence, and facilitating crucial third-party interactions. Throughout the process, he maintained focus on aligning legal details with the client’s broader business objectives to ensure the transaction progressed smoothly amid multiple legal complexities.

Jacob’s law practice focuses on business and real estate transactions. He is a member of the State Bar of Wisconsin.

attorneys.name: David Werley
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Green Bay, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney David Werley ("David") received his bachelor degree from the University of Wisconsin-Oshkosh, his master's degree in Public Policy and Leadership from the University of St. Thomas in St. Paul, Minnesota, and his law degree from Mitchell Hamline School of Law in St. Paul Minnesota. David graduated from Mitchell Hamline School of Law magna cum laude and was the student commencement speaker at graduation. His speech reminded students to always practice law with compassion, understanding while attorneys are trained to be fact-finders, these facts often have complex emotions behind them. While attorneys are advocates, we are also seen as friends, family, and trusted confidants for many clients.

David decided to become an attorney while working in the health insurance industry, where he worked for nine years. It was during his legal education where he discovered his passion for understanding how the law impacts everyday people going through the most difficult moments of their lives.

Blue collar in his communication and approach, David prides himself on explaining complex laws in ways that non-lawyers can understand. David's inherent personality of helping others, combined with his intense advocacy for the same, made his landing spot in family law and personal injury a perfect match.

David's experience as guardian ad litem, representing the children's interests in family law cases, allow him to inform his clients on likely outcomes in their cases. David encourages his clients to take reasonable positions in family law matters, but also reminds his clients no matter how reasonable his position is, he has little power over how reasonable the other side decides to be. It is when the opposing party becomes unreasonably that he wears the hat of fierce litigator, vigorously advocating for his client's position.

Outside of work, David enjoys his free time by coaching kids' soccer teams, camping with his family, slaying grilled foods, and like everyone else in this neck of the woods, cheering on the Packers. David is always open for recommendations on nachos as well, as he is well-known for being a nacho connoisseur.

David's experience as guardian ad litem, representing the children's interests in family law cases, allow him to inform his clients on likely outcomes in their cases. David encourages his clients to take reasonable positions in family law matters, but also reminds his clients no matter how reasonable his position is, he has little power over how reasonable the other side decides to be. It is when the opposing party becomes unreasonably that he wears the hat of fierce litigator, vigorously advocating for his client's position.

Outside of work, David enjoys his free time by coaching kids' soccer teams, camping with his family, slaying grilled foods, and like everyone else in this neck of the woods, cheering on the Packers. David is always open for recommendations on nachos as well, as he is well-known for being a nacho connoisseur.

attorneys.name: Christa O. Westerberg
attorneys.practice_type: Environmental and Energy Law Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Christa Westerberg is a Partner with the firm's Litigation Practice Group.

While experienced in a variety of civil litigation, Christa concentrates her practice in environmental and land use law, as well as open government law. She has represented individuals, non-profit groups, businesses, municipalities, and others in their efforts to protect environmental resources. Christa has obtained judgments and settlements for her clients in venues ranging from administrative agencies to federal court, and she has handled numerous appellate cases on a range of issues.

Christa also uses her expertise in regulatory and zoning matters to help non-profits, homeowners, and renewable energy developers navigate rules for solar and wind projects, and to obtain permits and approvals where needed.

Christa's work on open government issues on behalf of media, individuals, and others has resulted in published court decisions protecting the public's right to know. Wis. State Journal v. Blazel, 21AP1196; Lueders v. Krug, 2019 WI App 36; Juneau County Star-Times v. Juneau County, 2013 WI 4; State ex rel. Citizens for Open Government v. City of Milton, 2007 WI App 114. Christa has also represented clients experiencing violations of their civil rights in public accommodation and free speech contexts.

Christa frequently presents on environmental and open government issues. She is Vice President of the Wisconsin Freedom of Information Council, and is the former Chair of the State Bar of Wisconsin's Administrative and Local Government Section.

While in law school, Christa interned at the Center on Race, Poverty & the Environment in Delano, California.

attorneys.name: William Wetzel
attorneys.practice_type: Sex Discrimination Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Wetzel is a litigation associate in the Milwaukee Office of Cross Law Firm, S.C. Attorney Wetzel's practice is laser-focused on helping individual employees whose rights have been violated. He represents clients from all walks of life through litigation, mediations, hearings, negotiations, trials and all legal matters in between. He is committed to providing compassionate, high-quality, and down-to-earth legal advice in service of his clients' goals.

His areas of expertise include:

•Sex discrimination

•Race Discrimination

•Sexual harassment

•Retaliation

•Disability discrimination

•FMLA interference and retaliation

•Wage theft

•Unemployment

Attorney Wetzel knows that litigation, while sometimes necessary, is a last resort and he regularly represents clients in matters where litigation is a possible outcome, but not necessarily the best one. To this point, he regularly counsels clients through pre-litigation disputes including severance negotiations, contractual negotiations, and mediations. Attorney Wetzel is committed to providing high-quality, cost-effective legal guidance to his clients; no matter their financial situation or background. He strongly believes that every employee deserves a zealous advocate.

Attorney Wetzel joined Cross Law Firm, S.C. in 2016 after graduating from Wisconsin Law School. Attorney Wetzel is a proud "Double Badger", having also attended the University of Wisconsin where he received a Bachelor's Degree in Economics with an emphasis in Mathematics.

Prior to attending law school, Attorney Wetzel worked a variety of jobs ranging from barista, to working at a pizza joint, to painting houses. His work experience gives him extra insight into the issues faced by low-wage workers. During law school he gained experience interning for Outagamie County Circuit Court Judges, as well as working for the State of Wisconsin Department of Revenue in the Office of General Counsel. These experiences sharpened his legal skills and broadened his understanding of how the law in Wisconsin actually functions. To this day, he draws on these experiences when serving clients.

Attorney Wetzel is a member of the Wisconsin Employment Lawyers Association, the Milwaukee Bar Association, and the Milwaukee Young Lawyers Association.

In his free time, Attorney Wetzel enjoys cooking, spending time outside, trying new restaurants, and playing tennis.

attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Kenosha, WI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Lindsey M. White is an Associate Attorney with Probst Law Offices, S.C. Lindsey is known for her dedication to her clients, her compassion, and her professionalism both in and out of the courtroom. Lindsey understands that her clients are encountering some of life's greatest challenges as they face family law issues. She is a firm believer that no individual should ever have to confront a legal crisis on their own, especially one that impacts their family.

Lindsey develops a trusting relationship with her clients and goes the extra mile in making sure her client not only feels comfortable in speaking with her, but also ensuring that each client is treated as a top priority. Lindsey appreciates that family law matters are very sensitive in nature and her goal is to not only achieve the best result possible, but to also relieve some of the stress her clients may be experiencing. Lindsey takes pride in evaluating each situation on a case by case basis and understands that each family is different. Whether her clients wish to pursue litigation or go the collaborative route, they are always assured the highest level of personal attention and responsiveness.

attorneys.name: Geoffrey Wilber
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Born and raised in South Dakota, Geoff earned a Bachelor of Science Degree from South Dakota State University before moving to Milwaukee to obtain his Juris Doctorate Degree from Marquette University Law School.

Since graduating from law school, Geoff has dedicated his entire legal career to helping clients who were wrongfully injured as a result of someone else’s negligence. In advocating for his clients, Geoff draws from the work ethic instilled upon him while growing up in rural South Dakota, his competitiveness and doggedness from his time as a college linebacker, and his legal acumen and skills developed from over two decades as an accomplished trial lawyer.

As an experienced trial lawyer, Geoff has successfully tried dozens of cases to verdict in courthouses throughout the state of Wisconsin. In his career, Geoff has filed and resolved hundreds of lawsuits on behalf of his clients. In total, he has obtained tens of millions of dollars in settlement funds, including multiple million-dollar-plus settlements and jury verdicts, on behalf of over 4,500 clients throughout his career. Geoff is a member of the Wisconsin State Bar Association and is licensed to practice in all State and Federal Courts throughout Wisconsin.

Geoff, and his wife Macee, are proud to call Wisconsin home and have been extremely lucky to have raised their three daughters as proud Wisconsinites. In addition to his legal practice, Geoff has spent many years being an active member of his community which includes coaching multiple youth sports teams and volunteering at local charities. He spends his free time enjoying music with his girls, watching sports, cooking and enjoying meals with family and friends, and spending the weekends doing projects around his house with his dog, Tac, by his side.

attorneys.name: Denise R. Wilson
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Denise R. Wilson is an experienced family law attorney specializing in divorces, custody issues, post-judgment matters, and paternity cases. She is also taking on some elder law cases depending on the issue. She brings a wealth of expertise and a unique perspective to her practice, rooted in her diverse background as an educator, instructional designer, and project manager.

Originally from Maryland, Denise has lived and worked across the country, including Washington, D.C., Albuquerque, N.M., and Chicago, IL, finally putting down roots in Wisconsin since 2015. This broad range of experiences informs her compassionate and results-driven approach to family law.

After earning a Bachelor’s Degree in Secondary Education and Master’s Degree in Instructional Design and Technology, dedicating years to teaching and instructional design, Denise’s growing interest in how government policy and the legal system affect individuals led her to pursue a career in law. attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Andrea Winder is an Associate Attorney at Nicholson Goetz & Otis, S.C., where she practices both criminal defense and family law.

Prior to passing the Wisconsin Bar Exam, Attorney Winder attended law school at Stetson College of Law in Florida, where she took advantage of its #1 nationally ranked trial advocacy program by competing in and coaching mock trial and other advocacy competitions. Upon returning to Wisconsin, Attorney Winder interned for two circuit court judges, assisting them in drafting decisions and researching legal issues, as well as completing an internship for the Green County District Attorney’s Office where she was able to appear in court and handle hearings and trials under the supervision of prosecutors.

Attorney Winder began her career by founding her own law firm and primarily representing indigent defendants in criminal cases who faced charges ranging from low level misdemeanors to high level felonies. Attorney Winder has experience in numerous surrounding counties and is relied on by many judges to serve as court appointed counsel to protect and advocate for the constitutional rights of criminal defendants.

Attorney Winder is dedicated to her clients’ best interests and passionately advocates on their behalf while demonstrating the poise, preparedness, and proficiency required to effectively navigate all stages of a case up to and beyond trial. Attorney Winder believes that maintaining regular communication with her clients is paramount, and she strives to ensure that their concerns and questions are promptly addressed.

attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning and Probate Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Nancy brings an accounting background to the practice of law, allowing her to counsel her clients regarding their legal needs with an eye toward tax planning.

Nancy takes great pride in building and maintaining strong client relationships, based on service and trust. Together, Nancy and her father, Jay W. Winter, served the legal needs of Oregon and Madison-area families from one generation to the next. In 2013, Winter Law Office merged with The Law Center for Children & Families, forming The Law Center, S.C. As a result of the merger, the firm is able to serve more of its clients’ diverse legal needs, while continuing a tradition of long-term, personal client relationships.

PRACTICE AREAS

Business Law

Life and Estate Planning

Probate

Property and Real Estate

Tax Planning and Preparation

Marital Property and Cohabitation Agreements

LGBTQ Family Formation and Protection (contracts and estate planning)

EDUCATION

Nancy graduated with distinction from the University of Wisconsin-Madison School of Business with a B.B.A. (Bachelor of Business Administration) in Accounting. She earned her law degree from the University of Wisconsin in 1990.

COMMUNITY AND PROFESSIONAL ACTIVITIES

Nancy is a member of the Board of Directors of Canopy Center, a children’s rights non-profit, and she is particularly involved with Dane County CASA. “CASA” (Court Appointed Special Advocates) enlists volunteers to advocate for the needs of abused and neglected children who are unsafe at home and end up in the child welfare system. Nancy has coached track for the Oregon Area Chapter of Wisconsin Special Olympics for over a decade. She delivers “Meals on Wheels” through her Rotary Club. Nancy received recognition as a Paul Harris Fellow for her contributions to the Rotary Foundation, an establishment that takes pride in their humanitarian efforts and educational objectives.

attorneys.name: Gregory R. Wright
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Litigation Lawyers in Oshkosh, WI
attorneys.bio:
Greg is a busy civil trial attorney, whose practice has taken him into many of the courtrooms throughout Wisconsin. He devotes 100% of his practice to plaintiffs' personal injury work, representing Wisconsin citizens from all walks of life, who have been seriously injured, or have a loved one killed as the result of the negligence of another individual or corporation. Greg obtained his Board Certification as a Civil Trial Specialist from the National Board of Trial Advocacy in 1996 and has held that certification since. He has also been recently Board Certified as a Civil Pre-Trial Specialist by the same National Board of Trial Advocacy. He now handles all serious and complex injury and death cases, including defective products, trucking accidents, farming accidents, industrial injuries, and motor vehicle crashes.

Greg is known as a straight shooter. He is cunning, diligent, professional, efficient, and dedicated to his clients. Greg works closely with each client to provide individualized and personalized service to each case. Greg sees each case as unique and special thus taking an individualized approach to each client’s needs to successfully achieve the appropriate outcome. Greg works closely with his clients to ensure such specialized service. Clients see Greg not only as their lawyer but their friend, someone they can trust. These skills have been recognized by various professional organizations who have nominated Greg as a Wisconsin Super Lawyer in 2008 and 2009; and a named Top 100 Civil Trial Attorneys in Wisconsin in 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, and 2017.

Over his many years of experience, Greg has served as Court Commissioner in Marquette County and has served as a Guardian Ad Litem on multiple occasions for minors to adequately protect their interests in the legal system. Attorneys from Wisconsin and other states such as Illinois and Minnesota have requested Greg’s services as co-counsel on complex personal injury cases. Greg’s exceptional attitude, knowledge, and skill have led to a successful practice since 1978 and only continues to advance.

attorneys.name: Erica N. Young
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Milwaukee, WI
attorneys.bio:
Criminal Defense & Family Law Attorney

Attorney Erica Young brings a distinguished blend of legal insight, investigative experience, and public service to her practice. Before earning her law degree from the University of Wisconsin Law School in Madison, she spent over a decade in public service roles with the Wisconsin Department of Justice and the City of Milwaukee. Her tenure in the Attorney General’s Office and the Division of Criminal Investigation offered her a front-row seat to how criminal investigations unfold—knowledge that now informs her strategic and deeply informed criminal defense work.

While serving as a legislative aide for a Milwaukee alderperson, Attorney Young also gained first-hand experience with municipal governance and the legislative process—adding yet another dimension to her legal perspective.

During law school, she sharpened her litigation skills through her work with the Economic Justice Institute. There, she filed her first lawsuit, successfully negotiated landlord-tenant disputes, and worked to improve rent abatement policies for low-income residents in Dane County.

Today, Attorney Young is known for her passionate and compassionate defense of clients facing criminal charges across Wisconsin. She is skilled in all phases of criminal litigation—from arrest and charging decisions to plea negotiations and trial. Her client-centered approach emphasizes open communication, thorough investigation, and persuasive courtroom advocacy. Judges and juries alike respect her ability to present humanizing narratives that highlight the dignity and complexity of her clients.

In addition to her criminal defense work, Attorney Young is a tenacious advocate in family law matters, handling divorce, custody, placement, and child support disputes with empathy and resolve. Whether guiding a parent through a difficult separation or defending the rights of the accused, Attorney Young is driven by a steadfast belief in fairness, due process, and the transformative power of second chances.

content: Richard Carr v. City of Pewaukee, Waukesha County Case No. 21-CV-1180 (summary judgment for taxpayer on property tax objection claim, plus recovery of majority of client’s attorneys’ fees on sanctions award obtained against the municipality’s legal counsel).

US Bank Trust National Association v. Ambiguous Asset Corporation, 23-AP-1671 (court of appeals reversal of circuit court order denying motion to reopen order confirming foreclosure sale based on untimely filing of eligible third-party bidder affidavit).

Jennifer Buth v. Daniel and Jodi Pyawasay, et al., Milwaukee County Case No. 20-CV-5561 (summary judgment for clients defeating home buyer’s claims alleging fraud based on alleged non-disclosure of alleged house defects).

Christopher Hookstead v. Gary Beal, et al., No. 20-AP-895 (Wis. Ct. App. Aug. 5, 2021) (affirming jury verdict in client’s favor defeating plaintiff’s adverse possession claim and obtaining judgment on counterclaim for nearly $400,000 in damages, punitive damages, and attorneys’ fees, plus recovery of attorneys’ fees for defending verdict on appeal).

Mid America Steel Drum Properties, LLC, et al. v. Container Life Cycle Management LLC, Milwaukee County Case No. 19-CV-644 (jury verdict in client’s favor for over $450,000 in damages for unjust enrichment for the use of client’s industrial properties and judgment dismissing defendant’s claim for reformation of lease).

Great Lakes Excavating, Inc. v. Dollar Tree Stores, Inc., 2021 WI App 23, 397 Wis. 2d 210, 959 N.W.2d 351 (published decision of court of appeals affirming summary judgment for client and holding contractor waived its construction lien rights in disputed lien waiver document).

Wind Point Restoration, Inc. v. Anne Weikel, No. 18-AP-2258, 2020 WL 6051095 (Wis. Ct. App. Oct. 14, 2020) (affirming trial verdict in client’s favor recovering damages for breach of contract in home restoration project, dismissing homeowner’s counterclaims alleging violations of home improvement practices law, and awarding attorneys’ fees against homeowner).

Central United Methodist Church v. City of Milwaukee, Case No. 19-AP-778, 2020 WL 1264074 (Wis. Ct. App. Mar. 17, 2020) (reversing adverse ruling of circuit court and holding client’s church parking lot is tax exempt despite the church’s use of the lot to collect donations from people parking there for nearby concerts).

Parrish v. Weaver, Eastern District of Wisconsin Case No. 2:17-cv-01500 (summary judgment for client defeating home buyer’s claims alleging misrepresentation and failure to disclose alleged water entry into basement).

State ex rel. Peter Odgen Family Tr. of 2008 v. Bd. of Review, 2019 WI 23, 385 Wis. 2d 676, 923 N.W.2d 837 (unanimous decision of Wisconsin Supreme Court holding agricultural use of property does not require any business intent, saving client over $800,000 in assessed property tax value).

State ex rel. Peter Ogden Family Tr. of 2008 v. Bd. of Review for Town of Delafield, 2018 WI App 26, 381 Wis. 2d 161, 911 N.W.2d 653 (published decision of court of appeals reversing circuit court’s adverse ruling regarding classification of agricultural land for property tax purposes).

Talmer Bank & Tr. v. Jacobsen, 2018 WI App 15, 380 Wis. 2d 171, 908 N.W.2d 495 (published decision of court of appeals clarifying that the third-party exception to the American Rule applies in breach of contract actions and holding clients could recover their attorneys’ fees as damages for another party’s breach of contract).

attorneys.name: Jane F. Zimmerman
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
Ginger Zimmerman is a shareholder in Murphy Desmond S.C. having joined the firm in 1992. Her practice combines her experience in business, real estate, bankruptcy, secured transactions, agricultural and commercial transactions and litigation. She represents creditors, debtors, receivers and Trustees in bankruptcies, collections, reorganizations, liquidations and Wisconsin Chapter 128 proceedings.

Zimmerman also represents purchasers, sellers, landlords and tenants of commercial and agricultural real estate. Her practice includes consultation and representation related to the joint ownership of real estate. Her background in commercial and agricultural law is particularly helpful in structuring and negotiating financing for new businesses, refinancings, business purchases, expansions and reorganizations.

Zimmerman currently serves as chair of the firm's Creditors' Rights, Business Bankruptcy and Commercial Litigation Practice Group, and she serves on the firm's Board of Directors. She is included on lists for Best Lawyers in America and Wisconsin Super Lawyers and is rated AV (top) by Martindale-Hubbell. Zimmerman was honored by Wisconsin Law Journal as a recipient of the "Women in the Law"award for her work in the legal field and her support and encouragement of female attorneys in their careers.

Zimmerman, who works out of Murphy Desmond's Madison office, is available by appointment in the firm's Appleton and Janeville offices.

attorneys.name: David C. Zoeller
attorneys.practice_type: Wage and Hour Litigation Lawyers in Madison, WI
attorneys.bio:
David Zoeller is a Shareholder at Hawks Quindel, S.C. David represents individuals in wage and hour claims under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) and represents individuals in Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) appeals.

David joined Hawks Quindel’s Madison, Wisconsin office in 2009 after practicing as an employment and class action litigation attorney in Minneapolis, Minnesota. David has represented thousands of employees in multiple nationwide class and collective actions. David frequently represents individuals in social security disability appeals and is an effective and compassionate social security disability attorney familiar with the appeals process.

Mr. Zoeller graduated with honors from Colgate University in 2002 and from the University of Wisconsin Law School with honors in 2007. During law school, Mr. Zoeller was the recipient of the Wisconsin Association of Workers Compensation Attorneys' Scholarship, the Wisconsin Lawyers Mutual Scholarship, and was a member and competitor for the University of Wisconsin Moot Court Board.

Mr. Zoeller is dedicated to seeking fair treatment for workers through the enforcement of labor and employment laws and is a zealous advocate for his clients. Mr. Zoeller is admitted to practice in Minnesota and Wisconsin. Mr. Zoeller has spoken on wage and hour issues at the University of Wisconsin Law School, Marquette University Law School, and on behalf of the Wisconsin State Bar. Mr. Zoeller has been recognized by the Wisconsin Law Journal as one of Wisconsin’s Up and Coming Lawyers, and as a Rising Star by Super Lawyers. Mr. Zoeller also sits on the board of the University of Wisconsin Law School's Economic Justice Institute.
